definition_zh: 稀释；冲淡；削弱（效果、权力）；稀释过的
definition_en: to make a liquid weaker by adding water or another solvent, or to make something less forceful
core_image: 一小杯浓果汁倒进一大壶凉水，颜色从深褐立刻变浅
scene: 厨房里，服务员把一小杯浓缩果汁倒进一大壶凉水，颜色立刻从深褐变浅。 The waiter diluted the strong juice with cold water before serving it.
sceneCN: 这里 dilute 指加水使浓度降低（第 1 个义项：稀释）；句意为服务员上桌前用凉水把浓果汁稀释。图中可辨识物件：浓缩果汁、水壶、玻璃杯、搅拌勺。

senses.title: To add water and lower concentration
senses.definition: to add water or another solvent to a liquid so that the amount of active substance in each unit falls
senses.definitionCN: 向液体中加入水或其他溶剂，使每单位中有效物质的量下降
senses.example: Dilute the acid with three parts water.
senses.exampleCN: 用三份水把这种酸稀释。
senses.why: dilute comes from Latin diluere 'to wash away', so the core action is washing strength out into a larger volume.
senses.whyCN: dilute 出自拉丁 diluere「冲走」，核心动作就是把强度冲散到更大的体积里。

senses.title: To weaken a solution before testing
senses.definition: to reduce the strength of a sample so that it falls within the range an instrument or a procedure can handle
senses.definitionCN: 降低样品的强度，使仪器或操作能处理
senses.example: The technician diluted the sample before testing.
senses.exampleCN: 技术员在检测前把样品稀释了。
senses.why: a sample that is too strong must be reduced, so laboratory routine turns the first sense into a standard step.
senses.whyCN: 过浓的样品必须减弱，实验室流程就把第一义变成标准步骤。

senses.title: To weaken power or influence
senses.definition: to make authority, influence or an advantage less effective by spreading it among more parties
senses.definitionCN: 把权威、影响力或优势分散给更多方，使其效力下降
senses.example: Adding more members diluted the chairman's influence.
senses.exampleCN: 增加成员削弱了主席的影响力。
senses.why: influence behaves like a solute: the same amount spread through more volume acts more weakly at any one point.
senses.whyCN: 影响力像溶质：同样的量摊进更大体积，在任一点上的作用就更弱。

senses.title: To weaken taste, colour or feeling
senses.definition: to make a quality fainter by mixing it with something neutral
senses.definitionCN: 通过与中性之物混合使某种性质变淡
senses.example: Too much water diluted the taste of the tea.
senses.exampleCN: 水太多，把茶味冲淡了。
senses.why: taste and colour are intensities carried in a liquid, so adding liquid lowers them just as it lowers concentration.
senses.whyCN: 味道与颜色是液体承载的强度，加水会像降低浓度一样把它们压低。

senses.title: Weakened by water, as an adjective
senses.titleCN: 形容词：稀释过的、浓度低的
senses.definition: having had water added, so that the substance is present at low strength
senses.definitionCN: 已加水，使物质以低强度存在
senses.example: A dilute solution of bleach is safe on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 稀释的漂白液用在地面上是安全的。
senses.why: the adjective is the same form, describing the state that the verb has produced.
senses.whyCN: 形容词是同一形式，描述动词造成的那种状态。

senses.title: To make a promise less forceful
senses.titleCN: 使承诺或主张变得无力
senses.definition: to take the force out of a statement, promise or claim by adding qualifications or compromises
senses.definitionCN: 通过附加条件或折中，抽掉陈述、承诺或主张的力量
senses.example: The final clause diluted the promise of reform.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一条款把改革的承诺冲淡了。
senses.why: a claim is strong when nothing neutral is mixed in, so hedging works like adding water to a statement.
senses.whyCN: 主张在没有掺入中性成分时最强，因此含糊其辞就像给陈述加水。

senses.title: To reduce each shareholder's stake
senses.definition: to reduce the proportion of a company owned by existing shareholders by issuing more shares
senses.definitionCN: 通过发行更多股份，降低现有股东所占的公司比例
senses.example: Issuing new shares diluted existing holdings.
senses.exampleCN: 发行新股稀释了现有持股。
senses.why: ownership is a share of a fixed whole, so adding more shares spreads the same company over more claims.
senses.whyCN: 所有权是对一个固定整体的份额，增发股份就把同一家公司摊到更多索取权上。

senses.title: To spread intensity until it fades
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把强度摊到更大范围直至变淡
senses.definition: used figuratively of any intensity that loses force when spread over more time, space or recipients
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指任何强度因摊到更多时间、空间或对象而失去力量
senses.example: Praise repeated too often is diluted into noise.
senses.exampleCN: 赞美重复太多，就被冲淡成噪音。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the arithmetic of dilution: the same amount divided among more units counts for less in each.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了稀释的算术：同样的量分给更多单位，每一份就更少。

intro.en: Dilute comes from the Latin past participle dilutus, from diluere 'to wash away, dissolve, dilute', built on dis- 'apart' plus -luere, the combining form of lavere 'to wash'. It is recorded in English from the fifteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dilute 来自拉丁过去分词 dilutus，出自 diluere「冲走、溶解、稀释」，由 dis-「分开」加 -luere 构成，后者是 lavere「洗」的组合形式。英语自十五世纪有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lavere meant 'to wash'; its combining form -luere appears in diluere and in words about flooding, and its older root is reconstructed as a verb of washing.
items.cn: lavere 意为「洗」，其组合形式 -luere 出现在 diluere 以及表示洪水的词中，其更古老词根被重构为一个表示「洗」的动词。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' plus -luere gave diluere 'to wash away, to dissolve, to dilute', the image being strength carried off into a larger body of water.
items.cn: dis-「分开」加 -luere 构成 diluere「冲走、溶解、稀释」，画面是强度被带进更大一片水里。

items.en: The past participle dilutus 'washed away, diluted' is the direct source of the English adjective and of the verb built on it.
items.cn: 过去分词 dilutus「被冲走的、被稀释的」是英语形容词及由此构成的动词的直接来源。

items.en: From the fifteenth century English dilute meant to weaken a liquid by adding water, first in medicine and then in general use.
items.cn: 自十五世纪起，英语 dilute 指加水使液体变弱，先在医学中使用，后进入一般用法。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the verb described weakened power, claims and ownership, where the same arithmetic of spreading holds.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个动词已用于被削弱的权力、主张与所有权，因为「摊开」的算术是一样的。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin shape of the washing root is a reconstruction, and its exact first English citation is not recorded. Note that this root is not the luere 'to loosen' behind soluble.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：表示「洗」的词根在拉丁语之前的形式属于重构，英语最早书证没有确切记录。需注意这个词根并非 soluble 背后表示「松开」的 luere。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes whose roots are different despite similar spelling; group two holds verbs for making something weaker.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写相近而词根不同的形近词；第二组是表示使某物变弱的动词。

entries.definition: The act or result of diluting; it is the noun built on this verb, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 稀释的动作或结果；由这个动词构成的名词，并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: To break a solid apart into a liquid; dilute does not dissolve anything, it only lowers the strength of what is already dissolved.
entries.definitionCN: 把固体拆散进液体；dilute 不溶解任何东西，只降低已溶解物的强度。

entries.definition: From Latin latus 'wide': to widen or expand, as a pupil or an artery does; it has nothing to do with washing.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 latus「宽」：使变宽、扩张，如瞳孔或动脉；与「洗」无关。

entries.definition: From diluvium, a flood: water overwhelming everything, which is the violent version of the same washing image.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 diluvium「洪水」：水淹没一切，是同一「冲洗」意象的猛烈版本。

entries.definition: The broad verb for making anything less strong, with no image of water.
entries.definitionCN: 使任何事物变弱的通用动词，不含水的意象。

entries.definition: To make a liquid less thick, as paint with turpentine; it changes consistency rather than concentration.
entries.definitionCN: 使液体变稀薄，如用松节油调漆；改变的是稠度，而非浓度。

entries.definition: The plain phrase for adding water, and also for softening a statement; dilute is its formal counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 加水的日常说法，也指软化表述；dilute 是其正式对应词。

entries.definition: To reduce the strength of a signal, a virus or a force; common in physics and medicine rather than in cookery.
entries.definitionCN: 降低信号、病毒或力量的强度；多用于物理与医学，而非厨房。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Diluere 'to wash away': water carries the strength off into a larger volume.
normal.cn: diluere「冲走」：水把强度带进更大的体积。

normal.en: The family runs dilute, dilution, diluent, diluted, undiluted.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 dilute、dilution、diluent、diluted、undiluted。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the chemical sense: dilute acid, dilute a solution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出化学义：稀酸、稀释溶液。

normal.en: The figurative phrases mark the rest: dilute the effect, dilute ownership, dilute the message.
normal.cn: 比喻搭配标出其余义项：削弱效果、稀释所有权、冲淡信息。

normal.en: Remember the root is 'wash', not 'loosen': do not tie it to dissolve or soluble.
normal.cn: 记住词根是「洗」而不是「松开」：不要把它与 dissolve 或 soluble 系在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon of dark syrup turning a whole jug pale brown.
abstract.cn: 想象一勺深色糖浆把整壶水染成浅褐。

abstract.en: Picture applause spread thin over an hour until it sounds like background noise.
abstract.cn: 想象掌声摊薄在一小时里，最后听起来像背景噪音。

abstract.en: Picture one strong voice split among a hundred speakers.
abstract.cn: 想象一个洪亮的声音被分给一百个人。

examples.en: Always dilute the cleaning fluid before pouring it down the drain.
examples.cn: 把清洁液倒进排水口前一定要先稀释。

examples.en: The new partners diluted the founder's share to less than half.
examples.cn: 新合伙人把创始人的股份稀释到不足一半。

examples.en: Repeating the slogan at every stop diluted its effect.
examples.cn: 每到一站都重复这句口号，反而削弱了它的效果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「di（分开）+ lute（冲）」——把浓的冲散开：稀释、冲淡、削弱

root: 拉丁 diluere「冲走、稀释」的过去分词 dilutus = dis-（分开）+ -luere（洗，源自 lavere「洗」）；与 soluble 背后表示「松开」的 luere 并非同一词根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one washing away: water lowers a concentration, a sample is made testable, power is spread thin, taste and colour fade, the adjective names the weakened state, a promise loses force, shares are spread over more owners, and finally any intensity fades as it is divided.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次「冲走」：水降低浓度，样品被调到可测，权力被摊薄，味道与颜色变淡，形容词命名被削弱的状态，承诺失去力量，股份被摊到更多持有人，最后任何强度都因被分割而变淡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small cup of dark juice poured into a large jug of clear water until the colour turns pale.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小杯深色果汁倒进一大壶清水，颜色直到变浅。

branches.en: LOWERING STRENGTH: domestic dilution and laboratory dilution are one act at two scales.
branches.cn: 降低强度：日常稀释与实验室稀释，是同一动作的两个尺度。

branches.en: SPREAD AMONG MORE HOLDERS: influence and shares both lose force when divided among more parties.
branches.cn: 摊给更多持有者：影响力与股份一旦分给更多方，都会失去力量。

branches.en: FAINT QUALITIES: taste, colour and the force of a promise all fade when something neutral is mixed in.
branches.cn: 变淡的性质：味道、颜色与承诺的力量，都会因掺入中性之物而减退。

branches.en: THE WEAKENED STATE: the adjective simply names what the verb has already done.
branches.cn: 被削弱的状态：形容词只是命名动词已经做成的事。

branches.en: DIVIDED INTENSITY: any strength spread over more time or recipients counts for less at each point.
branches.cn: 被分割的强度：任何强度摊到更多时间或对象上，每一点的分量都更少。

intro.en: Dilute is a Latin verb made of a prefix and a root of washing, and the same pieces build the rest of its family.
intro.cn: dilute 是一个由前缀与「洗」词根构成的拉丁动词，同样的部分构成它其余的家族。

latinIntro.en: Dis- 'apart' plus -luere 'to wash' gives diluere and its participle dilutus; the same washing root appears in deluge and diluvial, not in dissolve.
latinIntro.cn: dis-「分开」加 -luere「洗」构成 diluere 及其分词 dilutus；同一「洗」词根出现在 deluge 与 diluvial 中，而不在 dissolve 中。

items.example: The prefix sends the strength away into the water.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把强度送进水里。

items.example: The root supplies the washing image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「洗」的意象。

items.example: Only the combining form appears inside diluere.
items.exampleCN: 在 diluere 内部只出现组合形式。

items.example: The Latin verb begins the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词开启词族。

items.example: Dilute the paint before the second coat.
items.exampleCN: 上第二遍前把漆稀释。

items.meaning: the act or result of diluting
items.example: Two dilutions brought the sample into range.
items.exampleCN: 两次稀释把样品调进了量程。

items.example: Water is the cheapest diluent here.
items.exampleCN: 水是这里最便宜的稀释剂。

items.example: The diluted bleach was safe to use.
items.exampleCN: 稀释过的漂白液可以安全使用。

items.example: He drank the juice undiluted.
items.exampleCN: 他没兑水就把果汁喝了。

items.example: The storm brought a deluge to the valley.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨给山谷带来一场洪水。

definition_zh: 水文学家；水文工作者；水文观测员；水资源顾问；工程水文专家；生态水文专家
definition_en: a person who studies or practises hydrology, especially the measurement and modelling of water
core_image: 一个人蹲在河岸，手里拿着水位计，身后的桌上摊着流域图
scene: 勘测队在干涸的河床上打井，年轻的技术员蹲下读取水位计的刻度。 A hydrologist traced the missing water to a fissure beneath the valley.
sceneCN: 这里指「从事水文学研究或实践的人」（第 1 个义项：受过水文训练、负责测量与解释水的分布和运动的专业人员）；句意为一位水文学家把消失的水追踪到谷底的一条裂隙。场景物件：水位计、河床、井架、流域图。

pos.zh: 水文学家；水文工作者（可数；复数 hydrologists）

forms.label: 相关形容词（美式）（水文的）

senses.title: A research hydrologist
senses.definition: a person who studies or practises hydrology, especially the measurement and modelling of water
senses.definitionCN: 从事水文学研究或实践、尤其负责水的测量与建模的人
senses.example: A hydrologist traced the missing water to a fissure beneath the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 一位水文学家把消失的水追踪到谷底的一条裂隙。
senses.why: Hydrology plus -ist marks the person who does the science, so the word names a practitioner rather than the field.
senses.whyCN: hydrology 加 -ist 标记做这门科学的人，因此这个词命名从业者，而非领域。

senses.title: A field practitioner
senses.definition: a worker who measures rainfall, river level and flow in the field
senses.definitionCN: 在野外测量降雨、河流水位与流量的工作者
senses.example: The hydrologist waded out to read the staff gauge.
senses.exampleCN: 水文学家涉水过去读取水尺。
senses.why: Most hydrological data are gathered outdoors, so the word often means the person at the gauge rather than the theorist.
senses.whyCN: 大部分水文数据在户外采集，因此这个词常指站在水尺旁的人，而不是理论家。

senses.title: A monitoring technician
senses.definition: a technician who maintains stations, sensors and records
senses.definitionCN: 维护水文站、传感器与记录的技术人员
senses.example: The hydrologist calibrated the pressure sensor before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 水文学家在风暴前校准了压力传感器。
senses.why: Instruments need care, so a distinct working role grew around the maintenance of observation networks.
senses.whyCN: 仪器需要照料，于是围绕观测网络的维护长出一个独立的工作角色。

senses.title: A water-resource consultant
senses.definition: a specialist who advises on supply, recharge and allocation
senses.definitionCN: 就供水、补给与分配提供建议的专家
senses.example: The hydrologist advised the city on its aquifer budget.
senses.exampleCN: 水文学家就城市含水层收支向市府提供建议。
senses.why: When the science is sold as a service, the practitioner becomes an adviser to clients and agencies.
senses.whyCN: 当这门科学作为服务出售，从业者就成了客户与机构的顾问。

senses.title: An engineering hydrologist
senses.definition: a specialist who supplies design floods and waterworks calculations
senses.definitionCN: 提供设计洪水与水利工程计算的专家
senses.example: The engineering hydrologist set the dam's design flood.
senses.exampleCN: 工程水文专家确定了大坝的设计洪水。
senses.why: Infrastructure needs a specialist who can turn records into design values, so a professional branch is named.
senses.whyCN: 基础设施需要能把记录变成设计值的专家，于是出现一个以专业命名的分支。

senses.title: An ecohydrologist
senses.definition: a specialist who studies water together with plants, animals and ecosystems
senses.definitionCN: 把水与植物、动物及生态系统一起研究的专家
senses.example: The ecohydrologist mapped where the wetland would dry first.
senses.exampleCN: 生态水文专家绘出了湿地最先干涸的位置。
senses.why: Where water science meets ecology, the practitioner takes a compound title that names both.
senses.whyCN: 当水科学与生态学相遇，从业者获得一个同时命名两者的复合头衔。

senses.title: A climate hydrologist
senses.definition: a specialist who studies how climate change alters water cycles
senses.definitionCN: 研究气候变化如何改变水文循环的专家
senses.example: The climate hydrologist projected a shorter snow season.
senses.exampleCN: 气候水文专家预测雪季会缩短。
senses.why: Global warming moved water questions into climate science, so a hybrid role emerged.
senses.whyCN: 全球变暖把水的问题推进气候科学，于是出现混合角色。

senses.title: A citizen hydrologist
senses.definition: a trained volunteer who records water data for a shared network
senses.definitionCN: 为共享网络记录水数据的受训志愿者
senses.example: A citizen hydrologist photographed the flood mark.
senses.exampleCN: 一位公民水文学家拍下了洪水痕迹。
senses.why: Observation networks need many hands, so the title widened to include trained volunteers.
senses.whyCN: 观测网络需要许多双手，因此这个头衔扩展到受训志愿者。

intro.en: Hydrologist is hydrology plus the person suffix -ist, which reaches Greek -istēs. The word is a nineteenth-century professional label. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hydrologist 是 hydrology 加人物后缀 -ist，后者上溯希腊 -istēs。这个词是十九世纪的职业标签。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hydōr 'water' is the root; its deeper origin is often linked to a reconstructed *wed- 'water', which remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: hydōr「水」是词根；其更深来源常被联系到重构的 *wed-「水」，那仍属重构。

items.en: Hydrology, the study of water, entered English in the eighteenth century from Greek hydro- plus -logia.
items.cn: hydrology 是对水的研究，十八世纪由希腊 hydro- 加 -logia 进入英语。

items.en: Greek -istēs marked a person who does or follows something; Latin -ista and French -iste carried it into English as -ist.
items.cn: 希腊 -istēs 标记从事或追随某事的人；拉丁 -ista 与法语 -iste 把它带入英语作 -ist。

items.en: Hydrologist appeared as water science became a paid profession in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 随着水科学在十九与二十世纪成为有薪职业，hydrologist 作为职业标签出现。

items.en: Later compound titles such as engineering hydrologist and ecohydrologist split the role by application.
items.cn: 后来工程水文专家、生态水文专家等复合头衔按应用把角色再细分。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Greek source of hydōr is uncertain, *wed- is a reconstruction, and the first use of hydrologist is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：hydōr 的前希腊语来源不确定，*wed- 属重构，hydrologist 最早的使用没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root person, field and adjective forms; group two holds neighbouring water professions that are not interchangeable.
note.cn: 第一组是同根的人物、领域与形容词形式；第二组是邻近但不可互换的水相关职业。

entries.definition: The science of water; hydrologist is the person who practises it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究水的科学；hydrologist 是从事它的人。

entries.definition: Relating to the science; it describes data or cycles, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 与这门科学有关的；它描述数据或循环，不指人。

entries.definition: A person who measures and charts water bodies for navigation; the work is mapping rather than cycle science.
entries.definitionCN: 为航行测量并绘制水体的人；其工作是制图，而不是循环科学。

entries.definition: A person who studies groundwater in rock; it is a branch of hydrology, not the whole profession.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩石中地下水的人；它是水文学的一个分支，不是整个职业。

entries.definition: An engineer who designs supply and drainage works; a hydrologist supplies the water data that engineer uses.
entries.definitionCN: 设计供水与排水工程的工程师；水文学家提供其使用的水数据。

entries.definition: A specialist in atmospheric water and precipitation; the focus is weather, not the whole land-water cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 研究大气水与降水的专家；重点在天气，而非整个陆水循环。

entries.definition: A scientist who studies organisms and their environment; an ecohydrologist works where water and life meet.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物与其环境的科学家；生态水文专家工作在水与生命交汇处。

entries.definition: A trained volunteer who collects data; a citizen hydrologist is the water-specific version.
entries.definitionCN: 收集数据的受训志愿者；公民水文学家是水领域的专称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real agent suffix, real professional titles and real branch names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实施事后缀、真实职业头衔与真实分支名称。

normal.en: Hydrology plus -ist makes the person who does hydrology.
normal.cn: hydrology 加 -ist，就是做水文学的人。

normal.en: The hydrologist reads the gauge, not just the textbook.
normal.cn: 水文学家读水尺，不只读教科书。

normal.en: Engineering, ecology and climate give the role its compound titles.
normal.cn: 工程、生态与气候给这个角色带来复合头衔。

normal.en: A hydrographer maps water; a hydrologist explains its movement.
normal.cn: 水文测量员绘制水，水文学家解释水的运动。

normal.en: A citizen hydrologist is a trained volunteer in the same network.
normal.cn: 公民水文学家是同一网络中的受训志愿者。

abstract.en: Picture a person kneeling at a gauge while a whole valley's water passes by.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人跪在水尺旁，整个山谷的水从身边流过。

abstract.en: Picture a detective following a missing river underground.
abstract.cn: 想象一名侦探在地下去追一条消失的河。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge between a rain cloud and a city's taps.
abstract.cn: 想象一座连接雨云与城市水龙头的桥。

examples.en: The hydrologist warned that the aquifer was being mined.
examples.cn: 水文学家警告含水层正在被透支。

examples.en: A hydrologist must explain uncertainty, not just averages.
examples.cn: 水文学家必须解释不确定性，而不只是平均值。

examples.en: The hydrologist's forecast gave the town two days to evacuate.
examples.cn: 水文学家的预报给小镇争取了两天撤离时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「hydrology（水文学）+ -ist（从事者）」——从事水文学的人 → 水文学家

root: 希腊 hydōr「水」（更深来源不确定，*wed- 为重构）+ -logia「研究」→ hydrology；加希腊 -istēs / 拉丁 -ista / 法语 -iste 形成的人物后缀 -ist → hydrologist。十九世纪起成为职业标签。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one practitioner: researcher, field worker, monitoring technician, consultant, engineering specialist, ecohydrologist, climate hydrologist and citizen volunteer.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一类从业者展开：研究者、野外工作者、观测员、顾问、工程专家、生态水文专家、气候水文专家与公民志愿者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person kneeling at a river gauge, a catchment map spread on the table behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人蹲在河岸水尺旁，身后的桌上摊着流域图。

branches.en: THEORY TO FIELD: the researcher and the gauge reader are the same role in two settings.
branches.cn: 从理论到野外：研究者与读水尺的人是同一角色在两种场景。

branches.en: SENSOR TO DESIGN: trustworthy readings become the design flood an engineer can use.
branches.cn: 从传感器到设计：可信的读数变成工程师可用的设计洪水。

branches.en: THE CONSULTANT: an estimate becomes a dam or drain on the ground.
branches.cn: 顾问：一份估算落到地上，变成大坝或排水沟。

branches.en: THE ECOLOGIST: the same training extends to how water shapes ecosystems.
branches.cn: 生态水文：同一套训练延伸到水如何塑造生态系统。

branches.en: CLIMATE TO CROWD: global projections and volunteer records both feed the same network.
branches.cn: 从气候到公众：全球预测与志愿者记录都汇入同一网络。

intro.en: Hydrologist is a transparent person noun: the field name plus -ist. The whole word can be read from its base and its agent suffix.
intro.cn: hydrologist 是透明的人物名词：领域名加 -ist。整个词可从基词与施事后缀读出。

latinIntro.en: The person suffix reached English through Latin -ista and French -iste from Greek -istēs; the base hydrology is Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 人物后缀经拉丁 -ista 与法语 -iste 上溯希腊 -istēs 进入英语；基词 hydrology 属希腊语。

items.example: Hydrology is the base of the title.
items.exampleCN: hydrology 是这个头衔的基词。

items.meaning: a person who does or follows
items.example: Biology plus -ist gives biologist.
items.exampleCN: biology 加 -ist 得到 biologist。

items.example: The hydrologist read the gauge at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 水文学家在黎明读取水尺。

items.example: Hydrologists shared the station data.
items.exampleCN: 水文学家们共享了站点数据。

items.example: The hydrological record spans a century.
items.exampleCN: 水文记录跨越一个世纪。

items.example: The hydrologic model runs daily.
items.exampleCN: 水文模型每日运行。

items.example: The hydrograph showed a sharp peak.
items.exampleCN: 过程线显示一个尖峰。

items.example: The hydrogeologist logged the borehole.
items.exampleCN: 水文地质学家记录了钻孔。

items.example: The hydrometeorologist forecast the rainfall.
items.exampleCN: 水文气象学家预报了降雨。

items.meaning: a specialist in water and ecosystems
items.example: The ecohydrologist mapped the drying wetland.
items.exampleCN: 生态水文专家绘出了干涸的湿地。

latinEntries.structure: -ista (m./f. agent suffix, medieval and modern Latin)

definition_zh: 等位基因；同一基因位置上的一种替代版本
definition_en: one of two or more alternative forms of a gene at the same position on a chromosome
core_image: 同一把椅子上放着可替换的坐垫，位置不变，垫子的花色不同
scene: 遗传课上，同一朵花的花色由同一个位置上的两份遗传信息决定。老师说： This plant carries two different alleles for flower color.
sceneCN: 这里指「等位基因」（第 1 个义项：同一基因位置上的一种可替代版本）；句意为这株植物在花色这个基因上携带两个不同的等位基因。

pos.zh: 等位基因；同一基因座的替代版本（可数，复数 alleles）

senses.title: One version of a gene
senses.definition: one of the alternative forms that a gene can take at a fixed position on a chromosome
senses.definitionCN: 一个基因在染色体固定位置上可以采取的一种替代形式
senses.example: This plant carries two different alleles for flower color.
senses.exampleCN: 这株植物在花色这个基因上携带两个不同的等位基因。
senses.why: The word names a version, not a place: the locus stays the same, while the sequence at that locus differs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一个版本，而不是一个位置：基因座不变，该位置上的序列却不同。

senses.title: One member of a pair
senses.titleCN: 成对等位基因中的一方
senses.definition: one of the two copies of a gene that a diploid organism carries
senses.definitionCN: 二倍体生物携带的两份基因拷贝中的一份
senses.example: Each parent contributed one allele to the child.
senses.exampleCN: 每个亲代都向孩子贡献了一个等位基因。
senses.why: Because chromosomes come in pairs, alleles are usually discussed in pairs, one inherited from each parent.
senses.whyCN: 因为染色体成对存在，等位基因通常也成对讨论，一份来自一个亲代。

senses.title: Multiple alleles in a population
senses.definition: any of three or more alternative forms of the same gene found in a population
senses.definitionCN: 同一基因在群体中出现的三种或更多替代形式之一
senses.example: Human blood groups depend on multiple alleles at one locus.
senses.exampleCN: 人类血型取决于同一基因座上的复等位基因。
senses.why: A single individual carries two copies, but a whole population can hold many versions, so the noun extends beyond the pair.
senses.whyCN: 单个个体只携带两份，但整个群体可以拥有许多版本，因此这个名词超出成对的范围。

senses.title: A dominant allele
senses.definition: an allele whose effect is visible even when only one copy is present
senses.definitionCN: 只有一份拷贝也能表现出效果的等位基因
senses.example: The dominant allele produces a dark seed coat.
senses.exampleCN: 这个显性等位基因产生深色种皮。
senses.why: The allele itself is neutral; 'dominant' describes what happens when it meets a different version in the same cell.
senses.whyCN: 等位基因本身是中性的；「显性」描述的是它与另一版本在同一细胞中相遇时的结果。

senses.title: A recessive allele
senses.definition: an allele whose effect is hidden when a dominant allele is present
senses.definitionCN: 与显性等位基因同时存在时效果被掩盖的等位基因
senses.example: The recessive allele reappears in the next generation.
senses.exampleCN: 隐性等位基因在下一代重新出现。
senses.why: A recessive version is still present and still inherited; it is only its visible effect that is covered.
senses.whyCN: 隐性版本仍然存在、仍然可遗传，被盖住的只是它可见的效果。

senses.title: A mutant allele
senses.definition: an allele produced by a mutation and differing from the original sequence
senses.definitionCN: 由突变产生、与原始序列不同的等位基因
senses.example: The mutant allele removes one base from the sequence.
senses.exampleCN: 这个突变等位基因从序列中删去了一个碱基。
senses.why: New alleles arise by mutation, so the word is also used for the fresh version before it spreads in a population.
senses.whyCN: 新的等位基因由突变产生，因此这个词也用来指在群体中扩散之前的那个新版本。

senses.title: A wild-type allele
senses.definition: the allele regarded as the standard or original form in a population
senses.definitionCN: 在群体中被视为标准或原始形式的等位基因
senses.example: The wild-type allele restores the normal wing shape.
senses.exampleCN: 野生型等位基因恢复了正常的翅形。
senses.why: Once a mutant is known, the common version needs a name, and 'wild type' marks the reference against which change is measured.
senses.whyCN: 一旦已知某个突变，常见版本就需要一个名称，「野生型」标记出衡量变化的参照。

senses.title: Allele frequency
senses.titleCN: 等位基因频率（群体层面）
senses.definition: the proportion of a particular allele among all copies of that gene in a population
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定等位基因在群体中该基因全部拷贝里所占的比例
senses.example: The allele frequency rose after the drought.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱之后该等位基因的频率上升了。
senses.why: Population genetics turns the version into a share, which is why the word appears in frequency counts and not only in pedigrees.
senses.whyCN: 群体遗传学把这个版本变成一个占比，因此这个词不仅出现在系谱中，也出现在频率统计中。

intro.en: Allele is a shortened form of allelomorph, a term coined in the early twentieth century from Greek allelon 'one another' and morphe 'form'. It is Greek in origin, with no Latin source. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: allele 是 allelomorph 的缩短形式；后者于 20 世纪初由希腊 allelon「彼此」与 morphe「形式」构成。它源自希腊语，没有拉丁语来源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Allēlon means 'of one another, mutually'. It marks the relation between alternative versions that occupy the same place.
items.cn: allēlon 意为「彼此的、相互的」，标记占据同一位置的不同版本之间的关系。

items.en: Morphē meant 'form, shape'. In scientific compounds it names a physical or structural form.
items.cn: morphē 意为「形式、形状」，在科学复合词中命名物理或结构形式。

items.en: The compound allelomorph was coined in the early 1900s, generally associated with William Bateson, for alternative forms of a gene.
items.cn: 复合词 allelomorph 于 1900 年代初被造出，一般与 William Bateson 相关，用来指基因的替代形式。

items.en: Allele is the shortened form and became the standard term in genetics; the longer allelomorph survives mainly in historical writing.
items.cn: allele 是缩短形式，后来成为遗传学的标准术语；较长的 allelomorph 主要留在历史文献中。

items.en: Modern genetics extends the word to allele frequencies, multiple alleles and reference alleles such as the wild type.
items.cn: 现代遗传学把这个词扩展到等位基因频率、复等位基因以及野生型等参照版本。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates and root): the exact coinage date of allelomorph is not settled, and the deeper origin of Greek allos 'other' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与词根）：allelomorph 的确切造词年代未有定论；希腊 allos「其他」的更深来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same Greek elements that are easily confused; group two holds neighbouring genetic terms for position and version.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊成分、容易混淆的形式；第二组是表示位置与版本的邻近遗传学术语。

entries.definition: The long historical word for an allele; it is the same concept, not a different kind of gene.
entries.definitionCN: 指等位基因的早期长词；是同一概念，而非另一类基因。

entries.definition: Relating to an allele; it describes a relationship, while allele names the version itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指与等位基因相关的；描述关系，而 allele 命名版本本身。

entries.definition: The state of existing as alternative forms at one locus; it is the abstract noun, not a countable allele.
entries.definitionCN: 指在同一基因座以替代形式存在的状态；是抽象名词，不是可数的等位基因。

entries.definition: The share of one allele among all copies in a population; it is a number, not the allele.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一等位基因在群体全部拷贝中的占比；是一个数值，不是等位基因本身。

entries.definition: A unit of inheritance at a locus; an allele is one version of that unit.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个基因座上的遗传单位；等位基因是该单位的一个版本。

entries.definition: The fixed position on a chromosome; alleles occupy a locus but are not the locus.
entries.definitionCN: 指染色体上的固定位置；等位基因占据基因座，但并不等于基因座。

entries.definition: The combination of alleles an individual carries; it is the pair, not either member.
entries.definitionCN: 指个体携带的等位基因组合；是成对的组合，而非其中一方。

entries.definition: Any differing version of a sequence; allele is its standard term when the version sits at a known gene locus.
entries.definitionCN: 指序列的任何不同版本；当该版本位于已知基因座时，标准术语就是等位基因。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: allelo- 'one another' + -morph 'form': alternative forms of one another.
normal.cn: allelo-「彼此」+ -morph「形式」：彼此替代的不同形式。

normal.en: The family runs allele, allelic, allelism, allelomorph, multiallelic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 allele、allelic、allelism、allelomorph、multiallelic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases pair it with dominance: dominant allele, recessive allele.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它与显隐性配对：显性等位基因、隐性等位基因。

normal.en: A gene is the position; an allele is one text written at that position.
normal.cn: 基因是位置，等位基因是写在该位置上的一版文字。

normal.en: Population genetics counts allele frequencies, not individual alleles alone.
normal.cn: 群体遗传学统计等位基因频率，而不只统计单个等位基因。

abstract.en: Picture one parking space where different cars can park.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个车位，可以停不同的车。

abstract.en: Picture one role in a play played by different actors on different nights.
abstract.cn: 想象同一出戏里的一个角色，不同夜晚由不同演员扮演。

abstract.en: Picture one socket that accepts several interchangeable parts.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个插口可以接上几种可互换的零件。

examples.en: A child inherits one allele from each parent.
examples.cn: 孩子从每个亲代各继承一个等位基因。

examples.en: The two alleles differ by a single base pair.
examples.cn: 这两个等位基因只差一个碱基对。

examples.en: Selection changed the allele frequencies within a decade.
examples.cn: 选择在十年内改变了等位基因频率。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿利尔」——同一个座位上轮流坐的另一个人 → 等位基因

root: 希腊 allelon「彼此」+ morphe「形式」，经早期术语 allelomorph 缩短而来；无拉丁语来源，属纯粹希腊来源的科学复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one position: a fixed locus accepts alternative versions, and those versions are then paired, counted across a population, and labelled by their effects.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个位置展开：固定的基因座接受不同版本，这些版本再被成对讨论、在群体中计数，并按效果获得标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one seat with interchangeable cushions.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个座位上放着可替换的坐垫。

branches.en: VERSION AND PAIR: one alternative form, and the two copies a diploid organism carries.
branches.cn: 版本与成对：一个替代形式，以及二倍体生物携带的两份拷贝。

branches.en: MANY VERSIONS: a population can hold more than two forms at one locus.
branches.cn: 多个版本：一个群体在同一基因座可以拥有两种以上的形式。

branches.en: EXPRESSION: dominant and recessive describe what happens when two versions meet.
branches.cn: 表现：显性与隐性描述两个版本相遇时发生什么。

branches.en: ORIGIN AND REFERENCE: mutant versions are new, wild-type versions are the standard.
branches.cn: 来源与参照：突变版本是新的，野生型版本是标准。

branches.en: POPULATION: the version becomes a share in a gene pool.
branches.cn: 群体：版本变成基因库中的一个占比。

intro.en: Allele is built from two Greek combining elements, allelo- 'one another' and -morph 'form'; it is a scientific compound, not a Latin root with suffixes.
intro.cn: allele 由两个希腊组合成分构成：allelo-「彼此」与 -morph「形式」；它是科学复合词，而非拉丁词根加后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element here: allēlon and morphē are Greek, and the word was coined inside modern genetics from Greek materials.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分：allēlon 与 morphē 都是希腊语，这个词是在现代遗传学内部用希腊语材料造出的。

items.structure: Greek allēlon (of one another) as a combining form
items.example: The element marks versions that stand in place of one another.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分标记彼此替代的版本。

items.example: The suffix also appears in polymorphic.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀也出现在 polymorphic 中。

items.meaning: an alternative form of a gene
items.example: Each allele sits at the same locus.
items.exampleCN: 每个等位基因都位于同一基因座。

items.example: Allelic variation is common in wild populations.
items.exampleCN: 等位变异在野生群体中很常见。

items.meaning: the state of being alternative forms
items.example: Allelism at one locus produces several phenotypes.
items.exampleCN: 同一基因座的等位性产生几种表型。

items.meaning: the older term for an allele
items.example: Allelomorph is now mainly historical.
items.exampleCN: allelomorph 现在主要见于历史文献。

items.example: Multiallelic loci complicate diagnosis.
items.exampleCN: 多等位基因的基因座使诊断复杂化。

items.meaning: the share of one allele in a population
items.meaningCN: 某一等位基因在群体中的占比
items.example: The allele frequency stayed near one half.
items.exampleCN: 该等位基因频率保持在二分之一附近。

definition_zh: 在数量上；从数量上；定量地；以数值方式；按数量计算地
definition_en: in terms of amount or number, especially by measuring and expressing things numerically
core_image: 把一堆模糊的感觉装进量杯，读出具体刻度
scene: 这里指「在数量上」。 The two lakes differ quantitatively in depth but not in water quality.
sceneCN: 这里 quantitatively 是「在数量上」（第 1 个义项：就深度这一可计量的量而言）；句意：这两个湖在深度上数量不同，但水质并无差别。图中可辨识物件：两支带刻度的量筒、标着数字的深度尺。

pos.zh: 在数量上；定量地；以数值方式

senses.title: In terms of amount
senses.definition: as far as amount, size or number is concerned rather than quality
senses.definitionCN: 就数量、规模或数目而言，而非性质
senses.example: The two proposals differ quantitatively but not in principle.
senses.exampleCN: 这两项提案在数量上不同，但原则上一致。
senses.why: Quantus meant 'how much'. The adverb sets the comparison on the scale of amount: it asks how much there is, not what kind it is.
senses.whyCN: quantus 意为“多少”。这个副词把比较放到数量尺度上：它问的是有多少，而不是什么性质。

senses.title: By measurement, not impression
senses.titleCN: 以测量而非印象的方式
senses.definition: by counting or measuring rather than by description or judgement
senses.definitionCN: 通过计数或测量，而非描述或判断
senses.example: The damage was assessed quantitatively with satellite images and ground counts.
senses.exampleCN: 损害通过卫星影像与地面计数作了定量评估。
senses.why: Here the adverb names a method: instead of saying 'severe', the researcher produces a number that others can check.
senses.whyCN: 这里的副词命名一种方法：研究者不说“严重”，而是给出别人可以核查的数字。

senses.title: Expressed as numbers
senses.definition: in a form that can be written as figures and compared arithmetically
senses.definitionCN: 以可以写成数字并进行算术比较的形式
senses.example: The report described the shortage quantitatively as a gap of four hundred units.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把短缺定量描述为四百个单位的缺口。
senses.why: Expression is the point here: an observation becomes numerical so that it can enter tables, ratios and models.
senses.whyCN: 这里的要点是表达：观察变成数值，从而能进入表格、比值与模型。

senses.title: In experimental practice
senses.definition: as a laboratory or field procedure that produces measurable values
senses.definitionCN: 作为产生可测数值的实验室或现场程序
senses.example: The team studied the reaction quantitatively by tracking mass at every minute.
senses.exampleCN: 团队每分钟记录质量，从而定量研究这一反应。
senses.why: Experimental science uses the adverb for procedure: the apparatus is arranged so that the outcome comes out as a reading, not an opinion.
senses.whyCN: 实验科学用这个副词指操作程序：仪器被安排得使结果呈现为读数，而不是意见。

senses.title: By counts and rates
senses.definition: through counts, frequencies or rates that can be added and compared
senses.definitionCN: 通过可相加、可比较的计数、频次或比率
senses.example: The survey compared the two districts quantitatively using hospital admissions.
senses.exampleCN: 该调查用住院人数对两个区作了定量比较。
senses.why: Statistics speaks of what can be counted: admissions, frequencies, rates. The adverb marks that those counts, not stories, carry the comparison.
senses.whyCN: 统计学谈可计数之物：住院人数、频次、比率。这个副词标记承载比较的是这些计数，而非故事。

senses.title: In a measurable degree
senses.definition: to a degree that can be measured and stated as an amount
senses.definitionCN: 达到可被测量并表述为一个数量的程度
senses.example: Performance improved quantitatively, though reviewers still found the writing weak.
senses.exampleCN: 表现在数量上有提升，不过评审仍认为文字薄弱。
senses.why: Sometimes the adverb limits a claim: whatever improved did so in measurable amount, while quality may have stayed the same.
senses.whyCN: 有时这个副词限定主张：提升发生在可度量的数量上，而质量可能没变。

senses.title: On the scale of quantity
senses.definition: judged on a scale of more or less rather than better or worse
senses.definitionCN: 按多与少的标尺判断，而非按好与坏
senses.example: The two cities are quantitatively similar in size but qualitatively very different.
senses.exampleCN: 这两座城市在规模上数量相近，性质上却大不相同。
senses.why: The adverb names the axis of comparison: one city may be bigger while the other is livelier, and only size belongs to this axis.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词命名比较的轴：一座城市可能更大，另一座更有活力，而只有规模属于这条轴。

senses.title: By numerical standard
senses.definition: according to a numerical threshold or target rather than a general impression
senses.definitionCN: 依据数值门槛或目标，而非整体印象
senses.example: Applicants were ranked quantitatively against a published scoring grid.
senses.exampleCN: 申请人依照公布的评分表按数值排序。
senses.why: Institutions use the adverb when a number decides: a grid, a threshold or a score replaces the feeling that something is good enough.
senses.whyCN: 机构在由数字决定时使用这个副词：评分表、门槛或分数取代了“够好”的感觉。

intro.en: Quantitatively is quantitative plus -ly. Quantitative comes from Medieval Latin quantitativus, built on quantitas, 'quantity', from quantus, 'how much or how many'. The Roman interrogative about size became the modern word for numerical measurement.
intro.cn: quantitatively 是 quantitative 加 -ly。quantitative 来自中古拉丁 quantitativus，建于 quantitas“数量”之上，而后者出自 quantus“多少”。罗马人问大小的疑问词，成了现代表示数值测量的词。

items.en: Quantus was the interrogative and relative word for 'how much, how many'. It asked about amount rather than kind; its partner qualis asked about kind.
items.cn: quantus 是表示“多少”的疑问与关系词，问的是数量而非种类；与之配对的 qualis 问的是种类。

items.en: Quantitas turned the question into a noun: 'amount, quantity, magnitude'. It let speakers talk about size as a thing in itself.
items.cn: quantitas 把疑问变成名词：“数量、量、大小”，使说话者能把规模当作一种事物来谈。

items.en: Scholars formed quantitativus for what belongs to quantity, in contrast with qualitativus for what belongs to quality.
items.cn: 学者造出 quantitativus 指属于数量的东西，与指属于性质的 qualitativus 相对。

items.en: English adopted quantitative through French and used it first in philosophy and mathematics, where the quantity/quality pair was already standard.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入 quantitative，最初用于哲学与数学，那里“量/质”的配对已是标准。

items.en: As chemistry and physics demanded numbers, quantitative became the label for methods that count, weigh and calibrate.
items.cn: 随着化学与物理要求数字，quantitative 成为计数、称重与校准方法的标签。

items.en: Economics and social research spread the adverb to surveys, scoring grids and quantitative easing in monetary policy.
items.cn: 经济学与社会科学把这个副词扩散到调查、评分表，以及货币政策中的量化宽松。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the adverb from the adjective, the noun and the different-root qualitative. The meaning group contrasts numerical, measurable and statistical description.
note.cn: 形近组区分副词与形容词、名词，以及词根不同的 qualitative；词义组比较数值、可测与统计三类描述。

entries.definition: relating to amount. It describes the kind of data, while quantitatively describes how something is expressed or compared.
entries.definitionCN: 与数量相关的。它描述数据种类，而 quantitatively 描述表达或比较的方式。

entries.definition: an amount or number. It is the base noun behind the whole family.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或数目。它是整个词族背后的基础名词。

entries.definition: in terms of quality. It looks parallel but comes from qualis 'of what kind', not quantus 'how much'.
entries.definitionCN: 就性质而言。它看起来结构平行，却来自 qualis“何种”，而非 quantus“多少”。

entries.definition: in a way that can be expressed as a quantity. It stresses possibility, while quantitatively stresses the mode of treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 以可以表示为数量的方式。它强调可能性，而 quantitatively 强调处理方式。

entries.definition: by means of numbers. It is close to sense 03 but says nothing about measuring method.
entries.definitionCN: 借助数字地。它接近第 3 义项，但不涉及测量方法。

entries.definition: to a degree that can be measured. It often modifies improvement or change, as in sense 06.
entries.definitionCN: 达到可测量的程度。它常修饰改进或变化，如第 6 义项。

entries.definition: according to statistical methods. It adds probability and sampling, which quantitatively alone does not.
entries.definitionCN: 按统计方法地。它增加概率与抽样，而单说 quantitatively 没有这些。

entries.definition: by calculation with numbers. It points to the operation rather than the measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 用数字计算地。它指向运算，而非测量。

normalIntro.en: These hooks fix the word to the question 'how much?', then let the answer become measurement, expression, counting, degree and standard.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词固定在“多少”这一问句上，再让答案变成测量、表达、计数、程度与标准。

normal.en: Split it as quant + itative + ly: how much + adjective + how. It answers 'how?' with numbers.
normal.cn: 拆成 quant + itative + ly：多少、形容词、方式。它用数字回答“如何”。

normal.en: Picture pouring a vague complaint into a measuring jug and reading a scale.
normal.cn: 想象把一句模糊的抱怨倒进量杯，读出刻度。

normal.en: Two lakes can be quantitatively different in depth while qualitatively identical in taste.
normal.cn: 两个湖在深度上可以有数量差异，在味道上却性质相同。

normal.en: A survey that counts admissions works quantitatively; one that records interviews works qualitatively.
normal.cn: 统计住院人数的调查按定量工作；记录访谈的调查按定性工作。

normal.en: When a scoring grid decides the ranking, the decision was made quantitatively.
normal.cn: 当评分表决定排名时，这个决定就是按数量作出的。

abstract.en: Keep the pair quantus/qualis in mind: one asks how much, the other asks of what kind.
abstract.cn: 心里记住 quantus 与 qualis 的配对：一个问多少，一个问何种。

abstract.en: The adverb can limit praise: quantitatively better means bigger or more, not necessarily finer.
abstract.cn: 这个副词可以限制赞美：数量上更好意味着更大或更多，未必更精细。

abstract.en: Notice the two directions: it can describe how something is measured, or how it is described. Both roads lead to numbers.
abstract.cn: 注意两个方向：它既可描述如何测量，也可描述如何表述。两条路都通向数字。

examples.en: The two economies differ quantitatively in output but share similar institutions.
examples.cn: 这两个经济体在产出数量上不同，但制度相似。

examples.en: The lab measured the pollution quantitatively rather than describing it in general terms.
examples.cn: 实验室对污染作了定量测量，而不是笼统描述。

examples.en: The reviewers asked whether the improvement could be shown quantitatively.
examples.cn: 评审要求证明这项改进能以数量方式呈现。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“宽提特提夫利”：把宽窄大小都提出来，逐条量成数字。

root: 拉丁 quantus“多少”派生 quantitas“数量”，中古拉丁 quantitativus 加英语 -ly 成副词；核心是“按多少、用数字来谈”。

sensesIntro.en: Each sense answers with a number: how much they differ, how the damage was measured, how the shortage is expressed, how the experiment was run, how the districts were counted, how far performance improved, which axis is being compared, and which threshold decided the ranking.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都用数字回答：差多少、损害如何测量、短缺如何表述、实验如何操作、各区如何计数、表现改进到什么程度、在比哪条轴、由哪个门槛决定排序。

core.en: Everything is pushed onto the axis of amount, where 'more' and 'less' are the only directions.
core.cn: 一切都被推到“数量”这条轴上，那里只有“更多”与“更少”两个方向。

branches.en: AXIS: the comparison is set on size, not on character.
branches.cn: 轴：比较建立在规模上，而非性质上。

branches.en: METHOD: counting and apparatus replace impression.
branches.cn: 方法：计数与仪器取代印象。

branches.en: EXPRESSION: the finding is written as a figure.
branches.cn: 表达：发现被写成数字。

branches.en: COUNTING: frequencies and rates carry the conclusion.
branches.cn: 计数：频次与比率承载结论。

branches.en: DEGREE: improvement and ranking are decided by a measurable threshold.
branches.cn: 程度：改进与排序由可测量的门槛决定。

intro.en: Quantitatively is quantus plus the quantity noun plus an adjective and an adverb ending. The items below follow the how-much stem and contrast it with the how-kind stem.
intro.cn: quantitatively 由 quantus、数量名词、形容词词尾与副词词尾构成。下列条目沿着“多少”词干，并与“何种”词干对照。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the interrogative and the noun. They explain why quantity, quantify and quantitative all begin with a question about size.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出疑问词与名词，解释为什么 quantity、quantify 与 quantitative 都以一个关于大小的疑问开头。

items.meaning: in terms of amount or number
items.example: The risks were compared quantitatively.
items.exampleCN: 这些风险作了定量比较。

items.example: Quantitative data filled the appendix.
items.exampleCN: 附录里满是定量数据。

items.example: A large quantity of sand was moved.
items.exampleCN: 大量沙子被运走。

items.example: It is hard to quantify the loss of trust.
items.exampleCN: 信任的损失难以量化。

items.meaning: the act of expressing as a quantity
items.example: The quantification of risk took months.
items.exampleCN: 风险的量化花了数月。

items.example: The interviews were analysed qualitatively.
items.exampleCN: 这些访谈作了定性分析。

items.example: Qualitative evidence came from diaries.
items.exampleCN: 定性证据来自日记。

items.meaning: a fixed amount; a unit of energy
items.example: The theory treats light as quanta.
items.exampleCN: 该理论把光当作量子。

definition_zh: 哄骗；用好话劝诱
definition_en: to persuade by flattery, sweet talk or gentle urging
core_image: 摊主把一颗糖塞进孩子手里，孩子乖乖就范
scene: 集市上，摊主笑着把糖果塞给孩子。 The vendor cajoled the child into tasting the cheese.
sceneCN: 这里 cajole 是「哄劝、甜言诱使」（第 1 个义项：以好话劝诱）；句意是摊主哄着孩子尝了那块奶酪。

derivatives.zh: 由 cajole 加 -ery 构成，义为「哄骗；甜言蜜语」
由动词加 -ing 转名词，义为「哄劝的行为」
由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「哄诱」

senses.title: To persuade by sweet talk
senses.definition: to persuade someone to do something by flattery or gentle deception
senses.definitionCN: 以奉承或温和的欺骗劝使某人做某事
senses.example: She cajoled her father into lending the car.
senses.exampleCN: 她哄得父亲把车借给了她。
senses.why: The French source literally meant to chatter like a jay.
senses.whyCN: 法语源词本义是「像松鸦一样喋喋不休」。

senses.title: To coax with persistence
senses.definition: to urge gently and persistently until agreement is won
senses.definitionCN: 以温和而持续的方式劝说得对方同意
senses.example: He cajoled and pleaded until the guard gave in.
senses.exampleCN: 他又哄又求，直到卫兵让步。
senses.why: Sweet talk repeated long enough wears down resistance.
senses.whyCN: 好话说得够久，抵抗便被磨平。

senses.title: To obtain by coaxing
senses.definition: to get something from someone by coaxing
senses.definitionCN: 用哄劝的方式从某人处取得
senses.example: The reporter cajoled a quote from the shy poet.
senses.exampleCN: 记者哄得那位腼腆诗人说了句引语。
senses.why: The act extends to the prize it wins.
senses.whyCN: 哄劝的行为延伸到它赢得的战利品。

intro.en: Cajole descends from French cajoler, to chatter like a jay in a cage, a bird of sweet nonsense.
intro.cn: cajole 源自法语 cajoler（如笼中松鸦般喋喋），像那只会说甜话的鸟。

items.en: behind Latin gaius, a jay, stands a reconstructed root for brightness or colour, uncertain in detail.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gaius（松鸦）背后是表「鲜亮、色彩」的重构词根，细节不确定。

items.en: gaius named the jay, the chattering bird.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gaius 指松鸦，那种爱聒噪的鸟。

items.en: gaiole, a cage, and jaiole tied the bird to its cage.
items.cn: 古法语 gaiole（笼子）与松鸦结缘。

items.en: cajoler came to mean to chatter, then to coax with sweet chatter.
items.cn: 法语 cajoler 由「喋喋」转指「以甜言哄劝」。

items.en: English borrowed cajole for insinuating persuasion.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入 cajole，指花言巧语的劝诱。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cajoler family; the near-meaning group gathers persuasion words.
note.cn: 形近组是 cajoler 同族；近义组是劝说类词。

definition_en: required by law, rule, office or custom, so that omitting it counts as a breach rather than as a free choice

senses.example: The charter makes attendance obligatory for every member of the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 章程规定委员会每位成员都必须出席。
senses.why: The Latin source means bound, and a rule that binds removes the option of simply not doing the thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁来源意为「被捆绑」，而把人绑住的规则，就取消了「不做」这个选项。

senses.title: Required by statute
senses.definition: imposed by legislation, so that failure to comply is an offence rather than a matter of taste
senses.definitionCN: 由立法施加，不遵守即构成违法，而不是品味问题
senses.example: Helmets are obligatory for riders under sixteen in this province.
senses.exampleCN: 在本省，十六岁以下的骑行者必须戴头盔。
senses.why: When a parliament binds everyone at once, the word stops describing a private duty and starts describing a legal floor.
senses.whyCN: 当议会一次性约束所有人，这个词就不再描述私人义务，而开始描述法律底线。

senses.title: Fixed by a professional code
senses.definition: laid down in a written procedure or code of practice, so that every qualified person must follow the same step
senses.definitionCN: 写进书面规程或执业守则，使每一位合格者都必须走同一步骤
senses.example: A second signature is obligatory before any sample leaves the freezer.
senses.exampleCN: 任何样本离开冷柜之前，第二个签名是必须的。
senses.why: Codes of practice borrow the word because a step that may be skipped is not a safeguard at all.
senses.whyCN: 执业守则借用这个词，因为可以被跳过的步骤根本算不上保障。

senses.title: Binding as a moral duty
senses.definition: felt or declared to be owed as a duty, even where no penalty is attached and no one can compel it
senses.definitionCN: 被感受或被宣告为应尽之责，即使没有处罚、也无人能够强迫
senses.example: He regarded a reply to every letter as obligatory, however late it came.
senses.exampleCN: 他认为每封信都该回，无论回得多晚。
senses.why: The sense of being bound does not need an external enforcer; a duty can bind a person from the inside.
senses.whyCN: 「被绑住」的感觉不必有外在执行者；义务也可以从内部把人绑住。

senses.title: A grammatical element that cannot be dropped
senses.definition: in linguistics, describing a word or category that a construction requires, such as an object with certain verbs
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学中指某一结构必须出现的词或范畴，例如某些动词必须带的宾语
senses.example: In this dialect the subject pronoun is obligatory even in short answers.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一方言里，即使简短回答也必须带主语代词。
senses.why: Grammar uses the word for what a sentence cannot do without, which is binding at the level of form.
senses.whyCN: 语法用这个词指句子离不开的成分，这是在形式层面的「捆绑」。

senses.title: A step a rite cannot omit
senses.definition: prescribed by a ceremony or institution as a step without which the act would not count as valid
senses.definitionCN: 由仪式或机构规定，缺少这一步，该行为便不成立
senses.example: The reading of the names is obligatory at the memorial service.
senses.exampleCN: 追思礼上宣读名字是不可省略的一环。
senses.why: A rite is a sequence in which each required step carries meaning, so omission is not economy but a broken form.
senses.whyCN: 仪式是一串每一步都有意义的程序，省略不是省事，而是把形式弄坏了。

senses.title: A course one must take
senses.definition: in education, describing a subject that every student in a programme has to complete before graduating
senses.definitionCN: 在教育中指某专业的学生在毕业前都必须完成的科目
senses.example: Statistics is obligatory for first-year students in every department.
senses.exampleCN: 统计课对每个系的一年级学生都是必修。
senses.why: Schools bind a whole cohort at once, so the word marks the line between what is required and what is merely offered.
senses.whyCN: 学校一次性约束整届学生，于是这个词标出「必修」与「只是开设」之间的界线。

senses.title: Expected by standing custom
senses.definition: required by convention rather than by written rule, so that skipping it draws disapproval instead of a penalty
senses.definitionCN: 由惯例而非成文规则要求，省略会招来非议而不是处罚
senses.example: A gift for the host is obligatory in that circle, though nobody writes it down.
senses.exampleCN: 在他们那个圈子里，给主人带礼物是必须的，尽管没有人写下来。
senses.why: Custom binds as tightly as law, and the word covers it because the pressure is felt as a requirement all the same.
senses.whyCN: 惯例绑人的力度不亚于法律，这个词也覆盖它，因为那种压力同样被感受为一项要求。

intro.en: Obligatory comes from Latin obligatorius 'binding, that which binds', a derivative of obligare 'to bind, to put under obligation', which joins ob- 'towards, against' to ligare 'to bind, tie'. The -ory ending marks 'having the nature of'. English took the adjective from Latin legal writing.
intro.cn: obligatory 来自拉丁 obligatorius「有约束力的、把人绑住的」，由 obligare「捆绑、使承担义务」派生，后者由 ob-「对着、朝向」加 ligare「绑、系」构成。词尾 -ory 表示「具有……性质的」。英语从拉丁法律文献中借入这个形容词。

items.en: Ligare meant 'to bind, tie, fasten'. It is the root of ligament, of religion and of ally, though each of those reaches it by a different prefix or path, so the family resemblance is real while the words are not interchangeable.
items.cn: ligare 意为「绑、系、捆紧」。它是 ligament、religion 与 ally 的词根，但这几个词各自经由不同的前缀或路径抵达它，因此同源属真，词义却不可互换。

items.en: Ob- 'towards, against' plus ligare produced obligare, 'to bind someone to something', literally to fasten a person to a duty or a promise.
items.cn: ob-「对着、朝向」加 ligare 构成 obligare，意为「把某人绑到某事上」，字面上就是把一个人捆在一项义务或承诺上。

items.en: The adjective obligatorius described what has binding force, and Late Latin legal writing used it of promises and duties that the law would enforce.
items.cn: 形容词 obligatorius 描述具有约束力的东西，晚期拉丁法律文献用它指法律会强制执行的那些承诺与义务。

items.en: The ending -ory forms adjectives meaning 'having the nature of, serving to', so obligatorius names something that possesses binding force rather than the act of binding.
items.cn: 词尾 -ory 构成形容词，表示「具有……性质的、用以……的」，因此 obligatorius 指某物带有约束力，而不是指捆绑这个动作。

items.en: The adjective entered English in legal and ecclesiastical contexts; the school sense of a required course and the grammatical sense are later extensions.
items.cn: 这个形容词进入英语后最早见于法律与教会语境；学校里的必修义与语法义都是后来的延伸。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of ligare): the pre-Latin shape of the root is reconstructed rather than recorded, and the exact path by which obligatorius entered English cannot be dated to a single year.
items.cn: 来源不确定（ligare 的更深来源）：这个词根在拉丁语之前的形式属重构而非有记录的形式；obligatorius 进入英语的确切路径也无法系于某一年份。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin binding root, and each one must be told apart by its prefix; two of them, religion and ally, look remote from the root but are genuine relatives reached by other prefixes. Group two holds adjectives of requirement that differ in who imposes the demand.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「绑」词根的词，须按前缀逐一分辨；其中 religion 与 ally 看上去离词根很远，却确是经其他前缀抵达的同源词。第二组是同样表示「必须」的形容词，区别在于由谁来施加要求。

entries.definition: The verb from the same Latin source: it means to bind someone by a promise or to do them a favour, and the favour sense has drifted far from obligation.
entries.definitionCN: 同出这一拉丁来源的动词：指以承诺约束某人，或帮某人一个忙，而「帮忙」这一义已离义务很远。

entries.definition: The noun names the tie itself, whether legal, financial or moral; obligatory describes whatever imposes such a tie.
entries.definitionCN: 这个名词指约束本身，无论法律的、金钱的还是道义的；obligatory 则形容施加这种约束的事物。

entries.definition: From ligare with a noun ending, naming the tissue that binds bones together; it keeps the physical sense of tying with no prefix added.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ligare 加名词词尾构成，指把骨头绑在一起的韧带；它保留了「系」的本义，且未加前缀。

entries.definition: Usually traced to re- 'back, again' plus ligare, a binding back; the prefix and the sense of a bond to the divine are wholly different from ob-.
entries.definitionCN: 通常追溯到 re-「回、再」加 ligare，意为「绑回去」；其前缀与「与神相连」之义都和 ob- 完全不同。

entries.definition: From ad- 'to' plus ligare, to bind to oneself; it names a partner bound by agreement, not a duty imposed on a person.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ad-「向」加 ligare 构成，意为「绑到自己这边」；它指以协定绑定的伙伴，而不是加于人的义务。

entries.definition: Required and backed by compulsion, often with a penalty; it stresses the force applied, where obligatory stresses the binding nature of the requirement.
entries.definitionCN: 被要求且有强制力支撑，常附带处罚；它强调施加的力量，而 obligatory 强调要求本身的约束性质。

entries.definition: Required by an authority's order, typically in law or official regulation; it is the closest neighbour but narrower in register.
entries.definitionCN: 由权威命令要求，多见于法律或官方规章；它是最接近的近义词，但语域更窄。

entries.definition: Describing an agreement or promise that legally holds the parties; it speaks of the tie created, not of a step everyone must perform.
entries.definitionCN: 形容在法律上约束各方的协议或承诺；它说的是所产生的约束关系，而不是人人必须执行的一步。

entries.definition: Necessary for a particular end, often of qualifications or supplies; necessity here serves a goal, not a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 为某一目的所必需，多指资格或用品；这里的必要是服务于目标，而不是服从规则。

entries.definition: Urgent and impossible to postpone; it describes practical urgency, while obligatory describes a formal requirement that may be resented.
entries.definitionCN: 紧急而无法推迟；它描述实务上的迫切，而 obligatory 描述可能招人反感的正式要求。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin morphemes, the genuine relatives reached by other prefixes, the real phrases, and the school and grammar uses that grew out of the legal core.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语素、经其他前缀抵达的真正同源词、真实的固定搭配，以及从法律核心生长出来的学校义与语法义。

normal.en: The root means to bind and the prefix means towards, so obligatory describes something that has been fastened onto a person as a duty.
normal.cn: 词根意为「绑」，前缀意为「朝向」，所以 obligatory 描述被当作义务捆到一个人身上的东西。

normal.en: The -ory ending means having the nature of, so the adjective names a quality of binding rather than the act of binding.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ory 意为「具有……性质的」，因此这个形容词指「有约束力」这一性质，而不是捆绑的动作。

normal.en: The family runs oblige, obligation, obligatorily, obligatoriness, obligate and obligative.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 oblige、obligation、obligatorily、obligatoriness、obligate 与 obligative。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the frame: obligatory for, make something obligatory, obligatory course, obligatory element.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出框架：对……是必须的、把某事规定为必须、必修课、必有成分。

normal.en: Ligament, religion and ally all reach the same binding root by other prefixes, so they resemble this family without sharing its prefix or its sense.
normal.cn: ligament、religion 与 ally 都经其他前缀抵达同一个「绑」词根，因此它们像这一词族，却不共享其前缀与词义。

abstract.en: Picture a door with only one handle, on the outside, so it can be opened for you but not by you.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇只有外侧把手的门，别人能为你打开，你自己却打不开。

abstract.en: Picture a signature line that is already printed, with no blank space beside it for a refusal.
abstract.cn: 想象一条已经印好的签名线，旁边没有留给出「不」的空白。

abstract.en: Picture a rope tied from a duty to a wrist, long enough to work with and too short to walk away.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳把一项义务系在手腕上，长度够干活，却不够走开。

examples.en: Reporting every accident is obligatory under the new safety code.
examples.cn: 根据新的安全规程，每起事故都必须上报。

examples.en: For most visitors a guided tour is optional, but for school groups it is obligatory.
examples.cn: 对多数参观者而言导览是可选项目，但对学校团体则是必须的。

examples.en: The grammar marks an obligatory object on every transitive verb in the list.
examples.cn: 这份清单把每个及物动词的必有宾语都标了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「对着 + 绑」——规则把人绑住不许松手，就是强制；被绑上的那件事，就是义务

root: 拉丁 obligatorius「有约束力的」← obligare「捆绑」= ob-（对着、朝向）+ ligare「绑、系」；词尾 -ory 表示「具有……性质的」。同根的 ligament 无前缀，religion 走 re-，ally 走 ad-，前缀不同故词义不同；ligare 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: something is tied to a person and cannot be dropped. The tie may be a rule with a penalty, a statute, a professional code, an inner duty, a slot a sentence requires, a step a rite requires, a course a degree requires, or a custom no one has written down.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：有件事被绑在一个人身上，放不下。这条绑绳可以是带处罚的规则、成文法律、执业规程、内心义务、句子必需的成分、仪式必需的一步、学位必需的课程，或无人写下却人人遵守的惯例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a duty fastened to a person like a rope that cannot be untied.
core.cn: 核心意象：一项义务像解不开的绳子一样系在人身上。

branches.en: ENFORCED FROM OUTSIDE: a rule and a statute both bind with a penalty behind them.
branches.cn: 外力执行：规则与法律都在背后带着处罚把人绑住。

branches.en: WRITTEN AND FELT: the same tie appears in a professional code and in a duty no one can enforce.
branches.cn: 写下的与感到的：同一条绑绳，既出现在执业规程里，也出现在无人能执行的义务里。

branches.en: THE SLOT A SENTENCE NEEDS: grammar binds form, where omission makes the sentence simply wrong.
branches.cn: 句子必需的槽位：语法绑住形式，省略之后句子就直接错了。

branches.en: RITE AND CURRICULUM: a ceremony and a degree each name steps that cannot be skipped.
branches.cn: 仪式与课程：典礼与学位都点出不可跳过的那几步。

branches.en: UNWRITTEN PRESSURE: custom binds without a penalty, and disapproval does the work of enforcement.
branches.cn: 不成文的压力：惯例没有处罚也照样绑人，非议承担了执行的角色。

intro.en: Obligatory is a Latin adjective built from a prefix, a verb root and an adjective ending, and all three parts recur in English legal and everyday vocabulary.
intro.cn: obligatory 是一个拉丁形容词，由前缀、动词词根与形容词词尾构成，这三部分都在英语的法律与日常词汇中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin ligare supplies the binding, ob- supplies the direction towards a person, and -ory turns the act into a quality; obligare and obligatio are the verb and noun behind the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ligare 提供「绑」，ob- 提供「朝某人而去」的方向，-ory 把动作变成性质；obligare 与 obligatio 是这个形容词背后的动词与名词。

items.example: The prefix shows that the binding is aimed at a particular person.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表明，这种捆绑是针对某一个具体的人的。

items.example: The root supplies the rope in the image behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供了这个词背后图景中的那根绳子。

items.meaningCN: 把某人绑到某事上；使承担义务
items.example: The verb names the act of fastening a duty to a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把一项义务系到一个人身上的动作。

items.example: Roman lawyers used the adjective of promises the courts would enforce.
items.exampleCN: 罗马法学家用这个形容词指法院会强制执行的承诺。

items.example: The charter makes attendance obligatory for every member.
items.exampleCN: 章程规定每位成员都必须出席。

items.example: The lease creates an obligation to repair the roof.
items.exampleCN: 这份租约产生了一项修缮屋顶的义务。

items.example: The form is obligatorily filed within seven days.
items.exampleCN: 这张表格必须在七天内提交。

items.example: The obligatoriness of the step is what makes the safeguard work.
items.exampleCN: 正是这一步的强制性，才让这项保障真正生效。

definition_zh: 排除；排斥；除外；被排除的状态；社会排斥
definition_en: the act of keeping someone or something out, or the state of being kept out
core_image: 一扇门在某人面前合上，门内是灯光和人群，门外只剩走廊。
scene: 实验室门口贴着「仅限授权人员」，新来的实习生被挡在门外。 A sign on the lab door reads authorised staff only, and the new intern stands outside: that is exclusion.
sceneCN: 这里 exclusion 是「被排除在外、不得进入」（第 1 个义项：被挡在某个范围之外的状态）；句意：实验室门口贴着仅限授权人员，新来的实习生被挡在门外，这就是被排除在外。

pos.zh: 排除；排斥；除外；被排除状态；（生态）竞争排斥

senses.title: Shutting someone out
senses.definition: the act of preventing a person or thing from entering or taking part
senses.definitionCN: 阻止人或物进入或参与的行为
senses.example: The exclusion of non-members from the vote caused an outcry.
senses.exampleCN: 把非会员排除在投票之外引发了抗议。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to shut the door. Exclusion is that closing seen as an act: the boundary is drawn by whoever holds the door.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为‘关上门’。exclusion 就是这次关门被视为一个动作：边界由掌着门的人画出。

senses.title: The state of being left out
senses.titleCN: 被排除的状态：人在门外的那一侧
senses.definition: the condition of being left outside a group, place, or activity
senses.definitionCN: 被留在群体、场所或活动之外的状态
senses.example: Her exclusion from the committee lasted two years.
senses.exampleCN: 她被排除在委员会之外长达两年。
senses.why: The same event can be told from the door's other side. Here the noun names the experience of the one who remains outside.
senses.whyCN: 同一件事可以从门的另一侧讲述。这里的名词命名的是留在门外那个人的经历。

senses.title: Exclusion clause
senses.titleCN: 除外条款：合同里预先排除的责任
senses.definition: a contractual or insurance clause that removes a risk or item from cover
senses.definitionCN: 把某项风险或项目排除在保障之外的合同或保险条款
senses.example: The policy's exclusion for flood damage was printed in bold.
senses.exampleCN: 保单对洪水损害的除外责任用粗体印出。
senses.why: Contracts define the protected space first, then list what is shut out of it. The clause is the door drawn on paper.
senses.whyCN: 合同先划定受保护的空间，再列出被关在门外的项目。条款就是画在纸上的那扇门。

senses.title: Social exclusion
senses.titleCN: 社会排斥：被挡在正常生活之外
senses.definition: the process by which groups are pushed to the margins of society and denied normal participation
senses.definitionCN: 某些群体被推到社会边缘、无法正常参与的过程
senses.example: Poor transport links deepen the social exclusion of rural families.
senses.exampleCN: 交通不便加深了农村家庭的社会排斥。
senses.why: Here the door is not one building but a whole set of institutions: work, school, housing, and health. Exclusion becomes structural rather than personal.
senses.whyCN: 这里的门不是一栋楼，而是一整套制度：工作、学校、住房与医疗。排斥由此变成结构性的，而非个人性的。

senses.title: Competitive exclusion
senses.titleCN: 竞争排斥：两个物种不能长期占同一生态位
senses.definition: the ecological principle that two species competing for the same resource cannot coexist indefinitely
senses.definitionCN: 两个物种争夺同一资源时无法无限期共存的生态学原理
senses.example: Competitive exclusion drove the native species from the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 竞争排斥把本地物种逐出了池塘。
senses.why: One species uses the shared resource slightly better, so the other is gradually shut out of its own niche. The door here is closed by competition, not policy.
senses.whyCN: 一个物种对共享资源的利用略好，另一个就被逐渐关在自己的生态位之外。这里的门由竞争关上，而非政策。

senses.title: Tax exclusion
senses.titleCN: 不计入项：税法里不纳入收入的部分
senses.definition: an item of income that is not counted for tax purposes
senses.definitionCN: 在计税时不计入收入的项目
senses.example: The tax exclusion for employer health cover reduced the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 雇主医保的免税待遇降低了税单。
senses.why: The tax base is a defined set. An exclusion removes one item before the rate is applied, so the item never enters the calculation.
senses.whyCN: 税基是一个被定义的集合。exclusion 在套用税率前移走一项，因此该项从未进入计算。

senses.title: Expulsion from an institution
senses.titleCN: 逐出：被学校或组织开除
senses.definition: the removal of a person from a school, club, or organization as a punishment
senses.definitionCN: 作为惩罚把某人从学校、俱乐部或组织中除名
senses.example: The exclusion was reduced to a suspension on appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 经上诉，开除处分被减为停学。
senses.why: An institution controls its own door. Expulsion is exclusion made punitive: the person is not merely outside but formally put outside.
senses.whyCN: 机构控制自己的门。开除是带惩罚性的 exclusion：当事人不仅在门外，而且是被正式放到门外。

senses.title: Exclusivity
senses.titleCN: 排他性：只让一部分人进入的安排
senses.definition: the quality of an arrangement that admits only a limited set of people
senses.definitionCN: 只接纳有限人群的安排所具有的性质
senses.example: The club's exclusion was part of its appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部的排他性正是其吸引力的一部分。
senses.why: Here exclusion is valued rather than resented: the closed door itself becomes the product, because being inside signals membership.
senses.whyCN: 这里的排斥被珍视而非怨恨：关着的门本身成了产品，因为‘在里面’标志着 membership。

intro.en: Exclusion is from Latin exclusio, from excludere, to shut out: ex- out plus claudere to shut. The same claudere runs through include, conclude, and clause.
intro.cn: exclusion 来自拉丁 exclusio，源头是 excludere‘关在外面’：ex-‘向外’加 claudere‘关’。同一个 claudere 贯穿 include、conclude 与 clause。

items.en: To shut, close, or enclose. It gives English close, clause, cloister, and the -clude verbs. The root image is a door or a barrier.
items.cn: 关、闭、围住。它给出英语 close、clause、cloister 以及 -clude 系列动词。词根意象是门或障碍。

items.en: Ex- out plus claudere shut: to shut out, exclude, or cut off. The verb assumes an inside that is being protected.
items.cn: ex-‘向外’加 claudere‘关’：关在外面、排除、切断。该动词预设了一个被保护的‘里面’。

items.en: A shutting out. In rhetoric it could also mean omission or rejection of a possibility; in law, a bar to entry.
items.cn: 关在外面。在修辞学里也可指省略或排除某种可能；在法律里指禁止进入。

items.en: French passed the noun to English. The legal sense of a bar or an exception travelled with it.
items.cn: 法语把名词传给英语，禁止进入或除外条款的法律义随之而来。

items.en: English exclusion is recorded in the 15c. Early uses were legal and institutional: exclusion from office, from a court, from a will.
items.cn: 英语 exclusion 在 15 世纪有记录。早期用法是法律与制度性的：排除公职、排除法庭、排除继承。

items.en: The 20c added social exclusion and competitive exclusion, extending the closed door from law to society and ecology.
items.cn: 20 世纪加入社会排斥与竞争排斥，把‘关上的门’从法律扩展到社会与生态。

note.en: The first group is the exclude family; the second compares ways of removing someone or something, each with a different mechanism.
note.cn: 第一组是 exclude 词族；第二组比较把人或物移走的不同方式，各自机制不同。

entries.definition: to shut someone or something out. It is the action; exclusion is the act or state.
entries.definitionCN: 把人或物关在外面；是动作，exclusion 是行为或状态。

entries.definition: limited to a particular group, or not shared. It describes the arrangement, not the act of shutting.
entries.definitionCN: 限于特定群体的，或不共享的；描述安排，而非关门动作。

entries.definition: only, and to the exclusion of everything else. It turns the adjective into a restriction on scope.
entries.definitionCN: 只；唯独；把其他一切排除在外。它把形容词变成范围限制。

entries.definition: tending to exclude people or things. It is used of rules, practices, and policies.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于排斥人或物的；用于规则、做法与政策。

entries.definition: something left out, often by mistake or by choice in writing. It does not require a door or a boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 被漏掉的东西，常因疏忽或书写选择；不需要门或边界。

entries.definition: the act of taking something away from its place. It focuses on the object being moved, not on who is kept out.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从其位置拿走；聚焦被移动的对象，而不是被挡在外面的人。

entries.definition: the act of forcing someone or something out, often physically. It is more violent than exclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 强行把人或物弄出去，常是物理性的；比 exclusion 更暴力。

entries.definition: the deliberate avoidance or shunning of a person by a group. It is exclusion carried out by many small refusals.
entries.definitionCN: 群体对某人有意回避、排斥；是许多次小拒绝共同完成的 exclusion。

entries.definition: the enforced separation of groups, especially by race or sex. It divides space rather than simply shutting one door.
entries.definitionCN: 按种族或性别等强制分隔群体；它分割空间，而不只是关一扇门。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ex- out plus claudere shut. Exclusion is the closing of a door in someone's face, seen either as an act or as a state.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ex-‘向外’加 claudere‘关’。exclusion 就是在某人面前关门，可作为动作也可作为状态来看。

normal.en: Ex- out, claudere shut: exclusion is being shut out.
normal.cn: ex- 向外，claudere 关：exclusion 就是被关在外面。

normal.en: Include and exclude are the two directions of the same door.
normal.cn: include 与 exclude 是同一扇门的两个方向。

normal.en: An exclusion clause is a door drawn on paper.
normal.cn: 除外条款就是画在纸上的一扇门。

normal.en: Social exclusion closes many doors at once.
normal.cn: 社会排斥同时关上许多扇门。

normal.en: A club's exclusion is its selling point: the closed door is the product.
normal.cn: 俱乐部的排他性就是卖点：关着的门本身是产品。

abstract.en: Every inside is made by an outside; exclusion is how a group learns its own shape.
abstract.cn: 每个‘里面’都由‘外面’造出；排斥是群体认识自身形状的方式。

abstract.en: The same closed door can be a punishment or a privilege, depending on which side you stand.
abstract.cn: 同一扇关着的门，可以是惩罚也可以是特权，取决于你站在哪一侧。

abstract.en: Exclusion is cheaper than inclusion, which is why systems drift toward it.
abstract.cn: 排斥比容纳便宜，所以系统会自然漂向排斥。

examples.en: The exclusion of the small firms from the scheme was challenged in court.
examples.cn: 把小公司排除在该计划之外的做法在法庭上受到挑战。

examples.en: He worked on the project to the exclusion of almost everything else.
examples.cn: 他做这个项目，几乎把其他一切排除在外。

examples.en: The report treated social exclusion as a health issue, not only a moral one.
examples.cn: 报告把社会排斥当作健康问题，而不只是道德问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一颗死路”——走到一颗标着‘死路’的门前，被关在外面：exclusion 排除、排斥。

root: 源自拉丁 excludere（ex-‘向外’+ claudere‘关’）与 exclusio‘关在外面’；核心是“把某人或某物挡在门外的动作或状态”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of exclusion, one image: a door closes and someone stays outside. The door may be a club, a contract, a society, a niche, a tax base, a school, or a membership rule.
sensesIntro.cn: exclusion 的八个义项共用一个意象：门关上，有人留在外面。这扇门可以是俱乐部、合同、社会、生态位、税基、学校或会员规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door closing with a person left in the corridor.
core.cn: 核心意象：门关上，一个人被留在走廊里。

branches.en: THE TWO SIDES OF THE DOOR: the act of shutting out and the experience of being outside.
branches.cn: 门的两侧：关门的动作与留在外面的经历。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN BOUNDARY: insurance clauses and tax rules remove items before they count.
branches.cn: 写下的边界：保险条款与税务规则在计算前移走项目。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL AND PUNITIVE DOOR: structural marginalization and formal expulsion both put a person outside.
branches.cn: 社会性与惩罚性的门：结构性边缘化与正式开除都把一个人放到外面。

branches.en: THE ECOLOGICAL DOOR: competition closes a niche on a rival species.
branches.cn: 生态的门：竞争对竞争者关上生态位。

branches.en: THE VALUED DOOR: exclusivity makes the closed door itself desirable.
branches.cn: 被珍视的门：排他性让关着的门本身变得有吸引力。

intro.en: Exclusion is ex- plus claud- plus -sion. The same root gives include, conclude, seclude, and the noun clause; the door image is shared across all of them.
intro.cn: exclusion 是 ex- 加 claud- 加 -sion。同一词根给出 include、conclude、seclude 与名词 clause；它们共享‘门’的意象。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms are claudere, excludere, and exclusio. Excludere is built from a real prefix and a real verb, so no reconstruction is needed here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁形式是 claudere、excludere、exclusio。excludere 由真实前缀与真实动词构成，这里不需要重构。

items.meaning: to shut out or leave out
items.example: The rules exclude late entries.
items.exampleCN: 规则排除迟交的参赛作品。

items.meaning: the act or state of being shut out
items.example: His exclusion from the team was temporary.
items.exampleCN: 他被排除在队伍之外是暂时的。

items.meaning: restricted to a few; not shared
items.example: The shop sells exclusive designs.
items.exampleCN: 这家店出售独家设计。

items.example: The room is used exclusively for meetings.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间只用于开会。

items.meaning: the state of being restricted to a few
items.example: The brand charges for exclusivity.
items.exampleCN: 这个品牌为排他性收费。

items.example: The zoning rules had an exclusionary effect.
items.exampleCN: 分区规则产生了排斥效果。

items.meaning: to shut inside, hence to contain
items.meaningCN: 包含；把……关在里面（in-‘在内’+ claudere‘关’）
items.example: The price includes breakfast.
items.exampleCN: 价格包含早餐。

items.meaning: to close together, hence to end or infer
items.meaningCN: 结束；得出结论（com-‘一起’+ claudere‘关’）
items.example: The talk concluded with a short summary.
items.exampleCN: 讲座以简短总结结束。

items.meaning: to shut apart, hence to isolate
items.meaningCN: 使隔离；隐居（se-‘分开’+ claudere‘关’）
items.example: The cabin was secluded by tall pines.
items.exampleCN: 小屋被高松林隔离起来。

items.meaning: a distinct part of a sentence or contract
items.meaningCN: 从句；条款；源自‘关闭、收束的部分’
items.example: The final clause limits the agreement to five years.
items.exampleCN: 最后一条条款把协议限制在五年内。

definition_zh: n. 瑕疵；污点；伤疤；v. 损毁；玷污
definition_en: a small flaw that spoils the perfection of something, or to spoil it
core_image: 白玉上的一粒黑点
scene: 买家对着灯细看白玉，指出一点黑痕。 The scandal blemished his spotless reputation.
sceneCN: 这里 blemish 是动词「玷污」（第 2 个义项：损坏原本完美之物）；句意是丑闻玷污了他无可挑剔的名声。

derivatives.zh: un- 加 blemished，义为「无瑕的；清白的」

senses.title: A small physical flaw
senses.definition: a mark or spot that spoils the surface or appearance
senses.definitionCN: 损坏表面或外观的痕迹或斑点
senses.example: The apple had one small blemish on its skin.
senses.exampleCN: 这只苹果表皮上有一处小瑕疵。
senses.why: Old French blessier meant to wound; a blemish is a tiny wound on a surface.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 blessier 意为「伤害」，blemish 即表面上的小伤。

senses.title: To spoil perfection
senses.definition: to damage the good condition or reputation of something
senses.definitionCN: 损坏某物完好的状态或名声
senses.example: The scandal blemished his spotless reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻玷污了他无可挑剔的名声。
senses.why: What wounds a surface wounds, too, a name held to be flawless.
senses.whyCN: 能伤表面者亦能伤被视为无瑕之名。

senses.title: A moral stain
senses.definition: a fault that stains an otherwise clean character or record
senses.definitionCN: 玷污本来清白品格或记录的过错
senses.example: One late payment was the only blemish on her credit file.
senses.exampleCN: 一次迟付款是她信用档案上唯一的污点。
senses.why: Records and characters are surfaces the eye of society inspects.
senses.whyCN: 记录与品格是社会目光检视的表面。

senses.title: A skin imperfection
senses.definition: a spot, pimple, or mark on the skin
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤上的斑点、丘疹或痕迹
senses.example: The cream promises to clear skin blemishes.
senses.exampleCN: 这款面霜号称能清除皮肤瑕疵。
senses.why: Skin is the most inspected surface of all, so beauty talk uses the word most.
senses.whyCN: 皮肤是被检视最多的表面，美妆语境因此最常用此词。

senses.title: A flaw in goods offered for sale
senses.definition: an imperfection that lowers the value of merchandise
senses.definitionCN: 降低商品价值的缺陷
senses.example: Blemished goods were sold at a discount.
senses.exampleCN: 有瑕疵的商品打折出售。
senses.why: Perfect surfaces fetch full price; any wound shows in the tag.
senses.whyCN: 完好表面值全价，一处伤痕便体现在价签上。

senses.title: A defect in a polished argument or text
senses.definition: a small weakness in something otherwise excellent
senses.definitionCN: 整体出色之作中的小弱点
senses.example: The only blemish in the essay is a weak conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章唯一的疵点是结尾无力。
senses.why: Writing is judged as a surface too; one dent catches the eye.
senses.whyCN: 文章亦被当作平面来审视，一处凹陷格外扎眼。

senses.title: A ritual imperfection in offerings
senses.definition: a defect that makes an animal unfit for sacrifice
senses.definitionCN: 使牲畜不合祭祀之用的缺陷
senses.example: The law forbade sacrificing animals with any blemish.
senses.exampleCN: 律法禁止献祭有任何瑕疵的牲畜。
senses.why: The altar demands perfection; the oldest moral use grew from it.
senses.whyCN: 祭坛要求完美，最古老的道德用法由此生长。

senses.title: To mar beauty of sound or movement
senses.definition: to spoil the flawless quality of a performance
senses.definitionCN: 破坏表演的完美品质
senses.example: One missed note blemished an otherwise perfect recital.
senses.exampleCN: 一个错音破坏了本已完美的独奏会。
senses.why: A performance is a surface of time; one dent is heard by everyone.
senses.whyCN: 表演是时间织成的表面，一处凹陷人人听得见。

intro.en: Blemish comes from Old French blemir, to wound or bruise.
intro.cn: blemish 来自古法语 blemir「伤害；使瘀青」。

items.en: probably from Frankish blesni, a wound, a Germanic borrowing into French.
items.cn: 一般认为出自法兰克语 blesni「伤口」，属日耳曼语借入法语。

items.en: blemissier and blemir meant to injure, bruise.
items.cn: 古法语 blemissier 与 blemir 意为「伤害、打伤」。

items.en: the legal sense of a defect in title or character formed in law French.
items.cn: 法律法语中形成了「产权或品格缺陷」的专业义。

items.en: English took blemish for both physical marks and moral stains.
items.cn: 英语于 13 至 14 世纪借入，兼指身体痕迹与道德污点。

items.en: now common in cosmetics, quality control, and moral commentary.
items.cn: 今常见于美妆、品控与道德评述。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the blem- sound; the near-meaning group gathers flaw words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 blem- 音；近义组收瑕疵类词。
