entries.definitionCN: 放逐——拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: marked with flaws
entries.definitionCN: 有瑕疵的——同根派生

entries.definition: to disappear
entries.definitionCN: 消失——拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a defect in structure or character
entries.definitionCN: 缺陷——偏内在结构

entries.definition: an imperfection lacking a part or quality
entries.definitionCN: 缺陷——偏功能缺失

entries.definition: a moral blot
entries.definitionCN: 污点——偏道德义

normalIntro.en: Blemish grew from a word for wounding; now it marks any small flaw.
normalIntro.cn: blemish 源自「伤害」之词，今指一切小瑕疵。

normal.en: Unblemished is the clean opposite.
normal.cn: unblemished 是无瑕的反义形容词。

normal.en: It works for skin, goods, and reputations.
normal.cn: 它可用于皮肤、商品与名声。

normal.en: A blemish is small; a ruin is total.
normal.cn: blemish 指小瑕疵，毁坏则是全盘的。

normal.en: Legal English still says title without blemish.
normal.cn: 法律英语仍说 title without blemish。

normal.en: Both noun and verb uses are common.
normal.cn: 名词与动词用法都常见。

abstract.en: See one black dot on a bowl of white pearls.
abstract.cn: 看一碗白珍珠上的一粒黑点。

abstract.en: Feel a fingernail scratch across polished glass.
abstract.cn: 感受指甲划过抛光玻璃的刺感。

abstract.en: Picture a perfect legal record spoiled by one late form.
abstract.cn: 想象被一份迟交表格毁掉的完美档案。

examples.en: The scandal blemished his spotless reputation.
examples.cn: 丑闻玷污了他无可挑剔的名声。

examples.en: The apple had one small blemish on its skin.
examples.cn: 这只苹果表皮上有一处小瑕疵。

examples.en: One late payment was the only blemish on her credit file.
examples.cn: 一次迟付款是她信用档案上唯一的污点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不乐意是」——玉上有个黑点，买家不乐意是必然的。

root: 古法语 blemir「伤害；使瘀青」（一般认为出自法兰克语 blesni「伤口」，日耳曼借词），经盎格鲁-法语在法律语境中形成「缺陷」义，13 至 14 世纪进入英语，兼指身体瑕疵与道德污点。

sensesIntro.en: From a wound on skin to a stain on character, blemish names the small flaw that perfect things cannot hide.
sensesIntro.cn: 从皮肤之伤到品格之污，blemish 指完美之物无法掩盖的小瑕疵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one black dot on flawless white jade
core.cn: 核心意象：无瑕白玉上的一粒黑点

branches.en: Marks on physical surfaces and skin
branches.cn: 实体表面与皮肤上的痕迹

branches.en: Spoiling what was perfect
branches.cn: 毁掉原本的完美

branches.en: Moral and ritual stains
branches.cn: 道德与祭祀上的污点

branches.cn: 贬值的商品瑕疵

branches.en: Weak spots in fine work
branches.cn: 佳作中的疵点

intro.cn: blemish 词族不大，但常见于品控语境。

latinIntro.cn: 日耳曼词源经古法语传入，无拉丁核心。

definition_zh: 因变量；实验中随自变量变化而被测量、被解释的结果变量
definition_en: the variable that is measured in an experiment and expected to change in response to the independent variable
core_image: 记录板上只留一列读数，每一行对应一种处理条件，最后一栏写着结果
scene: 记录板上只留一列读数，每一行对应一种处理条件。 Plant height is the dependent variable here, recorded after each week of treatment.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：实验中随自变量改变而被测量的结果变量；句意为株高在这里是因变量，每周处理后记录一次。图中可辨识物件：记录板、单列数字、处理标签、直尺。

a change in the dependent variable
the dependent variable and the independent variable

senses.title: The outcome that is measured
senses.definition: the factor that an experimenter measures, expected to respond to changes in the independent variable
senses.definitionCN: 实验者测量的因素，预期会随自变量的变化而作出反应
senses.example: Plant height is the dependent variable here, recorded after each week of treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 株高在这里是因变量，每周处理后记录一次。
senses.why: Its value is read only after the treatment is applied, so it hangs on the factor that was moved, and that dependence is the name.
senses.whyCN: 它的值只在处理实施之后才被读出，因此取决于被移动的那个因素，这种「依从」正是名称的由来。

senses.title: The response in statistics
senses.definition: in a statistical model, the quantity whose variation the analysis tries to account for
senses.definitionCN: 在统计模型中，分析试图解释其变异的那个量
senses.example: The response was treated as the dependent variable in every model.
senses.exampleCN: 每个模型都把响应量当作因变量。
senses.why: Statistics asks what explains variation, and the variable being explained sits on the outcome side of the equation.
senses.whyCN: 统计学追问什么解释了变异，而被解释的变量就坐在方程的「结果」一侧。

senses.title: The y of a function
senses.definition: in mathematics, the output of a function, whose value is fixed once the input is chosen
senses.definitionCN: 在数学中，函数的输出，其值在输入选定后即被确定
senses.example: In the equation, the dependent variable changes when the input changes.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个方程里，输入一变，因变量就变。
senses.why: A rule assigns one output to each input, so the output depends on the input by construction.
senses.whyCN: 规则为每个输入指定一个输出，因此输出在构造上就依赖于输入。

senses.title: The outcome in social research
senses.definition: in social science, the measured condition that a study tries to explain, such as a test score or a rate
senses.definitionCN: 在社会科学中，研究试图解释的被测状态，如考试分数或比率
senses.example: The study used the graduation rate as its dependent variable.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把毕业率作为因变量。
senses.why: When the outcome cannot be manipulated, it is still measured, and the word keeps the experimental image of reading a result.
senses.whyCN: 当结果无法被操纵时，它仍可被测量，这个词保留了「读出结果」的实验意象。

senses.title: The behaviour recorded in psychology
senses.definition: in psychology, the observed response, such as reaction time or a rating, treated as the outcome of a manipulation
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学中，被观察的反应，如反应时或评分，被视为操纵的结果
senses.example: Reaction time was the dependent variable in the attention task.
senses.exampleCN: 注意任务中的因变量是反应时。
senses.why: Behaviour is what the experiment can see, while the mental process is inferred, so the visible response becomes the measured variable.
senses.whyCN: 行为是实验看得见的东西，心理过程只能推断，因此可见的反应成了被测量的变量。

senses.title: The endpoint of a trial
senses.definition: in a clinical trial, the pre-specified outcome used to judge whether a treatment works
senses.definitionCN: 在临床试验中，用来判断治疗是否有效的预先指定结果
senses.example: The trial's dependent variable was the number of symptom-free days.
senses.exampleCN: 这项试验的因变量是无症状天数。
senses.why: A trial must name its outcome before it begins, so the measured endpoint is fixed in the protocol and called the dependent variable.
senses.whyCN: 试验必须在开始前指定结果，因此被测终点写进方案，并被称为因变量。

senses.title: The explained side of a regression
senses.definition: in regression analysis, the variable on the left of the equation, whose values the predictors are used to estimate
senses.definitionCN: 在回归分析中，方程左边的变量，其取值由预测变量来估计
senses.example: Income sat on the left as the dependent variable.
senses.exampleCN: 收入作为因变量放在左边。
senses.why: Regression draws a line from predictors to an outcome, and the outcome is dependent because the line is fitted to it.
senses.whyCN: 回归从预测变量画一条线到结果，结果之所以为因变量，是因为这条线是照着它拟合的。

senses.title: The quantity on the vertical axis
senses.definition: the quantity whose values are read up the vertical axis when a relation is graphed
senses.definitionCN: 作关系图时，其取值沿纵轴向上读取的量
senses.example: With yield as the dependent variable, the trend rises to the right.
senses.exampleCN: 以产量作因变量，趋势向右上升。
senses.why: By convention the effect is placed on the vertical axis, so the graph puts the dependent variable where the eye reads change.
senses.whyCN: 按惯例结果放在纵轴，因此图把因变量放在眼睛读取变化的位置。

senses.title: The outcome an economic model explains
senses.titleCN: 经济模型要解释的结果
senses.definition: in economics, the quantity a model seeks to account for, such as consumption responding to income
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学中，模型试图解释的量，如随收入变化的消费
senses.example: Consumption is the dependent variable, with income on the other side.
senses.exampleCN: 消费是因变量，收入在另一侧。
senses.why: A model is written to explain one quantity by others, and that quantity is dependent on the explanatory side.
senses.whyCN: 模型是为了用其他量解释某一个量，那个量就依赖于解释的一侧。

intro.en: Dependent variable joins dependent, from Latin dependere 'to hang from', to variable, from variare 'to change'. The pair with independent variable belongs to modern mathematics and experimental design.
intro.cn: dependent variable 把 dependent（拉丁语 dependere「悬挂于」）与 variable（variare「变化」）组合起来。它与自变量成对使用，属于现代数学与实验设计。

items.en: Dependere meant to hang from or be attached to, from de- 'down' and pendere 'to hang'.
items.cn: dependere 意为悬挂于、依附于，由 de-「向下」与 pendere「悬挂」构成。

items.en: Dependent entered English through French in the fifteenth century, meaning reliant on another for support.
items.cn: dependent 经法语在十五世纪进入英语，意为依靠他者供养。

items.en: Variare meant to change, from varius 'varied', and it gave the noun variable.
items.cn: variare 意为改变，出自 varius「杂色的」，由此产生名词 variable。

items.en: In the mathematics of functions, the input was called independent and the output dependent; the labels became standard in nineteenth-century algebra.
items.cn: 在函数数学中，输入被称为自变量，输出被称为因变量；这对标签在十九世纪代数中成为标准。

items.en: Laboratory and agricultural design in the later nineteenth and early twentieth centuries applied the pair to treatments and measured responses.
items.cn: 十九世纪后期至二十世纪初的实验室与农业设计，把这组词用到处理与测得反应上。

items.en: Regression, psychology and clinical trials each adopted the term for their own outcome, and the protocol fixed it in advance.
items.cn: 回归、心理学与临床试验各自采用这一术语指自己的结果，而试验方案会预先把它固定下来。

note.en: The first group shares one of the two words; the second group names the other factors of a design, with the differences spelled out.
note.cn: 第一组共享短语中的一个词；第二组是设计中的其他因素，并写明差别。

entries.definition: Reliant on something else; the adjective inside the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 依靠他物的；短语中的形容词。

entries.definition: The state of relying on another for support or value.
entries.definitionCN: 在供养或取值上依靠他者的状态。

entries.definition: A quantity that can take different values.
entries.definitionCN: 可取不同值的量。

entries.definition: To change; the verb behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 变化；名词背后的动词。

entries.definition: The factor that is deliberately changed, the cause side of the pair.
entries.definitionCN: 被刻意改变的因素，这一对中的原因一侧。

entries.definition: A factor held constant so it cannot explain the outcome; unlike the dependent variable, it is not measured as a result.
entries.definitionCN: 被保持恒定、因而无法解释结果的因子；与因变量不同，它不作为结果被测量。

entries.definition: The result itself, in ordinary language, without the statistical frame.
entries.definitionCN: 日常语言中的结果本身，不带统计框架。

entries.definition: What a system or subject does after a stimulus; the statistical word for the measured side.
entries.definitionCN: 系统或受试者在刺激之后的反应；统计中用来指被测的一侧。

entries.definition: The pre-declared measure of success in a trial, the clinical name for the dependent variable.
entries.definitionCN: 试验中预先声明的成功量度，是因变量的临床名称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the hanging root, the x-and-y image, and the fixed contrast with the independent variable.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「悬挂」词根、x 与 y 的意象，以及它与自变量的固定对照。

normal.en: Dependent is literally hanging from something: the measured outcome hangs on the factor that was changed.
normal.cn: dependent 字面是悬挂在某物上：被测结果挂在被改变的因素上。

normal.en: The family runs depend, dependent, dependence, variable, vary and variant.
normal.cn: 同族词有 depend、dependent、dependence、variable、vary 与 variant。

normal.en: In a graph the independent variable runs across and the dependent variable rises up the side.
normal.cn: 图上自变量横着走，因变量沿侧边上升。

normal.en: A trial declares its dependent variable, such as symptom-free days, before the first patient is enrolled.
normal.cn: 试验在第一位患者入组前就声明因变量，例如无症状天数。

normal.en: The pair is fixed: one factor is moved, the other is measured, and neither is held still.
normal.cn: 这一对是固定的：一个因素被移动，另一个被测量，两个都不被固定。

abstract.en: The dependent variable is the answer the experiment is allowed to give, and it must be chosen before the question is asked.
abstract.cn: 因变量是实验被允许给出的答案，而且必须在提问之前选好。

abstract.en: An outcome that nobody defined in advance can always be explained afterwards.
abstract.cn: 事先没有定义的结果，事后总能找到解释。

abstract.en: To depend is not weakness here; it is the mark of having been measured.
abstract.cn: 在这里，依赖不是软弱，而是「被测量过」的标志。

examples.en: The dependent variable was recorded at the same hour each day.
examples.cn: 因变量每天在同一时刻记录。

examples.en: A trial must state its dependent variable in the protocol.
examples.cn: 试验必须在方案中写明因变量。

examples.en: If the dependent variable is vague, the analysis cannot be repeated.
examples.cn: 如果因变量含糊，分析就无法重复。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「迪彭登特-维瑞额波」——挂在处理条件后面、等着被读出的那个结果：因变量

root: dependent 来自拉丁语 dependere「悬挂于」（de- 向下 + pendere 悬挂），经法语进入英语；variable 来自 variare「变化」。因变量与自变量成对，是十九世纪函数数学与实验设计的产物。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one measured outcome: the experimental response, the statistical response, the y of a function, a social outcome, a recorded behaviour, a trial endpoint, the left side of a regression, the vertical axis and an explained economic quantity.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一个被测量的结果：实验反应、统计响应、函数中的 y、社会结果、被记录的行为、试验终点、回归左侧、纵轴，以及被解释的经济量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a board holds a single column of readings, one row per treatment, and the last row is the result.
core.cn: 核心意象：记录板上只有一列读数，每种处理一行，最后一行就是结果。

branches.en: THE MEASURED OUTCOME: weekly height, or symptom-free days declared before a trial begins.
branches.cn: 被测结果：每周的株高，或试验开始前就声明的无症状天数。

branches.en: THE RESPONSE SIDE: the variation a model explains, the quantity on the left of a regression.
branches.cn: 响应一侧：模型所解释的变异，回归方程左边的量。

branches.en: THE Y: the output fixed once the input is chosen, and the quantity rising up the vertical axis.
branches.cn: 那个 y：输入选定后被固定的输出，以及沿纵轴上升的量。

branches.en: THE EXPLAINED FACT: graduation rates in social research, consumption responding to income.
branches.cn: 被解释的事实：社会研究中的毕业率，随收入变化的消费。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR: reaction time standing in for a mental process that cannot be seen.
branches.cn: 可见的行为：以反应时代表看不见的心理过程。

intro.en: The phrase pairs a Latin adjective of hanging with a Latin noun of change; the hyphen-free two-word unit is a modern technical name.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语「悬挂」形容词与「变化」名词配在一起；这个不带连字符的两词单位是现代技术名称。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is dependere, pendere, variare and varius, with -abilis in the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 dependere、pendere、variare 与 varius，名词中还有 -abilis。

items.example: The adjective describes a value that follows another.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述随另一量而定的值。

items.example: It marks the point from which something hangs.
items.exampleCN: 它标出悬挂的起点。

items.example: It also gives pendant and pendulum.
items.exampleCN: 它也是「吊坠」与「摆锤」两词的来源。

items.example: The verb joins physical hanging to logical reliance.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把物理悬挂与逻辑依赖连在一起。

items.example: The noun names a measurable quantity.
items.exampleCN: 名词指可测量的量。

items.example: The verb is the root of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的根。

items.example: It describes what is not uniform.
items.exampleCN: 它描述不齐一之物。

items.example: It builds the adjective that became the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成后来变作名词的形容词。

items.example: The pair splits moving from measuring.
items.exampleCN: 这一对把「移动」与「测量」分开。

items.example: The third term marks what must not move.
items.exampleCN: 第三个词标出不许变动的东西。

latinEntries.example: The compound gives English depend and dependent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个复合词给出英语 depend 与 dependent。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb pendere (pend-, pensum; to hang)
latinEntries.example: Latin pendere means to hang, and gives pendant and suspend.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 pendere 意为悬挂，并给出 pendant 与 suspend。

latinEntries.example: It is the verb behind variable and variation.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 variable 与 variation 背后的动词。

latinEntries.example: The adjective supplies the idea of changeability.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供「可变」这层意思。

latinEntries.example: It forms variabilis, the Latin adjective behind variable.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它构成 variabilis，即 variable 背后的拉丁形容词。

definition_zh: 使氧化；氧化（使某物与氧结合或失去电子）；生锈
definition_en: to make a substance combine with oxygen or lose electrons, or to undergo this change
core_image: 铁钉躺在漏雨的棚板下，几周后表面浮起一层橘红薄壳，用手一搓就掉粉
scene: 铁钉在潮湿的棚子里放了几周，表面起了一层橘红薄壳。 Damp air will oxidize the nails within weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 oxidize 指使金属与氧结合、表面生成氧化物（第 1 个义项：使与氧结合）；句意：潮湿空气会让这些钉子几周内氧化。图中可辨识物件：铁钉、锈壳、漏雨的棚顶、接雨的盆。

pos.zh: 使氧化；使与氧结合；使失去电子

derivatives.zh: 由 oxidize 加动作名词词尾构成，义为「氧化过程」
由 oxidize 加已然词尾构成，义为「已氧化的」
由 oxidize 加进行词尾构成，义为「有氧化能力的」
由 oxidize 加施动词尾构成，义为「氧化剂」

senses.title: Make a substance combine with oxygen
senses.definition: to cause a substance to combine with oxygen and form an oxide
senses.definitionCN: 使物质与氧结合并形成氧化物
senses.example: Damp air will oxidize the nails within weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 潮湿空气会让这些钉子几周内氧化。
senses.why: The verb is the working form of the oxygen-based name: an agent, or the air itself, brings the gas into combination.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是以氧命名的那个词的动作形式：某个作用者，或者空气本身，促使这种气体与物质结合。

senses.title: Strip electrons from something
senses.definition: to remove electrons from an atom, ion or molecule, raising its oxidation state
senses.definitionCN: 从原子、离子或分子中移走电子，使其氧化态升高
senses.example: The reagent oxidizes the alcohol to an aldehyde.
senses.exampleCN: 该试剂把醇氧化成醛。
senses.why: Once oxidation meant any loss of electrons, the verb took on the transitive reading of forcing that loss on something.
senses.whyCN: 当氧化泛指任何失电子之后，这个动词就带上「迫使某物失电子」的及物含义。

senses.title: Rust or tarnish on its own
senses.definition: to undergo slow surface corrosion in air, without a named agent
senses.definitionCN: 在空气中缓慢发生表面腐蚀，不点明作用者
senses.example: Silver oxidizes quickly in air that contains sulfur compounds.
senses.exampleCN: 银在含硫化合物的空气中很快氧化变暗。
senses.why: Everyday observation has no experimenter, only a metal and the weather, so the verb commonly appears without an agent.
senses.whyCN: 日常观察里没有实验者，只有金属与天气，因此这个动词常以不带作用者的形式出现。

senses.title: Food or drink turning stale
senses.definition: to spoil through contact with air, as fats, wine or cut fruit do
senses.definitionCN: 因接触空气而败坏，如脂肪、葡萄酒或切开的水果
senses.example: Left uncovered, the wine oxidizes and loses its freshness.
senses.exampleCN: 敞着不放，葡萄酒会氧化并失去新鲜感。
senses.why: The kitchen applies the verb to flavours rather than surfaces, but the cause is the same combination with oxygen.
senses.whyCN: 厨房把这个动词用在味道而不是表面，但成因仍是同一种与氧的结合。

senses.title: Break down fuel in the body
senses.definition: to convert fats, sugars or other nutrients into smaller units with the help of oxygen in cells
senses.definitionCN: 在细胞中借助氧把脂肪、糖等营养物转成更小单位
senses.example: Muscles oxidize glucose during long exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间运动时肌肉会氧化葡萄糖。
senses.why: Physiology treats the reaction as the body's way of extracting energy, so the verb can name what cells do to fuel.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把这一反应视为身体提取能量的方式，因此这个动词可以指细胞对燃料所做的事。

senses.title: Raise an element to a higher valence
senses.titleCN: 把元素氧化到更高价态
senses.definition: to convert an element into a compound in which it has a higher oxidation number
senses.definitionCN: 使某元素转成氧化数更高的化合物
senses.example: The process oxidizes sulfur dioxide into the trioxide.
senses.exampleCN: 该过程把二氧化硫氧化成三氧化硫。
senses.why: In chemical writing the verb marks a direction on the number scale rather than the visible decay of a surface.
senses.whyCN: 在化学写作里，这个动词标出数字尺度上的方向，而不是表面的可见衰败。

senses.title: Grow a protective oxide layer
senses.definition: to form a thin oxide film on a surface on purpose, so that further damage is slowed
senses.definitionCN: 有意在表面生成薄氧化膜，从而减缓进一步损坏
senses.example: Engineers oxidize the aluminium panel to harden its skin.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师对铝板作氧化处理，使其表层变硬。
senses.why: The same reaction is turned to advantage: the crust that ruins iron can, on another metal, seal the surface.
senses.whyCN: 同一反应被转为有利：毁掉铁的那层壳，换到另一种金属上却能封住表面。

senses.title: Bleach or deactivate by oxidation
senses.definition: to use oxidation to remove colour or to destroy an unwanted substance
senses.definitionCN: 利用氧化去除颜色或破坏不需要的物质
senses.example: The mill oxidizes the dye so that the cloth comes out pale.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂把染料氧化，使布匹变浅。
senses.why: Here the electron loss is valued for its side effect: colour and unwanted compounds are broken down rather than the metal being consumed.
senses.whyCN: 这里的失电子看重的是副作用：被拆掉的是颜色与不需要的化合物，而不是金属被消耗。

intro.en: Oxidize is built on oxide, itself from oxygen, the French scientific name of 1777; the verb's first date is approximate.
intro.cn: oxidize 由 oxide 派生，而 oxide 又出自 oxygen 这一 1777 年的法语科学命名；该动词的首见年代为约数。

items.en: The name of oxygen joins Greek oxys 'sharp, acid' with -genes 'producing', because Lavoisier believed the gas was required for acids.
items.cn: 氧的名称把希腊语 oxys「尖锐、酸」与 -genes「产生」合在一起，因为拉瓦锡相信酸的形成需要这种气体。

items.en: Lavoisier's new name spread through European science, and English adopted it at the end of the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 拉瓦锡的新名称在欧洲科学界传开，英语于 18 世纪末采用。

items.en: A compound of an element with oxygen was called an oxide, formed on the model of the new gas name with a chemical noun ending.
items.cn: 元素与氧形成的化合物被称为 oxide，是按新气体名称配上化学名词词尾构成的。

items.en: Oxidize was built directly on oxide with the ordinary verb ending that means 'to make or become', parallel to many other chemical verbs.
items.cn: oxidize 直接在 oxide 上加表示「使成为、变成」的普通动词词尾构成，与许多其他化学动词同型。

items.en: As chemistry, medicine and industry expanded, the verb was applied to metals, food, fuels, dyes and living tissue, and the noun oxidation followed the same range.
items.cn: 随着化学、医学与工业扩张，这个动词被用于金属、食物、燃料、染料与活组织，名词 oxidation 也覆盖同样的范围。

items.en: First date uncertain: the verb is recorded from the turn of the nineteenth century, but the earliest citations for the wider electron sense belong to later decades and are not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：该动词在 19 世纪之交已有记录，但更宽的失电子义的最早引文要晚数十年，具体年份并未精确固定。

note.en: The first group shares the oxygen stem and differs by word class; the second group holds the paired or neighbouring changes in the same reaction.
note.cn: 第一组共享由氧派生的词干而词类不同；第二组是同一反应中与之配对或相邻的变化。

entries.definition: The event itself; the verb names what an agent does, while the noun names what happens.
entries.definitionCN: 事件本身；动词命名作用者所做的事，名词命名所发生的事。

entries.definition: The compound left behind; it cannot take an object and describes no change in progress.
entries.definitionCN: 留下的化合物；它不能带宾语，也不描述进行中的变化。

entries.definition: A participle or adjective for matter that has already changed, not for the act of changing it.
entries.definitionCN: 表示已经变化的物质的分词或形容词，而不是使其变化的动作。

entries.definition: The substance that accepts electrons and drives the change; in everyday writing oxidizer is the more common twin.
entries.definitionCN: 接受电子并推动变化的物质；日常写作中更常见的是 oxidizer 这一同义形式。

entries.definition: To add electrons or lower an oxidation number; every oxidation is balanced by a reduction somewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 加上电子或降低氧化数；每一处氧化都在别处由还原平衡。

entries.definition: To wear a metal away by chemical action; it describes the damage rather than the electron transfer.
entries.definitionCN: 借化学作用磨损金属；它描述损坏，而非电子转移。

entries.definition: To dull or discolour a metal surface, especially silver; it is a visible result of oxidation, not its general name.
entries.definitionCN: 使金属表面失去光泽或变色，尤指银；它是氧化的可见结果，而非其通称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: oxide plus the verb ending: to turn something into an oxide.
normal.cn: oxide 加动词词尾：把某物变成氧化物。

normal.en: The family runs oxide, oxidize, oxidation, oxidized, oxidizing, oxidizer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 oxide、oxidize、oxidation、oxidized、oxidizing、oxidizer。

normal.en: Typical objects: oxidize a metal, oxidize fats, oxidize the surface.
normal.cn: 典型宾语：使金属氧化、使脂肪氧化、氧化表面。

normal.en: Air does it slowly, a reagent does it fast, a cell does it for energy.
normal.cn: 空气做得慢，试剂做得快，细胞则为了取能而做。

normal.en: The same verb can ruin a nail or protect an aluminium panel.
normal.cn: 同一个动词既能让钉子报废，也能保护铝板。

abstract.en: Picture a slice of apple browning on a plate before anyone touches it.
abstract.cn: 想象一片苹果摆在盘子里，没人碰就先变褐。

abstract.en: Picture a silver spoon going grey in the drawer where it is never used.
abstract.cn: 想象一把银勺在抽屉里久不使用，慢慢变灰。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed bottle that slowly loses its sparkle because air got in.
abstract.cn: 想象一瓶密封饮料因为进了空气，慢慢失去气泡感。

examples.en: Heat and light oxidize the pigment, so the sign fades.
examples.cn: 热与光会氧化颜料，于是标牌褪色。

examples.en: The alloy oxidizes more slowly than pure iron.
examples.cn: 这种合金比纯铁氧化得慢。

examples.en: Bacteria oxidize the sulfides in the sediment.
examples.cn: 细菌氧化沉积物中的硫化物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oxi（氧）+ dize（使）」——让氧上身，就是使氧化

root: 英语 oxide（出自 oxygen，1777 年法语科学命名，取自希腊语 oxys「尖锐、酸」+ -genes「产生」）+ 动词词尾。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one transfer of electrons: oxygen joins, charge leaves, a surface rusts, food spoils, cells burn fuel, an element climbs in valence, a protective film grows, and a dye is bleached away.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次电子转移：氧结合进来、电荷离开、表面生锈、食物变陈、细胞烧燃料、元素价态上升、保护膜生成、染料被漂掉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nail under a leaking roof, its bright skin turning into a soft orange powder.
core.cn: 核心意象：漏雨棚下的铁钉，亮皮变成松软的橘色粉末。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY READING: air alone makes a metal combine with oxygen, and the result is plain rust or tarnish.
branches.cn: 日常读法：仅靠空气就让金属与氧结合，结果就是直白的锈或暗斑。

branches.en: THE CHEMIST'S READING: electrons are pushed out and an element is driven to a higher valence.
branches.cn: 化学家的读法：电子被推走，某元素被推上更高的价态。

branches.en: THE KITCHEN COST: air attacks a flavour instead of a surface, and the change is tasted rather than seen.
branches.cn: 厨房的代价：空气攻击的是味道而非表面，变化靠尝而非靠看。

branches.en: THE ENERGY USE: cells oxidize fuel on purpose because the transfer releases power.
branches.cn: 能量的用法：细胞有意氧化燃料，因为这一转移能放出能量。

branches.en: THE INDUSTRIAL TWIST: the same reaction is made to seal a panel or to strip colour from cloth.
branches.cn: 工业的转折：同一反应被用来封住板材，或被用来剥去布上的颜色。

intro.en: Oxidize is a stem from the name of oxygen with a verb ending, and the family keeps that stem in every form.
intro.cn: oxidize 是以氧的名称作词干、再加动词词尾构成，整个词族在各种形式里都保留这个词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Greek and passed through French scientific naming; Latin supplies only the endings, so no Latin root relative is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词干源自希腊语并经法语科学命名传入；拉丁语只提供词尾，因此不列出该词根的拉丁同族词。

items.example: The opening element points to the acid-making claim.
items.exampleCN: 开头的成分指向「产酸」这一说法。

items.example: The suffix says the gas produces the quality named first.
items.exampleCN: 后缀说明这种气体产生前面所指的性质。

items.structure: oxygen stem plus a chemical noun ending
items.example: The oxide film dulls the metal.
items.exampleCN: 氧化膜使金属变暗。

items.example: The air oxidizes the nails.
items.exampleCN: 空气使钉子氧化。

items.structure: oxidize plus the action noun ending
items.example: Oxidation is faster in wet air.
items.exampleCN: 湿空气中氧化更快。

items.example: The oxidized surface no longer shines.
items.exampleCN: 已氧化的表面不再发亮。

items.example: Nitric acid is a strong oxidizing agent.
items.exampleCN: 硝酸是强氧化剂。

items.meaningCN: 使其他物质氧化的物质
items.example: The fuel needs an oxidizer to burn in space.
items.exampleCN: 燃料在太空燃烧需要氧化剂。

由 oxidize 加已然词尾构成，义为「已氧化的」
由 oxidize 加进行词尾构成，义为「有氧化能力的」

definition_zh: 敌对的；对立的；相互拮抗的；怀有敌意的
definition_en: showing active opposition or hostility, or acting against another force
core_image: 两个人从门框两侧同时推同一扇门，门轴被顶得吱呀作响
scene: 谈判开始前，双方代表都不肯先坐下，措辞里各自带着刺。 The two managers were openly antagonistic toward each other at the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 antagonistic 指人与人之间明显怀有敌意（第 1 个义项：敌视他人）；句意为两位经理在会上公然地互怀敌意。

senses.title: Hostile toward a person
senses.definition: openly hostile to a particular person or group
senses.definitionCN: 对某个特定的人或群体公然敌视
senses.example: His antagonistic remarks made cooperation impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 他带有敌意的话让合作无法进行。
senses.why: The Greek word began as a contest between two fighters; when it moves into a meeting room, the same two-sided opposition remains.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词最初指两名斗士之间的较量；进入会议室后，那种两边对峙的结构仍然保留。

senses.title: Two sides pushing apart
senses.definition: acting as one of two sides whose aims push in opposite directions
senses.definitionCN: 作为两个目标相反、彼此推开的一方
senses.example: The two committees held antagonistic views on the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 两个委员会对预算持对立看法。
senses.why: A contest needs two competitors facing each other; the adjective keeps that facing posture even when the struggle is verbal.
senses.whyCN: 较量需要两名参赛者正面相对；即使斗争只是言辞上的，这个形容词仍保留那种正面对峙的姿态。

senses.title: A muscle working in opposition
senses.definition: of a muscle, pulling in the direction opposite to another muscle at the same joint
senses.definitionCN: 指肌肉在同一关节上朝与另一块肌肉相反的方向拉动
senses.example: The biceps and triceps are antagonistic muscles.
senses.exampleCN: 肱二头肌与肱三头肌是拮抗肌。
senses.why: The body needs pairs of pullers: one bends the joint, the other straightens it, so opposition is a design feature rather than a fault.
senses.whyCN: 身体需要成对的牵引者：一块弯曲关节，另一块伸直关节，因此对立是设计特性而非缺陷。

senses.title: A substance acting against another
senses.definition: of a chemical or drug, counteracting or blocking the effect of another substance
senses.definitionCN: 指化学物质或药物抵消、阻断另一物质的作用
senses.example: The drug is antagonistic to the hormone it resembles.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药物与它所仿效的激素相互拮抗。
senses.why: A molecule can fit the same receptor without activating it, so it occupies the place and blocks the partner: opposition at the smallest scale.
senses.whyCN: 分子可以占据同一受体却不激活它，于是占住位置并挡住伙伴：这是最小尺度上的对立。

senses.title: Clashing interests
senses.definition: of interests or goals, competing in a way where one side's gain is the other's loss
senses.definitionCN: 指利益或目标相争，一方所得即另一方所失
senses.example: Labor and management were not always antagonistic.
senses.exampleCN: 劳资双方并非总是利益对立。
senses.why: When two groups want the same limited thing, their positions are drawn as arrows pointing away from each other.
senses.whyCN: 当两个群体想要同一件有限之物时，它们的立场就被画成两支彼此背离的箭头。

senses.title: A hostile manner
senses.definition: expressed in a sharp, provocative or uncooperative way
senses.definitionCN: 以尖刻、挑衅或不合作的方式表达
senses.example: She answered the question in an antagonistic tone.
senses.exampleCN: 她以敌对的语气回答了这个问题。
senses.why: Tone is the surface where the inner opposition becomes audible; the word can describe the manner as well as the relation.
senses.whyCN: 语气是内在对立变得可听见的表面；这个词既可描述关系，也可描述方式。

senses.title: Competing for one resource
senses.definition: of organisms, competing for the same limited resource in an ecosystem
senses.definitionCN: 指生物在生态系统中争夺同一有限资源
senses.example: The two species are antagonistic in their feeding habits.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个物种在取食习性上相互竞争。
senses.why: Ecology borrows the contest image: two populations drawing on one food supply behave like two rivals at one table.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用了较量意象：两个种群取用同一份食物，就像两个对手坐在同一张桌旁。

senses.title: A force against the hero
senses.definition: of a character or force in a story, standing in opposition to the protagonist
senses.definitionCN: 指故事中与主人公相对抗的人物或力量
senses.example: The novel sets an antagonistic brother against the hero.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说让一个敌对的兄弟与主人公对抗。
senses.why: Narrative needs resistance; the antagonist supplies the wall that the hero must move through.
senses.whyCN: 叙事需要阻力；反派提供那堵主人公必须穿过的墙。

intro.en: Antagonistic comes from the Greek word for a rival in a contest, built from 'against' and 'struggle'.
intro.cn: antagonistic 来自希腊语中表示「比赛对手」的词，由「反对」与「争斗」构成。

items.en: English formed antagonistic in the 17c. from antagonist, and by the 19c. it described opposed forces in politics, medicine and biology.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪由 antagonist 造出 antagonistic；到十九世纪，它已描述政治、医学与生物学中的对立力量。

items.en: Antagonistes meant 'a rival, an opponent in a contest', one who struggles against another.
items.cn: antagonistes 意为「对手、比赛中的竞争者」，即与另一人争斗的人。

items.en: The prefix anti- means 'against, in opposition to', as in antidote and antipathy.
items.cn: 前缀 anti- 意为「反对、对抗」，如 antidote 与 antipathy。

items.en: Agon meant 'contest, struggle', especially the athletic and dramatic contests of Greek festivals; it gives agony and agonize.
items.cn: agon 意为「竞赛、争斗」，尤指希腊节庆中的体育与戏剧比赛；它产生了 agony 与 agonize。

items.en: Medicine named opposing muscles and opposing drugs antagonistic, while ecology applied the word to species competing for one resource.
items.cn: 医学把相互对抗的肌肉与药物称为拮抗；生态学则用这个词指争夺同一资源的物种。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Greek contest root; the near-meaning group names forms of opposition.
note.cn: 形近组共享希腊语「竞赛」词根；近义组列出对立的各种形态。

entries.definition: a rival or opponent, especially the chief opponent in a story.
entries.definitionCN: 对手或敌手，尤指故事中的主要反对者。

entries.definition: active hostility or opposition between sides.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间积极的敌意或对立。

entries.definition: in a hostile or opposing manner.
entries.definitionCN: 以敌对或对立的方式。

entries.definition: to suffer intense struggle or worry, from the same Greek agon.
entries.definitionCN: 承受剧烈挣扎或焦虑，来自同一个希腊词 agon。

entries.definition: treating the other side as an opponent to be defeated.
entries.definitionCN: 把对方当作必须击败的对手。

entries.definition: unfriendly and ready to attack or oppose.
entries.definitionCN: 不友好并准备攻击或反对。

entries.definition: holding a position against something or someone.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事物或某人持反对立场。

entries.definition: hostile to something and likely to damage it.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事物怀有敌意并可能损害它。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the 'against' prefix and the picture of two people at one door.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想利用「反对」前缀和「两人同推一扇门」的画面。

normal.en: anti means against, agon means contest: an antagonistic person is against you in the contest.
normal.cn: anti 意为反对，agon 意为竞赛：antagonistic 的人就是在竞赛中站到你对面的人。

normal.en: Picture two hands on one door, one on each side, both pushing inward.
normal.cn: 想象两只手分别按在门的两侧，同时往里推。

normal.en: The -ist ending names the person, the -istic ending describes the attitude.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ist 命名那个人，词尾 -istic 描述那种态度。

normal.en: Link it with protagonist: the pro is for the hero, the ant is against.
normal.cn: 把它和 protagonist 联系：pro 站在主角一边，ant 站在对面。

normal.en: Say the middle syllable as 'tagon', like two tag teams facing off.
normal.cn: 把中间音节读成 tagon，像两支接力队正面对峙。

abstract.en: Opposition can be a design feature, as with muscles that pull both ways.
abstract.cn: 对立可以是设计特性，就像朝两个方向拉动的肌肉。

abstract.en: At molecular scale, blocking a receptor is the same contest in miniature.
abstract.cn: 在分子尺度上，占据受体就是同一场较量的缩小版。

abstract.en: A story needs a wall, and the antagonist is that wall.
abstract.cn: 故事需要一堵墙，反派就是那堵墙。

examples.en: His antagonistic remarks made cooperation impossible.
examples.cn: 他带有敌意的话让合作无法进行。

examples.en: The two departments have long been antagonistic.
examples.cn: 这两个部门长期以来相互对立。

examples.en: Antagonistic muscles work in pairs to move the joint.
examples.cn: 拮抗肌成对工作以带动关节。

dict_mnemonic.text: anti（反对）+ agon（竞赛）+ istic：在竞赛里站到对面，就是「敌对的」。

root: 希腊语 antagonistes（对手）：anti-（反对）+ agon（竞赛）

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep the same geometry, two forces facing each other; the differences lie in whether the forces are people, muscles, molecules, interests or story roles.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个几何结构，即两股力量正面相对；差别在于这两股力量是人、肌肉、分子、利益还是故事角色。

core.en: TWO FORCES FACING OFF
core.cn: 两股力量正面对峙

branches.en: People and groups that stand against one another.
branches.cn: 相互对立的人与群体。

branches.en: Bodies and molecules where blocking is a function, not a fault.
branches.cn: 身体与分子层面，其中阻断是功能而非缺陷。

branches.en: Interests that clash, and the tone that carries the clash.
branches.cn: 相互冲突的利益，以及承载冲突的语气。

branches.en: Species competing for one limited resource.
branches.cn: 争夺同一有限资源的物种。

branches.en: The story role that supplies resistance to the hero.
branches.cn: 为英雄提供阻力的故事角色。

intro.en: The word is a Greek prefix and root carried into English through a Latin-shaped adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语前缀与词根，经拉丁式形容词词尾进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Greek entries show the contest image that the modern word still carries.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的希腊语条目展示现代词中仍然携带的竞赛意象。

items.meaning: acting against another in a contest
items.example: Their goals were antagonistic.
items.exampleCN: 他们的目标相互对立。

items.example: The antagonist blocks the hero.
items.exampleCN: 反派阻挠主人公。

items.example: The meeting ended in open antagonism.
items.exampleCN: 会议在公开敌意中结束。

items.example: His joke antagonized the audience.
items.exampleCN: 他的玩笑惹恼了观众。

items.example: She agonized over the choice.
items.exampleCN: 她为这个选择痛苦挣扎。

items.example: The injury left him in agony.
items.exampleCN: 伤让他痛苦不堪。

items.example: Antipathy means strong dislike.
items.exampleCN: antipathy 意为强烈反感。

items.example: Artistic means showing artistic quality.
items.exampleCN: artistic 意为具有艺术品质。

definition_zh: 生物个体的；个体生物层面的；有机体层面的
definition_en: relating to an individual organism as a level of biological organization
core_image: 一只完整的甲虫被放在培养皿旁，旁边还有放大的细胞与整片森林，三张比例尺并排
scene: 这里指「生物个体的」。 Organismal biology asks how an entire animal survives, not just how its cells divide.
sceneCN: 这里 organismal 指「个体生物层面的」（第 2 个义项：以完整生物个体为研究层次）；句意：个体生物学研究的是整只动物如何存活，而不只是细胞如何分裂。图中可辨识物件：完整甲虫、细胞放大图、森林比例尺。

pos.zh: 生物个体的；个体生物层面的；有机体层面的（由 organism 加 -al 构成，多用于 organismal biology 等搭配）

collocations.zh: 个体生物学；生物体生物学

senses.title: Of the Individual
senses.titleCN: 生物个体的：以单个活体为单位
senses.definition: relating to an individual living thing
senses.definitionCN: 与单个活的个体有关的
senses.example: Organismal survival depends on finding enough water.
senses.exampleCN: 生物个体的存活取决于能否找到足够的水。
senses.why: Organism plus -al makes an adjective of the individual. The suffix adds no new idea; it simply attaches the noun to whatever is being described, such as survival or health.
senses.whyCN: organism 加 -al 构成「个体」的形容词。后缀并未增添新观念，只是把这个名词挂到所描述的对象上，例如 survival 或 health。

senses.title: The Whole-Animal Level
senses.titleCN: 个体层面的：整体生物这一层
senses.definition: at the level of the complete organism rather than a cell or molecule
senses.definitionCN: 处于完整生物体这一层，而不是细胞或分子层
senses.example: Organismal biology asks how an entire animal survives, not just how its cells divide.
senses.exampleCN: 个体生物学研究的是整只动物如何存活，而不只是细胞如何分裂。
senses.why: Biology is organized in levels: molecule, cell, tissue, organ, organism, population. The adjective names the rung of that ladder, which is why it appears so often in course titles.
senses.whyCN: 生物学按层次组织：分子、细胞、组织、器官、个体、种群。这个形容词命名的正是梯子上的这一级，因此常出现在课程名称里。

senses.title: A Branch of Biology
senses.titleCN: 学科分支的：个体生物学
senses.definition: belonging to the branch that studies whole organisms
senses.definitionCN: 属于研究完整生物体的分支
senses.example: She teaches organismal biology to first-year students.
senses.exampleCN: 她给一年级学生讲授个体生物学。
senses.why: Once the level has a name, it can become a field. Organismal biology sits between molecular biology below and ecology above, and borrows methods from both.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某个层次有了名字，它就能变成领域。个体生物学位于下方的分子生物学与上方的生态学之间，并借用两者的方法。

senses.title: The Unit of Ecology
senses.definition: treating a single living thing as the unit of study or count
senses.definitionCN: 把单个活物当作研究或计数的单位
senses.example: Organismal patterns of dispersal shape the whole meadow.
senses.exampleCN: 个体层面的扩散格局塑造了整片草甸。
senses.why: Ecology moves between individuals and populations. The adjective marks the lower end of that scale, where a single life still counts as one.
senses.whyCN: 生态学在个体与种群之间移动；这个形容词标出该尺度的下端，在那里一条生命仍算作一个单位。

senses.title: Developmental Whole
senses.titleCN: 个体发育的：从合子到成体
senses.definition: relating to the development of a whole organism from a single cell
senses.definitionCN: 与整个生物体从单个细胞发育而来有关
senses.example: Organismal development begins with one fertilized cell.
senses.exampleCN: 个体发育始于一个受精细胞。
senses.why: Development turns one cell into an integrated body. The adjective distinguishes that journey from the molecular events that accompany it.
senses.whyCN: 发育把一个细胞变成一个整合的身体；这个形容词把这段旅程与伴随其发生的分子事件区分开来。

senses.title: Whole-Body Response
senses.titleCN: 整体反应的：全身一起应答
senses.definition: belonging to the response of the whole body rather than one organ
senses.definitionCN: 属于全身而非单个器官的反应
senses.example: The organismal response to cold includes shivering and reduced blood flow.
senses.exampleCN: 对寒冷的整体反应包括发抖与血流减少。
senses.why: An organ can react alone, but many reactions only make sense across the whole body. The adjective gathers those scattered events into one subject.
senses.whyCN: 器官可以单独反应，但许多反应只有放在全身才说得通；这个形容词把这些分散的事件收拢成一个主体。

senses.title: Trait of the Whole
senses.titleCN: 个体性状的：属于整体的特征
senses.definition: describing a trait that belongs to the whole organism
senses.definitionCN: 指属于整个生物体的性状
senses.example: Body size is an organismal trait; enzyme speed is not.
senses.exampleCN: 体型是个体性状，酶的反应速度则不是。
senses.why: Some traits exist only at the whole-body level. The adjective sorts them from traits that belong to tissues or molecules, which matters in comparing species.
senses.whyCN: 有些性状只存在于全身层面；这个形容词把它们与属于组织或分子的性状分开，这在物种比较中很重要。

senses.title: Philosophical Individualism
senses.titleCN: 个体主义的：以个体为解释起点
senses.definition: explaining biological facts primarily through the individual organism
senses.definitionCN: 主要通过生物个体来解释生物学事实
senses.example: An organismal view of selection begins with the fate of individuals.
senses.exampleCN: 以个体为起点的选择观，从个体的命运出发。
senses.why: The adjective can mark a stance in theory: start from the individual, not the gene or the group. It is a level choice that carries consequences for how selection is described.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可以标出一种理论立场：从个体出发，而不是从基因或群体出发。这是一种层次选择，会影响到如何描述选择。

intro.en: Organismal is organism plus -al. Organism itself is a nineteenth-century formation on Greek organon 'tool, instrument'. The adjective is a later, chiefly scientific coinage whose exact first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: organismal 是 organism 加 -al。organism 本身是十九世纪建立在希腊 organon「工具、器具」之上的构词。该形容词是更晚的、主要用于科学的造词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Organon meant 'tool, instrument', and by extension a body organ, since an organ is the instrument of a function. The word supplied Latin organum.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具」，引申指身体器官，因为器官是完成某项功能的工具；该词给出拉丁 organum。

items.en: Organism was coined to name a living body as an organized whole. The exact coiner is uncertain; the word spread with the rise of biology as a discipline.
items.cn: organism 被造出来，用来指作为有组织整体的活体。确切的造词者不确定；该词随生物学成为一门学科而传播。

items.en: Twentieth-century biology formalized levels from molecule to biosphere. Adjectives such as cellular, organismal and ecological were created to name each rung.
items.cn: 二十世纪生物学把从分子到生物圈的层次正式化；cellular、organismal、ecological 这类形容词被造出来，为每一级命名。

items.en: Organismal appears mainly in scientific writing from the twentieth century, above all in organismal biology. Its first citation is not firmly dated.
items.cn: organismal 主要出现在二十世纪的科学写作中，尤其是 organismal biology；其首见书证没有可靠年代。

items.en: English developed two adjectives. Organismal marks the level of the individual; organismic marks the philosophical claim that the whole organizes its parts. The division became standard in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 英语发展出两个形容词：organismal 标出个体这一层次；organismic 标出「整体组织其部分」的哲学主张。这一分工在二十世纪成为标准。

note.en: The first group separates the two adjectives built on organism, which are close but not interchangeable. The second holds near-synonyms that name different levels.
note.cn: 第一组区分建立在 organism 上的两个形容词，它们相近但不可互换；第二组是命名不同层次的近义词。

entries.definition: Marks the view or study that treats the whole as organizing its parts. It is about holism, while organismal is about the level of the individual.
entries.definitionCN: 标出把整体视为组织其部分的那种观点或研究；它讲的是整体论，而 organismal 讲的是个体这一层次。

entries.definition: Means 'of living things' or 'grown without chemicals'. It describes a property and never names a level of organization.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「生物的」或「不用化学方式种植的」；描述性质，从不命名组织层次。

entries.definition: The living individual itself. The adjective attaches to it, so the two cannot occupy the same grammatical slot.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指活的个体本身；形容词依附于它，因此两者不能占据同一语法位置。

entries.definition: Relating to the entire body. It is the everyday version of the medical and physiological uses of organismal.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个身体有关的；是 organismal 在医学与生理学用法中的日常说法。

entries.definition: Relating to a single entity as distinct from a group. It is broader, since individuals need not be alive.
entries.definitionCN: 与单个实体有关，区别于群体；更宽泛，因为个体不必是活物。

entries.definition: Relating to cells. It is the neighbouring rung below organismal on the ladder of biological organization.
entries.definitionCN: 与细胞有关的；在生物组织层次的梯子上，是 organismal 下面相邻的一级。

entries.definition: Relating to populations and environments. It is the neighbouring rung above organismal.
entries.definitionCN: 与种群和环境有关的；是 organismal 上面相邻的一级。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: organism + -al: the adjective of the individual living thing.
normal.cn: organism + -al：活的个体这一名词的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs organism, organismal, organismic, organic, organ, organelle.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 organism、organismal、organismic、organic、organ、organelle。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the level: organismal biology, organismal level, organismal development, organismal ecology.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出层次：个体生物学、个体层面、个体发育、个体生态学。

normal.en: The ladder runs molecule, cell, tissue, organ, organismal, ecological, biosphere.
normal.cn: 梯子依次是：分子、细胞、组织、器官、个体、生态、生物圈。

normal.en: organismal is a level word; organismic is a holism word.
normal.cn: organismal 是层次词，organismic 是整体论词。

abstract.en: Picture three photographs side by side: a cell, a whole beetle, and the meadow it lives in.
abstract.cn: 想象三张照片并排：一个细胞、一只完整的甲虫，以及它所在的草甸。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder where each rung is studied by a different department.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，每一级都由不同的系所研究。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor asking how the patient feels, not only what one organ shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一位医生询问病人整体感受，而不只看某个器官的指标。

examples.en: Organismal biology bridges molecular detail and ecological pattern.
examples.cn: 个体生物学连接分子细节与生态格局。

examples.en: The study measured organismal, not cellular, responses to heat.
examples.cn: 该研究测量的是整体层面对热的反应，而非细胞层面。

examples.en: Organismal traits such as body size evolve slowly.
examples.cn: 体型这类个体性状演化得很慢。

dict_mnemonic.text: organism（生物）+ al（……的）→ 生物个体的、个体层面的

root: 希腊 organon「工具、器官」→ 拉丁 organum → 英语 organism（十九世纪）→ organismal。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all locate a subject at the level of the individual living thing: its survival, its biological level, its branch of study, its ecological unit, its development, its whole-body response, its traits and its explanatory stance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把对象定位在「单个活物」这一层：它的存活、它在生物学中的层次、相关学科分支、生态单位、发育过程、整体反应、个体性状与解释立场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cell, a whole beetle and a meadow shown at three different scales.
core.cn: 核心意象：细胞、完整甲虫与草甸，以三种不同比例尺并排呈现。

branches.en: THE INDIVIDUAL AND ITS BODY: survival and whole-body responses belong to one living thing.
branches.cn: 个体及其身体：存活与整体反应都属于同一个活物。

branches.en: THE LEVEL AND THE FIELD: a rung on the biological ladder becomes a named branch and a course.
branches.cn: 层次与领域：生物学梯子上的一级变成具名分支与课程。

branches.en: THE ECOLOGICAL UNIT: a single life counted as one within a population.
branches.cn: 生态单位：在种群中，一条生命算作一个。

branches.en: DEVELOPMENT AND TRAITS: one cell becomes a body, and some traits exist only at that level.
branches.cn: 发育与性状：一个细胞变成一个身体，而有些性状只存在于这一层次。

branches.en: THE EXPLANATORY STANCE: begin with individuals rather than with genes or groups.
branches.cn: 解释立场：从个体出发，而不是从基因或群体出发。

intro.en: Organismal is a noun of organized life with the adjective suffix -al: an instrument-root, a suffix of state, and a suffix of belonging.
intro.cn: organismal 是「有组织的生命」名词加形容词后缀 -al：器具词根、状态后缀与归属后缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon, Latin organum, English organism and organismal form one line. The same root gives organ, organic, organize, organization and organelle.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon、拉丁 organum、英语 organism 与 organismal 构成一条线索；同一词根给出 organ、organic、organize、organization、organelle。

items.example: Organismal heat tolerance varies with body size.
items.exampleCN: 个体耐热性随体型而变。

items.example: The organism lives in the leaf litter.
items.exampleCN: 该生物生活在落叶层中。

items.meaning: of the whole as organizing parts
items.example: Organismic theory treats the whole as primary.
items.exampleCN: 有机体论把整体视为首要。

items.example: Organic remains were found in the clay.
items.exampleCN: 黏土中发现了生物遗骸。

items.example: The gill is a respiratory organ.
items.exampleCN: 鳃是呼吸器官。

items.meaningCN: 细胞内的小型功能结构
items.example: Mitochondria are organelles.
items.exampleCN: 线粒体是细胞器。

items.meaning: to arrange into a working whole
items.example: Cells organize into tissues.
items.exampleCN: 细胞组织成组织。

items.example: The organization of the colony follows a strict order.
items.exampleCN: 该群体的组织遵循严格的秩序。

definition_zh: 冷淡的；疏远的；超然离群的（副词：远离地；冷淡地）
definition_en: not friendly or forthcoming; distant and cool, or at a distance
core_image: 船头迎风站开、不靠人群的那个人
scene: 聚会上众人围坐说笑，他却站在窗边。 She remained aloof from the gossip.
sceneCN: 这里的 aloof 是「疏远的、超然的」（第 1 个义项：有意保持距离的冷淡）；句意是她对那些闲话保持超然。

derivatives.zh: 由 aloof 加 -ness 构成，义为「冷淡；超然」
同源航海词，义为「船头」的旧称

senses.title: Cool and distant in manner
senses.definition: physically or emotionally distant in dealing with others
senses.definitionCN: 待人接物时保持身体或情感上的距离
senses.example: The new manager seemed aloof at first.
senses.exampleCN: 新经理起初显得很冷淡。
senses.why: From sailors keeping "to windward", apart; distance became coldness.
senses.whyCN: 源于水手「迎风在上风处」避开；距离引申为冷淡。

senses.title: Uninvolved in a matter
senses.definition: deliberately not taking part or taking sides
senses.definitionCN: 有意不参与、不站队
senses.example: He kept aloof from office politics.
senses.exampleCN: 他对办公室政治置身事外。
senses.why: Standing apart in space maps onto standing apart in affairs.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的站开映射到事务上的不沾手。

senses.title: Reserved out of shyness
senses.definition: withholding oneself because of shyness rather than contempt
senses.definitionCN: 因羞怯而非轻蔑而退缩不前
senses.example: Aloof in crowds, she opened up one on one.
senses.exampleCN: 她在人群中拘谨，一对一却很健谈。
senses.why: The same distance can spring from fear of exposure, not pride.
senses.whyCN: 同样的距离感可以源于怕暴露，而非傲慢。

senses.title: Superior and disdainful
senses.definition: distancing oneself from others as if beneath one's notice
senses.definitionCN: 视他人不值得注意而与之保持距离
senses.example: The professor was aloof toward undergraduates.
senses.exampleCN: 教授对本科生态度高傲。
senses.why: Distance read upward becomes disdain.
senses.whyCN: 距离一旦向上解读就成了轻蔑。

senses.title: Objectively detached, positively
senses.definition: neutrally detached in judgment, free of bias or faction
senses.definitionCN: 判断上中立超然，不受派系或偏见影响
senses.example: A referee must stay aloof from the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判必须不为观众所动。
senses.why: Distance can be a virtue: the judge above the fray.
senses.whyCN: 距离也可以是美德：裁判立于纷争之上。

senses.title: Standing at a physical distance
senses.definition: as an adverb, standing or kept apart in space
senses.definitionCN: 作副词，指在空间上站开或保持距离
senses.example: The sentry called, "Stand aloof!"
senses.exampleCN: 哨兵喝道：「站开！」
senses.why: This is the original nautical sense before the emotional one.
senses.whyCN: 这是情感义之前的原始航海义。

senses.title: Guarded and unrevealing
senses.definition: guarded in speech, revealing little of oneself
senses.definitionCN: 言语谨慎，很少袒露自我
senses.example: He stayed aloof about his past.
senses.exampleCN: 他对自己的过去讳莫如深。
senses.why: Withholding words is a form of keeping distance.
senses.whyCN: 不吐露言语是保持距离的一种形式。

senses.title: Detached by temperament
senses.definition: having a naturally solitary, unsociable temperament
senses.definitionCN: 天性孤僻、不合群
senses.example: Cats are famously aloof.
senses.exampleCN: 猫以孤高著称。
senses.why: When distance becomes a character trait, the word describes nature, not mood.
senses.whyCN: 当距离成为性格，词就描述本性而非一时情绪。

intro.en: Aloof comes from the nautical phrase a-luff, "to windward", where a ship's head keeps clear.
intro.cn: aloof 源自航海短语 a-luff「迎风向上风处」，指船头保持清距。

items.en: lof or looch, "windward", the nautical term.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 lof/looch「上风」，航海术语。

items.en: a loof, "to windward", used in sailing orders.
items.cn: 中古英语 a loof「向上风」，用于操船口令。

items.en: aloof as adverb, "at a distance, apart".
items.cn: 十六世纪 aloof 作副词「隔开、远离」。

items.en: The emotional sense "distant in manner" develops.
items.cn: 十七世纪发展出「态度疏远」的情感义。

items.en: Used by major writers for proud or shy detachment.
items.cn: 被重要作家用于写骄傲或羞怯的疏离。

items.en: Chiefly adjectival today; the adverb use is older-fashioned.
items.cn: 如今以形容词为主，副词用法较旧。

note.en: Aloof is distinct from aloft by one letter, and near in meaning to distant and reserved.
note.cn: aloof 与 aloft 仅差一个字母，意义上与 distant、reserved 相近。

entries.definition: up in the air; one letter apart, related nautical history but opposite direction.
entries.definitionCN: 在高处；仅差一字母，同有航海渊源但方向相反。

entries.definition: the Dutch nautical source of aloof.
entries.definitionCN: 荷兰语航海来源词。

entries.definition: an animal's foot; rhymes only.
entries.definitionCN: 蹄；仅押韵。

entries.definition: not intimate; broader, covering space and manner.
entries.definitionCN: 不亲近的；兼指空间与态度，更宽泛。

entries.definition: slow to show feelings; less cold than aloof.
entries.definitionCN: 不外露感情的；比 aloof 少冷意。

entries.definition: emotionally uninvolved, often neutrally.
entries.definitionCN: 情感上不介入的，常为中性。

normalIntro.en: Anchor aloof in the ship that keeps clear.
normalIntro.cn: 把 aloof 锚定在保持清距的船上。

normal.en: a + loof "to windward": a ship holding off, staying clear.
normal.cn: a + loof「上风」：船保持距离、不靠近。

normal.en: aloof vs aloft: up the mast is aloft; away from the crowd is aloof.
normal.cn: aloof 与 aloft：爬上桅杆是 aloft，避开人群是 aloof。

normal.en: Noun: aloofness; phrases: keep/stand/remain aloof from.
normal.cn: 名词 aloofness；短语 keep/stand/remain aloof from。

normal.en: Adjective or adverb: an aloof manner / stand aloof.
normal.cn: 可作形容词或副词：an aloof manner / stand aloof。

normal.en: Tone watch: aloof can blame (cold) or praise (impartial).
normal.cn: 语气注意：aloof 可贬（冷漠）可褒（超然）。

abstract.cn: 一把椅子被拉离人群一臂之遥。

abstract.en: A cat watching the party from the top of the bookshelf.
abstract.cn: 猫在书架顶上看派对。

abstract.en: A ship holding its bow into the wind, keeping a gap of gray water.
abstract.cn: 船顶着风，与人群隔开一线灰色的海。

examples.en: She stayed aloof during the quarrel.
examples.cn: 争吵期间她保持超然。

examples.en: His aloof manner hid deep shyness.
examples.cn: 他冷淡的举止掩盖了深深的羞怯。

examples.en: The judge kept aloof from the media frenzy.
examples.cn: 法官与媒体的狂热保持距离。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿路夫」——阿婆站在路口夫人们之外，隔着三步看热闹，冷冷的不搭腔。

definition_zh: 城市规划；城市总体规划；土地利用规划；交通与基础设施规划；城市空间设计

scene: 会议桌上摊开一张街区图，红线标出将来的轻轨，绿色块留给公园。 City planning decides where the rail line will cut through the old quarter.
