plan + -ed（过去分词作定语）→ 偏移为「按计划建成的」
un-（否定前缀）+ planned → 偏移为「未经规划的」
city + -scape（景观后缀，仿 landscape）→ 偏移为「城市景观整体」
zone + -ing（动名词后缀）→ 偏移为「按用途划分土地的制度」

senses.title: The profession
senses.titleCN: 城市规划这一专业与学科
senses.definition: the profession and academic field that studies how cities should be laid out
senses.definitionCN: 研究城市应如何布局的专业与学科
senses.example: City planning grew out of public health surveys of overcrowded housing.
senses.exampleCN: 城市规划是从对拥挤住房的公共卫生调查中生长出来的。
senses.why: planning names the activity of arranging in advance, and city names its object, so the phrase is the profession of arranging cities.
senses.whyCN: planning 指预先安排的活动，city 指其对象，因此这个短语就是安排城市的专业。

senses.title: A master plan
senses.definition: the single long-range document that sets a city's intended shape for decades
senses.definitionCN: 为城市数十年形态定下意图的长远文件
senses.example: The master plan of city planning reserved a green belt in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 城市规划的总体方案在北部保留了一条绿带。
senses.why: a profession needs one binding document, and the phrase shifts from the activity to that document.
senses.whyCN: 一个专业需要一份有约束力的文件，于是这个短语从活动转指那份文件。

senses.title: Land-use planning
senses.definition: the allocation of parcels to housing, industry, farming or open space
senses.definitionCN: 把地块分配给住房、工业、农业或空地
senses.example: City planning decides which fields may become factories.
senses.exampleCN: 城市规划决定了哪些田地可以变成工厂。
senses.why: land is the scarce thing a city allocates, so use-allocation is the core of the craft.
senses.whyCN: 土地是城市分配中最稀缺的东西，所以用途分配就成了这门行当的核心。

senses.title: Transport and infrastructure planning
senses.definition: the routing of roads, rail, water and power before they are built
senses.definitionCN: 在建造之前安排道路、铁路、供水与电力的走向
senses.example: City planning decides where the rail line will cut through the old quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 城市规划决定了轻轨将怎样穿过老城区。
senses.why: networks last longer than buildings, so their routes are fixed first and constrain everything after.
senses.whyCN: 管网比建筑存续更久，所以它们的走向先被定下，并约束其后的一切。

senses.title: Urban design and layout
senses.definition: the shaping of streets, blocks and public space at the scale of the neighbourhood
senses.definitionCN: 以街区尺度塑造街道、地块与公共空间
senses.example: Good city planning makes a square that people actually cross.
senses.exampleCN: 好的城市规划会做出人们真的愿意穿过的广场。
senses.why: planning at drawing scale becomes design, where dimensions and frontages decide how a place feels.
senses.whyCN: 规划落到图纸尺度就成了设计，尺寸与临街面决定一个地方给人的感受。

senses.title: Neighbourhood planning
senses.definition: planning carried out at the level of a district with resident participation
senses.definitionCN: 在有居民参与的区级层面进行的规划
senses.example: City planning at this level begins with the school run.
senses.exampleCN: 这一层面的城市规划从送孩子上学的那条路开始。
senses.why: national and city-wide rules must be applied somewhere, and that somewhere is a neighbourhood.
senses.whyCN: 全国与全市的规则总要落到某个具体地方，而那个地方就是街区。

senses.title: Rules and regulation
senses.definition: the ordinances, permits and zoning rules that give plans legal force
senses.definitionCN: 赋予规划法律效力的条例、许可与分区规则
senses.example: City planning without enforcement is only a drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 没有执行的规划只是一张图。
senses.why: a plan changes nothing until it is written into law, so the phrase covers the rule-making as well.
senses.whyCN: 规划不写进法律就什么都改变不了，因此这个短语也涵盖规则的制定。

senses.title: Planning for renewal
senses.definition: the replanning of districts that are already built, often with relocation involved
senses.definitionCN: 对已建成城区重新规划，常涉及搬迁
senses.example: City planning here means deciding who must move before the blocks come down.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的城市规划意味着在街区被拆掉之前决定谁必须搬走。
senses.why: when there is no new land, planning becomes a negotiation over existing space and existing residents.
senses.whyCN: 没有新土地时，规划就变成围绕既有空间与既有居民的协商。

intro.en: City planning joins city, from Latin civitas, to planning, from plan, whose Latin source is planum 'flat surface'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: city planning 把来自拉丁 civitas 的 city 与来自 plan 的 planning 组合起来，而 plan 的拉丁来源是 planum「平面」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Civitas named a citizen-body and its town; city entered English through French cité.
items.cn: civitas 指公民共同体及其城镇；city 经法语 cité 进入英语。

items.en: Planum meant 'a flat surface', from planus 'flat, level'. A plan was first a drawing on a flat sheet.
items.cn: planum 意为「平面」，来自 planus「平的、平坦的」。plan 最初指画在平面纸上的一张图。

items.en: French plan carried both the drawing and the scheme senses into English.
items.cn: 法语 plan 把「图」与「方案」两层意思一并带入英语。

items.en: City planning emerged as a named activity when industrial cities began to be laid out with sewers, parks and bylaws.
items.cn: 当工业城市开始被按排水、公园与附例来布局时，city planning 才作为一项有名字的活动出现。

items.en: In the twentieth century the phrase named a licensed profession and a municipal department, not only a drawing.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个短语指一门有执照的专业与一个市政部门，而不只是一张图。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first use of the phrase is unrecorded, and the deeper origin of planus is unsettled, so any earlier form proposed is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个短语的确切首见没有记录，planus 的更早来源亦无定论，因此提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates the phrase from its near-synonyms and from the documents it produces; group two holds the practices it overlaps with.
note.cn: 第一组把这一短语与近义说法以及它产出的文件分开；第二组是与之重叠的实践。

entries.definition: The commoner term for the same profession; it is wider because it covers regions as well as cities.
entries.definitionCN: 同一专业更常见的说法；它更宽，因为同时涵盖区域与城市。

entries.definition: The document or drawing produced; planning is the activity, a plan is its output.
entries.definitionCN: 所产出的文件或图纸；规划是活动，方案是产出。

entries.definition: The long-range framework document; it is one product of city planning, not the whole field.
entries.definitionCN: 长远的框架文件；它是城市规划的一项产出，而非整个领域。

entries.definition: The division of land into use districts; zoning is a tool that planning uses, not its equal.
entries.definitionCN: 把土地划为用途分区；分区是规划所用的一种工具，并不等同于规划。

entries.definition: The design of buildings, streets and spaces as a coherent whole; it is the three-dimensional side of planning.
entries.definitionCN: 把建筑、街道与空间作为整体来设计；它是规划的三维一面。

entries.definition: The allocation of land to uses; it is a core branch of city planning rather than a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 把土地分配给各类用途；它是城市规划的核心分支，而非同义词。

entries.definition: Rebuilding land that was already built on; it follows a plan and is not the planning itself.
entries.definitionCN: 对已建成土地的再建；它依规划而行，本身不是规划。

entries.definition: The routing of roads, water and power; it is one specialized branch of the wider field.
entries.definitionCN: 安排道路、供水与电力的走向；它是更宽领域中的一个专门分支。

entries.definition: A settled course of action adopted by an authority; planning produces policy but also responds to it.
entries.definitionCN: 权威采纳的既定行动方向；规划既产出政策，也受政策约束。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real halves, the Latin source of plan and the real instruments.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的部分、plan 的拉丁来源与真实工具名称。

normal.en: planum 'flat surface' gives plan: a scheme is first a drawing on a flat sheet.
normal.cn: planum「平面」给出 plan：方案最初是画在平面纸上的一张图。

normal.en: The family runs plan, planner, planning, planned, unplanned, zoning, cityscape.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 plan、planner、planning、planned、unplanned、zoning、cityscape。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the office: city planning department, city planning policy, city planning map.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出机构：城市规划部门、城市规划政策、城市规划图。

normal.en: The commoner synonym is urban planning, which also covers regional scales.
normal.cn: 更常见的同义说法是 urban planning，它还覆盖区域尺度。

normal.en: A plan without enforcement is only a drawing: policy turns it into law.
normal.cn: 没有执行的方案只是一张图：政策把它变成法律。

abstract.en: Picture a red line drawn across a map years before anyone digs the trench.
abstract.cn: 想象一条红线在地图上画下多年之后，才有人去挖那条沟。

abstract.en: Picture a green square that forbids a building that has not yet been imagined.
abstract.cn: 想象一个绿色方块，禁止了一栋尚未被想象出来的建筑。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting where the school run is used as evidence about a road.
abstract.cn: 想象一场会议，把送孩子上学的路线当作关于一条路的证据。

examples.en: City planning failed where the new blocks had no school.
examples.cn: 新区没有配学校的地方，城市规划失败了。

examples.en: The city planning office publishes its maps online.
examples.cn: 城市规划办公室把图纸公布在网上。

examples.en: City planning must consider drainage before it draws the streets.
examples.cn: 城市规划必须先考虑排水，再画街道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「city（城市）+ planning（预先安排）」——给城市事先画好图、定好规矩 → 城市规划

root: city（拉丁 civitas「公民共同体」）+ planning（plan 来自拉丁 planum「平面」，planus「平的」）；短语在十九世纪工业城市布局中成为专门说法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: someone arranges a city in advance, and that act appears as a profession, a master document, land allocation, transport routes, three-dimensional design, neighbourhood work, legal rules and replanning of what already stands.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：有人事先安排城市，这个动作依次表现为专业、总体文件、土地分配、交通走向、三维设计、街区工作、法律规则，以及对已建成之物的重新规划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn on paper that will later become a trench, a wall or a park.
core.cn: 核心意象：画在纸上的一条线，日后会变成沟、墙或公园。

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS DOCUMENT: a profession of arranging, and the one long-range plan it produces.
branches.cn: 动作与文件：一门安排的专业，以及它产出的那份长远方案。

branches.en: WHO GETS WHICH LAND: the allocation of parcels is the core decision of the craft.
branches.cn: 谁得到哪块地：地块分配是这门手艺的核心决定。

branches.en: ROUTES FIXED FIRST: transport and utility lines outlast buildings and constrain everything after.
branches.cn: 先定走向：交通与管线比建筑活得久，并约束后来的一切。

branches.en: FROM DRAWING TO FEELING: dimensions and frontages decide how a place feels, and residents meet the plan at street level.
branches.cn: 从图纸到感受：尺寸与临街面决定一个地方的感受，而居民在街道层面遇见规划。

branches.en: FORCE AND REVISION: rules give the plan legal force, and renewal applies them to ground already occupied.
branches.cn: 效力与修订：规则赋予方案法律效力，更新则把它们用于已被人占用的地面。

intro.en: City planning is two words, each with its own productive endings and compounds.
intro.cn: city planning 是两个词，各自带有高产词尾与复合形式。

latinIntro.en: Both halves trace to Latin: civitas for city and planum for plan, the latter from planus 'flat'.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都可上溯拉丁语：city 出自 civitas，plan 出自 planum，后者来自 planus「平的」。

items.example: The word names the political town.
items.exampleCN: 这个词命名的是政治意义上的城镇。

items.meaning: a wide view of a kind
items.example: Cityscape names the city as a view.
items.exampleCN: cityscape 把城市指为一种景观。

items.example: The word began as a surface, not a scheme.
items.exampleCN: 这个词最初指一个表面，而不是方案。

items.example: The adjective described ground easy to draw on.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述易于绘图的地面。

items.example: The plan fits on one sheet.
items.exampleCN: 这张方案能放在一张纸上。

items.example: The planner walks the site first.
items.exampleCN: 规划师先走一遍场地。

items.example: Planning is the activity, a plan is the output.
items.exampleCN: 规划是活动，方案是产出。

items.example: A planned district has services in place.
items.exampleCN: 规划过的城区已把设施安排好。

items.example: Unplanned growth outruns the drains.
items.exampleCN: 未经规划的增长跑得比排水快。

items.example: Zoning divides the map into belts of use.
items.exampleCN: 分区把地图切成用途带。

latinEntries.structure: zona, zonae (f., first declension, Greek loanword)

definition_zh: 商人；交易员；从事某类货物买卖的人
definition_en: a person or firm that buys and sells goods, currencies or securities as a business
core_image: 交易大厅里一个人盯着屏幕上的报价，桌上的电话响个不停，手边摊着几张成交单
scene: 交易大厅里，一个人盯着屏幕上的报价，手边的电话一直响。 A currency trader watches the rate move before placing an order.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「以买卖为业的人」（第 1 个义项：从事买卖的人）；句意为一名外汇交易员在下单之前盯着汇率变动。图中可辨识物件：报价屏幕、电话、成交单、座椅。

pos.zh: 商人；交易员；（某类货物的）买卖者

senses.title: A person who buys and sells as a business
senses.definition: someone whose living comes from buying goods and selling them on
senses.definitionCN: 靠买进货物再卖出谋生的人
senses.example: The grain trader buys from farms and sells to mills.
senses.exampleCN: 粮商从农场买进，再卖给磨坊。
senses.why: Trade names the activity, and the ending names the one who performs it.
senses.whyCN: trade 指这种活动，词尾则指从事这种活动的人。

senses.title: A professional in a financial market
senses.titleCN: 金融市场里的专业人员
senses.definition: someone employed to buy and sell currencies, shares or contracts for a firm
senses.definitionCN: 受雇为某机构买卖外汇、股票或合约的人
senses.example: The trader closed the position before the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 交易员在公告发布前平掉了头寸。
senses.why: The market keeps the old word for dealing but adds speed and a screen.
senses.whyCN: 市场沿用旧的「买卖者」一词，只是加上了速度与屏幕。

senses.title: A seller at a stall or on the street
senses.definition: a small seller working from a stall, a cart or a pavement
senses.definitionCN: 在摊位、推车或人行道上做小本买卖的人
senses.example: A street trader sold roasted nuts outside the station.
senses.exampleCN: 一位街头小贩在车站外卖炒货。
senses.why: The oldest kind of trader is simply the person standing beside the goods.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的商人，就是站在货物旁边的那个人。

senses.title: A dealer in physical commodities
senses.titleCN: 实物大宗商品的交易商
senses.definition: a firm that handles actual cargoes of oil, metal or grain rather than paper claims
senses.definitionCN: 处理石油、金属或谷物实际货物、而非纸面权益的公司
senses.example: The commodity trader chartered a ship for the copper.
senses.exampleCN: 大宗商品交易商为这批铜租下了一条船。
senses.why: When the goods are heavy, the trader must handle ships and warehouses, not only prices.
senses.whyCN: 当货物沉重时，商人要处理船与仓库，而不只是价格。

senses.title: A short-term speculator
senses.definition: someone who opens and closes positions within one day to profit from small moves
senses.definitionCN: 在一天之内开仓又平仓、靠小幅波动获利的人
senses.example: A day trader may make a dozen decisions before lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 当日冲销者午饭前可能做十几次决定。
senses.why: The same dealing word takes a time prefix, and the prefix becomes the identity.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示买卖的词加上时间前缀，前缀就成了身份。

senses.title: A specialist in one kind of goods
senses.titleCN: 专做某一类货物的买卖者
senses.definition: a person known by the goods they handle, such as silk, wine or furs
senses.definitionCN: 以所经营货物而得名的人，如丝绸、葡萄酒或毛皮
senses.example: Her grandfather was a fur trader on the northern route.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖父是北方线路上的毛皮商人。
senses.why: The goods can be attached to the trader, and the phrase becomes a trade name.
senses.whyCN: 货物名可以挂在商人前面，这个短语就成了行业名号。

senses.title: One who trades in influence or favors
senses.titleCN: 拿影响力或人情做交换的人
senses.definition: a person who exchanges information, favors or access as if they were goods
senses.definitionCN: 把信息、人情或门路当作货物来交换的人
senses.example: The columnist called him a trader in rumors.
senses.exampleCN: 那位专栏作家称他是拿传闻做买卖的人。
senses.why: The market word can be borrowed for any exchange, including one with no goods at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个市场词可被借去指任何交换，包括完全没有货物的交换。

senses.title: A merchant on a long trade route
senses.titleCN: 长途贸易路线上的商人
senses.definition: a historical figure who carried goods between distant regions
senses.definitionCN: 在遥远地区之间运送货物的历史人物
senses.example: Caravan traders linked the coast to the inland towns.
senses.exampleCN: 商队商人把海岸与内陆城镇连了起来。
senses.why: Before markets had screens, the trader was the person who moved goods across distance.
senses.whyCN: 在市场还没有屏幕之前，商人就是把货物跨越距离的人。

intro.en: Trader is trade plus the native agent ending -er. Trade first meant a track or a course of life, and only later the business of buying and selling; its source is Germanic, not Latin.
intro.cn: trader 是 trade 加本族施事后缀 -er 构成。trade 最初指「路径、生活方式」，后来才指买卖这种行业；其来源属日耳曼语，不是拉丁语。

items.en: Trade meant a track, a course or a way of life, and it passed into English from the Low Countries.
items.cn: trade 意为「路径、行程、生活方式」，从低地国家传入英语。

items.en: In Middle English trade still meant a path or a habitual course, including a craft and its practice.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，trade 仍指路径或惯常的行当，包括手艺及其做法。

items.en: By the sixteenth century trade had narrowed to the business of buying and selling, the sense that now dominates.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，trade 已收窄为买卖这种行业，这一义项如今占主导。

items.en: Trader added the agent ending to the new commercial sense, naming a person who lives by dealing.
items.cn: trader 在这个新的商业义上加施事后缀，指以买卖为生的人。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word moved onto exchange floors and trading desks.
items.cn: 在十九与二十世纪，这个词进入交易所大厅与交易台。

items.en: The older sense survives in phrases such as fur trader, where the goods and the route define the person.
items.cn: 较旧的用法仍保留在「毛皮商人」这类说法里，货物与路线共同界定这个人。

note.en: The first group holds the word, its base and two look-alikes from different sources; the second holds other names for someone who sells.
note.cn: 第一组是这个单词、它的词基，以及两个来源不同的形近词；第二组是卖东西的人的其他叫法。

entries.definition: The business of buying and selling; the person ending turns it into the one who does it.
entries.definitionCN: 买卖这一行业；加上表示人的词尾，就变成从事它的人。

entries.definition: The activity itself, often used of markets and sessions; it names the doing, not the doer.
entries.definitionCN: 活动本身，常用于市场与交易时段；它指做的事，不指做的人。

entries.definition: A skilled worker or a small shopkeeper; it stresses a craft or a shop, not market dealing.
entries.definitionCN: 熟练工匠或小店店主；它强调手艺或店铺，而非市场买卖。

entries.definition: One who betrays, from Latin tradere, to hand over; the spelling is close but the root is entirely different.
entries.definitionCN: 背叛者，来自拉丁语 tradere「交出」；拼写相近，但词根完全不同。

entries.definition: A wholesale dealer, often importing or exporting; more formal and larger in scale than trader.
entries.definitionCN: 批发商，常指进出口商；比 trader 更正式、规模更大。

entries.definition: A person or firm that buys goods in order to sell them, common in cars, art and securities.
entries.definitionCN: 买进货物再出售的个人或公司，常见于汽车、艺术品与证券。

entries.definition: An intermediary who arranges a deal for a fee rather than owning the goods.
entries.definitionCN: 收取费用替他人安排交易的中介，并不拥有货物。

entries.definition: The party that sells in a particular transaction, often used in law and on the street.
entries.definitionCN: 某一笔交易中的卖方，常用于法律文书与街头场景。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real parts, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Trade plus er: the one who lives by buying and selling.
normal.cn: 「买卖」加施事后缀：靠买进卖出为生的人。

normal.en: The family runs trade, trading, trader, tradesman and tradeable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 trade、trading、trader、tradesman 与 tradeable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the market and the street: currency trader, commodity trader, street trader.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出市场与街头两面：外汇交易员、大宗商品交易商、街头小贩。

normal.en: Keep trader and traitor apart: one deals, the other hands over what should be kept.
normal.cn: 把商人与叛徒分开：一个做买卖，一个把该守住的东西交出去。

normal.en: A trader stands beside the goods, whether the goods are crates or screens.
normal.cn: 商人站在货物旁边，无论货物是木箱还是屏幕。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that never stops passing objects across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手不停地从桌子这头把东西递到那头。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose shadow is a price tag.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人的影子是一张价签。

abstract.en: Picture two market stalls facing each other, and one figure walking between them all day.
abstract.cn: 想象两个相对的摊位，一个人整天在其间来回走动。

examples.en: The trader keeps a record of every cargo he handles.
examples.cn: 这名商人记录他经手的每一批货物。

examples.en: A bond trader can move millions before the market opens.
examples.cn: 债券交易员能在开市前调动数百万资金。

examples.en: The street trader pays a small fee for the pitch.
examples.cn: 街头小贩为这个摊位付一小笔费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「trade（买卖）+ er（人）」——靠买进卖出为生的人 → 商人、交易员

root: trade 来自中古低地德语 trade「路径、行程、生活方式」，后收窄为买卖之义；加本族施事后缀 -er 成为 trader。来源属日耳曼语，无拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one dealer: a general buyer and seller, a market professional, a stall keeper, a commodity house, a day speculator, a specialist in one good, a trader in favors and a merchant on a long route.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个买卖者展开：一般的买进卖出者、市场专业人员、摊位小贩、大宗商品商、短线投机者、专做一类货物的人、拿人情做交换的人，以及长途路线上的商人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure beside a screen with a telephone and a stack of dealing slips.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人守在屏幕旁，手边有电话与一叠成交单。

branches.en: THE SAME PERSON IN TWO PLACES: a general dealer and a stall keeper differ only in the size of the counter.
branches.cn: 同一个人在两个地方：一般商人与摊位小贩的差别只在于柜台大小。

branches.en: SPEED: a market professional and a day speculator are the same role at different time scales.
branches.cn: 速度：市场专业人员与当日投机者是同一角色在不同时间尺度上。

branches.en: CARGO AND SPECIALITY: heavy goods need ships, and one kind of goods gives the trader a name.
branches.cn: 货物与专长：沉重的货物需要船，而某一类货物给了商人一个名号。

branches.en: NO GOODS AT ALL: favors and rumors can be traded like crates.
branches.cn: 根本没有货物：人情与传闻也能像木箱一样被买卖。

branches.en: DISTANCE: the oldest trader is the one who carries goods between far places.
branches.cn: 距离：最古老的商人，是在远方之间运送货物的人。

intro.en: The word is a Germanic noun of path and practice plus the native ending for a person, so it reads as one whose course of life is dealing.
intro.cn: 这个词由日耳曼语中表示「路径与行当」的名词，加本族表示人的词尾构成，读作「以买卖为行当的人」。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root in this word; trade is Germanic and the ending is native, so the Latin entries stay empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根；trade 属日耳曼语，词尾是本族成分，因此拉丁语词形一栏留空。

items.meaning: a path; a craft; buying and selling
items.example: Trade began as a word for a way of life.
items.exampleCN: 这个词最初指一种生活方式。

items.example: The ending turns a practice into a practitioner.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把一种行当变成从业者。

items.example: The trader buys the crop at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 商人在农场门口买下收成。

items.example: Trading stopped when the storm cut the road.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨切断道路后，买卖停了下来。

items.example: The tradesman repaired the roof himself.
items.exampleCN: 这位手艺人自己修了屋顶。

items.meaning: able to be bought and sold
items.example: Only graded grain is tradeable on the exchange.
items.exampleCN: 只有分级的谷物才能在交易所交易。

items.structure: Latin mercari (to trade), through Old French marchant
items.example: A merchant ships the cloth abroad.
items.exampleCN: 批发商把布匹运往海外。

items.example: They deal in used machinery.
items.exampleCN: 他们做二手机械的买卖。

items.meaning: a market where goods or claims are traded
items.example: The exchange sets a price every morning.
items.exampleCN: 交易所每天早上定出一个价格。

definition_zh: 诉讼；官司；已向法院提起的民事案件
definition_en: a civil case brought by one party against another in a court of law
core_image: 一叠写满诉求的纸被送进法院的收件窗口，从此两个人的争执变成一件有编号的案件
scene: 两家的供货合同谈崩了，一方把成箱的往来邮件交给律师。 The supplier filed a lawsuit over the unpaid invoices.
sceneCN: 这里 lawsuit 指一方就欠款向法院提起的民事案件（第 1 个义项：已进入法院的民事案件）；句意：供货方就未付的货款提起了诉讼。图中可辨识物件：成箱单据、律师公文包、法院收件窗口。

pos.zh: 诉讼；官司（可数名词，一件件独立的案件）

senses.title: A civil case in court
senses.titleCN: 已进入法院的民事案件
senses.definition: a dispute between private parties that has been brought before a court
senses.definitionCN: 私人之间已提交法院审理的争议
senses.example: The neighbor filed a lawsuit over the boundary wall.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居就那道界墙提起了诉讼。
senses.why: Law fixes the rule and suit is the following of a case through court, so the compound names a dispute that has been converted into a numbered proceeding.
senses.whyCN: law 定下规则，suit 指按规则一路跟下去，于是这个词指的是一场争执被转成有编号的程序。

senses.title: The act of suing
senses.definition: the step of starting legal proceedings against someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人启动法律程序的那一步
senses.example: Filing the lawsuit took longer than the hearing itself.
senses.exampleCN: 提起诉讼花的时间比开庭本身还长。
senses.why: The word names the thing filed as well as the filing, because in law the paper and the act that delivers it are hard to separate.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既指被递交的那份东西，也指递交这个动作，因为在法律上文书与递交行为很难分开。

senses.title: A claim for money
senses.definition: a suit asking the court to order payment or compensation
senses.definitionCN: 请求法院判令付款或赔偿的诉讼
senses.example: The builder brought a lawsuit for the final payment.
senses.exampleCN: 施工方为尾款提起了一桩诉讼。
senses.why: Most civil suits end in a money figure, so the word often means a demand for damages rather than a demand for an order.
senses.whyCN: 多数民事案件最后都落到一个金额上，所以这个词常指索赔，而不是请求作出某种命令。

senses.title: A suit over reputation
senses.definition: a suit claiming harm to reputation or to a published name
senses.definitionCN: 主张名誉或姓名被损害的诉讼
senses.example: The actor's lawsuit alleged that the article had ruined his name.
senses.exampleCN: 这名演员的诉讼称那篇文章毁了他的名声。
senses.why: Harm that leaves no visible mark still needs a form, and a lawsuit supplies the form: the injury is written down and priced.
senses.whyCN: 看不见的伤害也需要一个形式，诉讼正好提供这个形式：把损害写下来并标出价码。

senses.title: A business dispute taken to court
senses.definition: a suit between companies over contracts, supply or competition
senses.definitionCN: 公司之间因合同、供货或竞争而起的诉讼
senses.example: The two airlines spent four years in a lawsuit over landing slots.
senses.exampleCN: 两家航空公司为起降时段打了四年官司。
senses.why: Where contracts are long and money is large, the threat of a lawsuit becomes a normal instrument of business planning.
senses.whyCN: 合同长、金额大的地方，诉讼威胁就成了商业筹划中的常规工具。

senses.title: A suit brought by many
senses.titleCN: 由许多人共同提起的诉讼
senses.definition: a suit in which a group of people with the same injury sue together
senses.definitionCN: 一群受同一损害的人共同提起的诉讼
senses.example: Thousands of customers joined the lawsuit against the maker.
senses.exampleCN: 数千名顾客加入了针对制造商的那桩诉讼。
senses.why: One small claim is expensive to pursue; joining many small claims into one lawsuit makes the cost bearable, so the word covers group actions.
senses.whyCN: 单笔小额索赔诉讼成本太高，把许多小额请求并成一案才划得来，于是这个词也覆盖群体索赔。

senses.title: A suit as leverage
senses.titleCN: 作为谈判筹码的诉讼威胁
senses.definition: the mention of a possible suit used to pressure a settlement
senses.definitionCN: 以可能打官司来施压、促成和解的用法
senses.example: A quiet mention of a lawsuit was enough to bring them back to the table.
senses.exampleCN: 一句轻描淡写的诉讼威胁就足以把他们拉回谈判桌。
senses.why: Because filing is cheap and public, the word can be used before any paper exists, as a warning rather than a description.
senses.whyCN: 因为立案便宜又公开，这个词可以在任何文书存在之前就使用，作为警告而不是描述。

senses.title: The long life of a case
senses.definition: the whole course of a case, from filing through appeal
senses.definitionCN: 从立案到上诉的整个案件过程
senses.example: The lawsuit outlasted two of the lawyers who started it.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩官司比最初接手的两名律师撑得还久。
senses.why: Since a contested case can run for years, the same noun can name not the paper but the entire stretch of time it keeps alive.
senses.whyCN: 有争议的案件能拖很多年，于是同一个名词也可以不指那份文书，而指它维持的整段时间。

intro.en: Lawsuit joins two old English nouns of different ancestry: law from Old Norse, suit from Latin by way of French. The compound itself is early modern.
intro.cn: lawsuit 把两个来源不同的古老英语名词接在一起：law 来自古诺斯语，suit 经法语来自拉丁语。复合词本身出现于近代早期。

items.en: Old Norse lag meant 'something laid down, a layer', and it gave Old English lagu 'law, rule'. The same Germanic root lies behind lay, and the legal sense is 'that which is laid down' for people to follow.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 lag 意为「被放下之物、一层」，由此产生古英语 lagu「法律、规则」。同一日耳曼词根也在 lay 之中，法律义就是「为众人放下、须遵守的东西」。

items.en: Sequi meant 'to follow'. Its past participle secutus and the derived noun *sequita underlie a whole family of following words, including sequence, consequent and suit.
items.cn: sequi 意为「跟随」。其过去分词 secutus 与派生名词 *sequita 支撑了一整族表示「跟随」的词，包括 sequence、consequent 与 suit。

items.en: Old French suite meant a following, a train of attendants, or a set of things in order; English borrowed it in the thirteenth century as suit.
items.cn: 古法语 suite 指跟随、随从队伍或一组有序之物；英语在十三世纪借入，写作 suit。

items.en: By the fourteenth century English suit at law meant the pursuit of a case in court, and the verb sue was formed from it. This is the sense that survives inside lawsuit.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，英语里「依法律追究」的说法已指在法院追究一桩案件，动词「起诉」也由此产生。lawsuit 里保留的正是这一义。

items.en: Lawsuit appears in the seventeenth century, joining law to suit so that the legal reading would be unmistakable; earlier writers said suit or action.
items.cn: lawsuit 于十七世纪出现，把「法律」接到「追究」上，使法律义不再有歧义；更早的作者只说「诉」或「诉讼」。

items.en: The first date usually given for the compound is an approximation drawn from printed citations, and dictionaries differ by a few decades; the sources of both halves are not in doubt.
items.cn: 这个复合词通常给出的首见年代，是从印刷书证推算的约数，各家辞书相差数十年；两半的来源本身并无疑问。

note.en: Group one holds words of the same suit family, including one near homophone; group two holds the everyday names for legal proceedings.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 suit 词族的词，其中一个读音极近；第二组是法律程序的日常说法。

entries.definition: The root noun: legal action in older use, and also a set of clothes or a set of cards.
entries.definitionCN: 词根名词：旧用法指诉讼，也指一套衣服或一组同花色的牌。

entries.definition: A set of rooms or a set of musical pieces; it came from the same French word but never took the legal sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一套房间或一组乐曲；来自同一个法语词，却从未发展出法律义。

entries.definition: The verb formed from suit: to bring a case against someone.
entries.definitionCN: 由 suit 形成的动词：对某人提起诉讼。

entries.definition: The rule system itself, not the case; law is Germanic while suit is Latin in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 规则体系本身，不是案件；law 是日耳曼来源，suit 才是拉丁来源。

entries.definition: To plunge into liquid or to pickle; the vowel and the final consonant are close, but the word is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 浸入液体或腌渍；元音与词尾相近，但这个词毫无亲缘关系。

entries.definition: The general word for a matter before a court; it can be civil or criminal.
entries.definitionCN: 法院受理事项的通称，民事刑事皆可。

entries.definition: The formal British term for civil proceedings, as in bring an action.
entries.definitionCN: 英式正式用语，指民事诉讼程序。

entries.definition: Litigation names the activity or the whole set of proceedings, not one countable case.
entries.definitionCN: 指诉讼活动或一整批程序，不指单件可数的案件。

entries.definition: The demand stated inside a lawsuit; a claim may exist before any suit is filed.
entries.definitionCN: 诉讼中提出的请求；请求可以在立案之前就存在。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two real halves, the real verb formed from suit, and the real phrases used in practice.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两个真实成分、由 suit 形成的真实动词，以及实务中真实的固定说法。

normal.en: Law plus suit: the rule plus the following of a case under it.
normal.cn: law 加 suit：规则，加上按规则一路追究一桩案子。

normal.en: Suit, sue and suite share one Latin verb of following; only suit and sue took the legal path.
normal.cn: suit、sue 与 suite 共享同一个表示「跟随」的拉丁动词，只有前两个走了法律这条路。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the stages: file a lawsuit, settle a lawsuit, face a lawsuit.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出阶段：提起诉讼、和解结案、面临诉讼。

normal.en: A class-action lawsuit is one suit carrying many claims, which is why one word covers a crowd.
normal.cn: 集体诉讼是一案承载许多请求，所以一个词就能覆盖一群人。

normal.en: Law itself came from Old Norse, not from Latin, so the two halves of this compound are strangers joined late.
normal.cn: law 本身来自古诺斯语而非拉丁语，所以这个复合词的两半是晚年才结亲的陌生人。

abstract.en: Picture a quarrel being folded into a paper folder and given a number: the moment it gets a number, it becomes a lawsuit.
abstract.cn: 想象一场口角被折进一个纸夹并编上号：它一拿到编号，就成了 lawsuit。

abstract.en: Picture two people walking the same corridor for years, always one behind the other: that is what following a case means.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人多年走在同一条走廊上，永远一个跟着另一个：这就是「追究一桩案子」的样子。

abstract.en: Picture a small stone placed on a scale: the scale is the law, the stone is the claim, and the lawsuit is the act of putting it there.
abstract.cn: 想象一块小石头被放上天平：天平是法律，石头是请求，而 lawsuit 就是把它放上去的那个动作。

examples.en: The city settled the lawsuit before the trial date was set.
examples.cn: 市里在确定开庭日期之前就和解了这桩诉讼。

examples.en: A single lawsuit can force a manufacturer to redesign a product.
examples.cn: 一桩诉讼就能迫使制造商重新设计产品。

examples.en: She kept every receipt in case of a future lawsuit.
examples.cn: 她留好每一张收据，以防日后打官司。

dict_mnemonic.text: law（法律）+ suit（跟随、追究）——按法律一路追究下去的那件事 → 诉讼、官司

root: law 来自古诺斯语 lag（被放下之物），经古英语 lagu 成为「法律」；suit 经古法语 suite 上溯拉丁 sequi（跟随）。lawsuit 为十七世纪英语复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a case from being filed, through the claim it states and the parties who bring it, to the years it can run and the pressure its mere mention creates.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着一桩案件走：从立案，到它写明的请求、提起诉讼的人，再到它可能拖的年份，最后到仅凭提及就能产生的压力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quarrel folded into a numbered file and carried down a long corridor.
core.cn: 核心意象：一场争执被折进一份编号案卷，沿着长走廊被一路带下去。

branches.en: THE FILE ITSELF: the dispute has become an object with a number, and that object is the lawsuit.
branches.cn: 案卷本身：争执变成一个带编号的东西，这个东西就是诉讼。

branches.en: THE OPENING ACT: the filing is the moment the file begins, so the word also names the doing.
branches.cn: 开启动作：立案是案卷开始的那一刻，所以这个词也指那个动作。

branches.en: WHAT IS ASKED FOR: money or reputation, both get written into the claim.
branches.cn: 请求什么：钱或名誉，都被写进请求里。

branches.en: WHO CARRIES IT: one company or a crowd of customers can be the party that sets the file moving.
branches.cn: 谁在推动：一家公司或一大群顾客都可能成为让案卷往前走的一方。

branches.en: THE FILE AS FORCE: before it exists it can still pressure, and once it exists it can outlast the people who opened it.
branches.cn: 案卷的力量：存在之前就能施压，存在之后又能比立案的人活得更久。

intro.en: Lawsuit is a compound of two free nouns, so its structure is read by joining rather than by adding affixes; only the derived verb and adjective show suffixes.
intro.cn: lawsuit 由两个自由名词复合而成，结构靠拼接来读，而不是靠加词缀；只有派生出的动词与形容词带后缀。

latinIntro.en: Suit goes back to Latin sequi 'to follow', while law is Germanic and unrelated to Latin lex 'law'. The family of sequi also gives sequence, consequent and obsequious.
latinIntro.cn: suit 上溯拉丁 sequi「跟随」；law 是日耳曼语词，与拉丁 lex「法律」并无亲缘。sequi 词族还衍生 sequence、consequent 与 obsequious。

items.structure: law (free noun from Old English lagu, from Old Norse lag)
items.meaning: a rule laid down for a community
items.meaningCN: 为群体放下、须遵守的规则
items.example: The new law takes effect in spring.
items.exampleCN: 新法律春天生效。

items.structure: suit (free noun from Old French suite, from Latin sequi)
items.example: He brought a suit against the firm.
items.exampleCN: 他对这家公司提起了诉讼。

items.structure: law + suit (compound of two free nouns)
items.meaning: a civil case brought under the law
items.meaningCN: 依法律提起的民事案件（复合后由「跟随」收窄为「进入法院的案件」）
items.example: The lawsuit lasted five years.
items.exampleCN: 这桩官司持续了五年。

items.meaning: to bring a case against someone
items.meaningCN: 对某人提起诉讼（由名词逆构出动词，语义由「跟随」变为「启动追究」）
items.example: She sued the landlord.
items.exampleCN: 她起诉了房东。

items.meaning: the act of bringing a case
items.meaningCN: 提起诉讼的行为（动名词后缀把动作名词化）
items.example: Suing is cheaper than most people think.
items.exampleCN: 打官司比多数人想的便宜。

items.meaningCN: 法律允许的（形容词后缀把规则变成性质）
items.example: The search was lawful.
items.exampleCN: 这次搜查是合法的。

items.meaningCN: 无法无天的（否定后缀把「有规则」翻成「无规则」）
items.example: The district grew lawless after the floods.
items.exampleCN: 洪水之后该地区变得无法无天。

items.structure: law + -yer (person suffix, variant of Old French -ier)
items.meaningCN: 以法律为业的人（人名词缀把规则变成一个职业者）
items.example: Her lawyer read the contract.
items.exampleCN: 她的律师读了合同。

items.structure: suit + case (compound, different sense of suit)
items.meaningCN: 装衣物的旅行箱（这里的 suit 取「一套衣服」义，与诉讼义无关）
items.example: He packed one suitcase.
items.exampleCN: 他只装了一只箱子。

latinEntries.meaning: a way followed; a course, a sect

definition_zh: 染色体的；与染色体有关的
definition_en: relating to chromosomes or occurring on a chromosome
core_image: 显微镜下一排编号的短棒，旁边标着它们的缺陷位置
scene: 这里指「染色体的」。 Chromosomal abnormalities account for a small share of early miscarriages.
sceneCN: 这里 chromosomal 指「染色体的」（第 1 个义项：与染色体有关的异常）；句意：染色体异常只占早期流产的一小部分。

pos.zh: 染色体的；染色体上的；由染色体引起的

senses.title: Of chromosomes in general
senses.definition: relating to chromosomes as structures
senses.definitionCN: 与染色体这一结构有关的
senses.example: Chromosomal DNA is packed with histone proteins.
senses.exampleCN: 染色体 DNA 与组蛋白紧密包装在一起。
senses.why: The adjective simply turns the noun into a modifier, so any statement about chromosomes as objects can use it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词变成修饰语，因此任何关于染色体这一对象的陈述都可以用它。

senses.title: Located on a chromosome
senses.definition: situated at a particular place on a chromosome
senses.definitionCN: 位于染色体某一特定位置的
senses.example: The gene's chromosomal location was narrowed to a small region.
senses.exampleCN: 该基因的染色体位置被缩小到一个很小的区域。
senses.why: Once genes are known to sit on chromosomes, the adjective marks the address rather than the whole structure.
senses.whyCN: 既然已知基因位于染色体上，这个形容词标出的就是「地址」，而不是整个结构。

senses.title: Abnormalities
senses.definition: describing a change in chromosome number or structure
senses.definitionCN: 指染色体数目或结构的改变
senses.example: Chromosomal abnormalities can be detected before birth.
senses.exampleCN: 染色体异常可以在出生前被检出。
senses.why: Medicine needed a compact modifier for defects whose cause is a chromosome, and the adjective supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要一个简短的修饰语来指病因在染色体上的缺陷，这个形容词正好承担这一功能。

senses.title: Inheritance patterns
senses.definition: describing traits whose transmission follows chromosome behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 指传递方式随染色体行为而定的性状
senses.example: The trait shows a chromosomal pattern of inheritance.
senses.exampleCN: 该性状表现出染色体式的遗传规律。
senses.why: Because chromosomes are copied and sorted predictably, traits they carry inherit in patterns the adjective can label.
senses.whyCN: 由于染色体按可预测的方式复制与分配，它们携带的性状就以这个形容词可以命名的规律遗传。

senses.title: Sex determination
senses.definition: describing sex determination by chromosome composition
senses.definitionCN: 指由染色体组成决定性别的方式
senses.example: Birds use a chromosomal system opposite to that of mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟类使用的染色体性别系统与哺乳动物相反。
senses.why: Where sex follows from which chromosomes are present, the adjective marks the mechanism rather than the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 当性别取决于存在哪些染色体时，这个形容词标出的是机制，而不是结果。

senses.title: Laboratory technique
senses.definition: describing tests that examine chromosomes directly
senses.definitionCN: 指直接检查染色体的检测
senses.example: Chromosomal analysis requires cells that are actively dividing.
senses.exampleCN: 染色体分析需要处于活跃分裂状态的细胞。
senses.why: A test aimed at chromosomes is named by the adjective plus a noun such as analysis or test.
senses.whyCN: 针对染色体的检测，就用这个形容词加 analysis（分析）或 test（检测）之类的名词来命名。

senses.title: In evolution and species
senses.definition: describing differences between species that lie in chromosome number or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 指物种间在染色体数目或排列上的差异
senses.example: Chromosomal differences help distinguish the two species.
senses.exampleCN: 染色体层面的差异有助于区分这两个物种。
senses.why: Speciation often involves rearrangements that the adjective marks as the level at which the difference exists.
senses.whyCN: 物种形成常涉及重排，这个形容词标出的正是差异所在的层次。

senses.title: Of chromosome behaviour in division
senses.definition: describing how chromosomes move, pair or separate during division
senses.definitionCN: 指分裂过程中染色体如何移动、配对或分开
senses.example: Chromosomal pairing fails when the spindle is disturbed.
senses.exampleCN: 纺锤体受到干扰时，染色体的配对会失败。
senses.why: During division chromosomes behave as physical objects, and the adjective names that behavioural level.
senses.whyCN: 在分裂过程中，染色体表现为物理对象，这个形容词命名的就是这一行为层面。

intro.en: Chromosomal is the English adjective of chromosome, formed by adding -al to the German-coined Greek compound.
intro.cn: chromosomal 是 chromosome 的英语形容词，在德语造出的希腊语复合词后加 -al 构成。

items.en: Greek chroma, 'colour', supplies the first element. It named the dye uptake that made the bodies visible.
items.cn: 希腊语 chroma「颜色」提供第一个成分，指使这些小体可见的染料吸收。

items.en: Greek sōma, 'body', supplies the second element, so chromosome is literally a coloured body.
items.cn: 希腊语 sōma「身体」提供第二个成分，因此 chromosome 字面就是「有色的物体」。

items.en: Chromosom was coined in German in 1888, generally attributed to Waldeyer-Hartz. The English form chromosome followed soon after.
items.cn: Chromosom 于 1888 年在德语中造出，一般认为出自 Waldeyer-Hartz。英语形式 chromosome 随后出现。

items.en: The adjective chromosomal was built in English with -al, on the model of other scientific adjectives. Its first printed use is not firmly dated.
items.cn: 形容词 chromosomal 是英语加 -al 构成的，模仿其他科学形容词的模式。确切的首见印刷用例没有定论。

items.en: As cytogenetics grew, chromosomal became routine in names of disorders, analyses and rearrangements.
items.cn: 随着细胞遗传学发展，chromosomal 在疾病、分析与重排的名称中成为常规用法。

note.en: The first group separates the adjective from the noun and from its adverbial form; the second separates chromosomal from modifiers of other genetic scales.
note.cn: 第一组把这个形容词与名词及其副词形式分开；第二组把它与其它遗传尺度的修饰语分开。

entries.definition: The countable object itself; chromosomal is the form used before nouns such as abnormality, DNA or analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 是可数名词，指对象本身；chromosomal 用在 abnormality、DNA、analysis 等名词之前。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning 'at the level of chromosomes'; it modifies verbs such as determined or normal.
entries.definitionCN: 是副词，意为「在染色体层面」，修饰 determined、normal 之类的词。

entries.definition: The DNA-protein material itself; chromatin is not an adjective and cannot modify abnormality.
entries.definitionCN: 指 DNA 与蛋白质构成的物质本身；chromatin 不是形容词，不能修饰 abnormality。

entries.definition: Relating to genes and heredity; a genetic disorder may involve one gene, while a chromosomal one involves a whole chromosome.
entries.definitionCN: 指与基因和遗传有关的；遗传病可能只涉及一个基因，而染色体病涉及整条染色体。

entries.definition: Relating to the entire genome; it is broader than chromosomal, which concerns individual chromosomes.
entries.definitionCN: 指与整个基因组有关，比 chromosomal 更宽，后者只涉及单条染色体。

entries.definition: Relating to the study of chromosomes under the microscope; it names the technique as much as the object.
entries.definitionCN: 指在显微镜下研究染色体的学科，既指对象也指方法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: chromosome + -al: the adjective that stands before abnormality, DNA and analysis.
normal.cn: chromosome + -al：站在 abnormality、DNA、analysis 前面的那个形容词。

normal.en: The family runs chromosome, chromosomally, chromatin and chromosome mapping.
normal.cn: 同族词有 chromosome、chromosomally、chromatin、chromosome mapping。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: chromosomal abnormality, chromosomal rearrangement, chromosomal disorder.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：染色体异常、染色体重排、染色体疾病。

normal.en: If the defect is in a whole chromosome, the modifier is chromosomal, not genetic.
normal.cn: 如果缺陷在整条染色体上，修饰语就是 chromosomal，而不是 genetic。

normal.en: The adjective almost always appears in medical and cytological writing.
normal.cn: 这个形容词几乎只出现在医学与细胞学写作中。

abstract.en: Think of a library where a whole shelf has been misplaced, not just one book: that is chromosomal, not genetic.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆里整排书架被放错了位置，而不只是一本书：这就是 chromosomal，而不是 genetic。

abstract.en: A chromosomal map is a street plan where each gene has an address.
abstract.cn: 染色体图谱就是一张街道图，每个基因都有一个门牌号。

abstract.en: A chromosomal rearrangement is a deck of cards cut and reshuffled.
abstract.cn: 染色体重排就像一副牌被切开又重洗。

examples.en: Chromosomal analysis is offered to women at higher risk.
examples.cn: 染色体分析提供给风险较高的女性。

examples.en: The chromosomal location of the gene was confirmed by two labs.
examples.cn: 该基因的染色体位置由两个实验室确认。

examples.en: Chromosomal rearrangements can silence a gene without changing its sequence.
examples.cn: 染色体重排可以在不改变序列的情况下使一个基因沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「chromosome + -al」→ 染色体那一类的 → 染色体的、染色体上的

root: 希腊语 chroma「颜色」+ sōma「身体」→ chromosome；英语加形容词后缀 -al 构成 chromosomal。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses show the adjective spreading across levels: the structure itself, its addresses, its defects, its inheritance patterns, sex determination, tests, species differences and behaviour during division.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项显示这个形容词如何铺开到各层面：结构本身、基因位置、缺陷、遗传规律、性别决定、检测、物种差异与分裂中的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: numbered rods under a microscope with defects marked on them.
core.cn: 核心意象：显微镜下一排编了号的短棒，上面标着缺陷位置。

branches.en: THE OBJECT AND ITS BEHAVIOUR: the structure itself, and how it moves during division.
branches.cn: 对象与行为：结构本身，以及它在分裂中如何移动。

branches.en: ADDRESS: a gene's position on a chromosome.
branches.cn: 地址：基因在染色体上的位置。

branches.en: DEFECT AND DETERMINATION: abnormal counts, and the pair that sets sex.
branches.cn: 缺陷与决定：异常的数目，以及决定性别的那个配对。

branches.en: INHERITANCE AND SPECIES: patterns that follow chromosomes, and differences between species.
branches.cn: 遗传与物种：随染色体而定的规律，以及物种间的差异。

branches.en: METHOD: the laboratory analysis that reads chromosomes directly.
branches.cn: 方法：直接读取染色体的实验室分析。

intro.en: The adjective adds -al to a Greek compound; the affixes in its family belong to cytology and genetics.
intro.cn: 这个形容词在希腊语复合词后加 -al；其词族的词缀都属于细胞学与遗传学。

latinIntro.en: Greek chroma and sōma build the base; the English suffix -al comes from Latin -alis. The adverbial -ly is English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 chroma 与 sōma 构成词基；英语后缀 -al 源自拉丁语 -alis；副词词尾 -ly 是英语的。

items.example: The chromosomal defect was inherited from the mother.
items.exampleCN: 该染色体缺陷遗传自母亲。

items.example: The chromosome was first seen in dividing cells.
items.exampleCN: 染色体最早是在分裂的细胞中被看到的。

items.example: The two populations are chromosomally distinct.
items.exampleCN: 这两个群体在染色体层面有区别。

items.example: Chromatin condenses before division.
items.exampleCN: 染色质在分裂前凝缩。

items.example: Autosomal traits appear in both sexes.
items.exampleCN: 常染色体性状在两性中都出现。

items.example: Cytogenetic testing found the deletion.
items.exampleCN: 细胞遗传学检测发现了这段缺失。

items.example: Polyploid plants often grow larger.
items.exampleCN: 多倍体植物往往长得更大。

items.meaning: the chromosome complement of a cell
items.meaningCN: 一个细胞的染色体组成
items.example: The karyotype showed an extra chromosome.
items.exampleCN: 核型显示多出一条染色体。

items.meaning: a piece of chromosome moved elsewhere
items.example: A translocation joined two chromosomes.
items.exampleCN: 一次易位把两条染色体接在一起。

latinEntries.structure: Greek combining form used in scientific compounds

definition_zh: 尊重；敬重；好评；认为；视为
definition_en: to respect and value someone or something highly, or a feeling of high respect
core_image: 双手接过一件旧物，郑重地把它放到最高一层
scene: 毕业多年后，学生回到母校，把一本旧词典送还给老师。 Years later, the student still holds the old teacher in high esteem.
sceneCN: 这里 esteem 是「尊重、敬重」（第 1 个义项：对某人怀有很深的敬意）；句意：多年以后，这名学生依然非常敬重这位老师。

derivatives.zh: esteem 加后缀 -able 构成，值得敬重的；可敬的
由拉丁语 aestimatio 而来，判断；评价；估计
self 加 esteem 构成的复合词，自尊；自尊心

senses.title: High respect
senses.definition: a feeling of deep respect and approval for someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人怀有的深切敬意与认可
senses.example: The old coach is held in great esteem by his players.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老教练深受队员们的敬重。
senses.why: The Latin verb aestimare means to fix a value, so esteeming a person is setting a high value on that person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 aestimare 意为「估定价值」，所以敬重一个人就是给这个人定下很高的价值。

senses.title: Good opinion, standing
senses.definition: the good opinion that other people have of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 他人对某人或某物持有的好评与看重
senses.example: The school has risen in public esteem over the past decade.
senses.exampleCN: 过去十年间，这所学校在公众中的声誉提高了。
senses.why: Once a value has been assigned, the word can name the standing a person enjoys in the eyes of others.
senses.whyCN: 价值一经评定，这个词就转而指一个人在他人眼中的地位与声望。

senses.title: To regard as
senses.definition: to consider or judge something to be a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 把某事看作或判定为某种性质
senses.example: I esteem it a privilege to speak at this ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 我认为能在这场典礼上发言是一种荣幸。
senses.why: The old appraisal sense survives in the pattern esteem something as something, where the mind assigns a value or a label.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「估价」义保留在「esteem 某物为某物」的句式中：头脑给事物贴上价值或名目的标签。

senses.title: To appraise, to value
senses.definition: to judge the worth or amount of something, an older use
senses.definitionCN: 判断某物的价值或数量，属于较古的用法
senses.example: In old ledgers the land was esteemed at a modest sum.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧账簿里，这块地被估为一个不大的数目。
senses.why: This is the original Latin sense of aestimare, a plain valuation, before the word narrowed to respect.
senses.whyCN: 这正是拉丁语 aestimare 的本义，平实的估价；后来词义才收窄为尊重。

intro.en: Esteem goes back to Latin aestimare, to value or appraise, through Old French estimer.
intro.cn: esteem 可追溯到拉丁语 aestimare（估价、评定价值），经古法语 estimer 进入英语。

items.en: Aestimare means to value or to appraise something.
items.cn: aestimare 意为给某物估价、评定价值。

items.en: Aestimatio names the act of valuation and the value set.
items.cn: aestimatio 指估价这一行为以及被定下的价值。

items.en: Estimer carries the verb into French with the sense of holding in regard.
items.cn: estimer 把动词带入法语，并带上「看重」的含义。

items.en: Estemen appears in English for valuing and for respecting.
items.cn: 中古英语 estemen 出现，兼有估价与尊重两义。

items.en: Modern English keeps esteem mainly as respect, while estimate takes over the counting sense.
items.cn: 现代英语里 esteem 主要保留尊重，而 estimate 接过了计量估价之义。

note.en: Esteem sits inside the Latin value family and beside the everyday words for respect.
note.cn: esteem 与拉丁语「估价」词族相连，也与日常表示尊重的词相邻。

entries.definition: worthy of respect
entries.definitionCN: 值得敬重的；可敬的

entries.definition: a judgement or opinion of value
entries.definitionCN: 判断；评价；估计

entries.definition: respect for oneself
entries.definitionCN: 自尊；自尊心

entries.definition: a feeling of admiration for someone
entries.definitionCN: 尊敬；敬意

entries.definition: attention or respect for someone
entries.definitionCN: 尊重；关注

entries.definition: a feeling of great approval
entries.definitionCN: 钦佩；赞赏

normalIntro.en: Esteem is a scale in the mind: a person is weighed and found valuable.
normalIntro.cn: esteem 是心里的一杆秤：把人称过之后，认定其价值很高。

normal.en: To hold someone in high esteem is to respect that person deeply.
normal.cn: hold someone in high esteem 就是深深敬重某人。

normal.en: Self-esteem is the value you place on yourself.
normal.cn: self-esteem 是你给自己定下的价值。

normal.en: A mark of esteem is a sign that others value you.
normal.cn: a mark of esteem 是别人看重你的表示。

normal.en: Esteem and estimate share one Latin root but have drifted apart.
normal.cn: esteem 与 estimate 同出一个拉丁词根，后来分道扬镳。

normal.en: The phrase esteem it a privilege keeps the old sense of judging something to be valuable.
normal.cn: esteem it a privilege 这个说法保留了「判定某物有价值」的古义。

abstract.en: Picture both hands receiving an old book and placing it on the top shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象双手接过一本旧书，把它放到书架最高一层。（对应第 1 个义项：把人放在心里的高处，就是敬重）

abstract.en: Imagine a name rising on a public list as neighbours nod in approval.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字在众人名单上往上走，邻居们纷纷点头称许。（对应第 2 个义项：声望就是别人眼中的位置）

abstract.en: Picture a judge setting a high price on a small object and calling it precious.
abstract.cn: 想象鉴定人给一件小物件定下高价，称它珍贵。（对应第 3 个义项：认为、视为就是给事物定名分）

examples.en: The students hold their teacher in high esteem.
examples.cn: 学生们非常敬重他们的老师。

examples.en: Her self-esteem grew after she finished the course.
examples.cn: 完成课程后，她的自尊心增强了。

examples.en: The village esteemed him as a fair judge.
examples.cn: 村里人把他视为公正的裁判。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一斯汀」——记成「一心一意把对方当尊长」，于是有敬重之意；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aestimare（估价、评定价值）→ aestimatio（评价）→ 古法语 estimer → 中古英语 estemen → 英语 esteem，核心义「给某人定下很高的价值」。

sensesIntro.en: Esteem starts as a valuation, becomes the respect a person commands, and keeps a formal verb sense of regarding something as valuable.
sensesIntro.cn: esteem 从估价出发，转为一个人赢得的敬重与声望，并保留「认为某物有价值」的正式动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of hands weighing something and setting it high.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手把某物掂量之后，放到高处。

branches.en: Respect is the value placed on a person.
branches.cn: 敬意是给一个人定下的价值。

branches.en: Public esteem is the standing others grant.
branches.cn: 声誉是他人给予的地位。

branches.en: To esteem as is to judge something to be valuable.
branches.cn: 认为、视为就是判定某物有价值。

branches.en: Both the noun and the verb keep the old valuation image.
branches.cn: 名词与动词都保留着古老的估价意象。

branches.en: A judgement repeated by many people hardens into public standing.
branches.cn: 许多人的判断反复叠加，就固化为公众声望。

intro.en: Esteem belongs to the Latin value family, and English builds estimable, estimation, and self-esteem around it.
intro.cn: esteem 属于拉丁语「估价」词族，英语围绕它构成 estimable、estimation 与 self-esteem。

latinIntro.en: Latin aestimare means to value, and aestimatio means a valuation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aestimare 意为估价，aestimatio 意为估价、评价。

items.example: Aestimare is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: aestimare 是整个词族的源头。

items.example: Aestimatio names the act of valuing.
items.exampleCN: aestimatio 指估价这一行为。

items.meaning: to value, to hold in regard
items.example: Old French estimer carries both senses.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 estimer 兼有估价与看重两义。

items.example: Esteem keeps the noun sense of respect.
items.exampleCN: esteem 保留表示尊重的名词义。

items.example: The verb esteems a person or a plan.
items.exampleCN: 动词 esteem 可接人或计划作宾语。

items.example: The suffix -able forms estimable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 estimable。

items.example: Estimable describes a person worth valuing.
items.exampleCN: estimable 形容值得看重的人。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms estimation.

items.example: Estimation moves toward judgement.
items.exampleCN: estimation 偏向判断、看法。

items.example: The prefix self- forms self-esteem.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 self- 构成 self-esteem。

items.exampleCN: self-esteem 是自己给自己定下的价值。

definition_zh: 支出结构；支出模式（各类开销在总支出中的比例与走向）
definition_en: the way spending is distributed across categories, and how that distribution changes over time
core_image: 一张分成几栏的账页，食品、房租、交通各占一条高低不同的色带，色带整体缓慢移动
scene: 账本摊开，几类开销被画成高低不同的色带，食品、房租与交通各自占去一块。 The survey found that the expenditure pattern of city households had shifted towards services.
sceneCN: 账页上几类开销被画成高低不同的色带，各占一块；句中的 expenditure pattern 指「各类支出在总支出中的分布方式」（第 1 个义项：按类别划分的支出构成）。图中可辨识物件：分类账页、彩色条带、比例尺、铅笔、计算器。

collocations.phrase: a change in the expenditure pattern

derivatives.zh: 有图案的；按模式形成的

senses.title: How spending is split across categories
senses.titleCN: 支出在各类别之间的分配方式
senses.definition: the shares of total spending that go to different categories such as food, housing and transport
senses.definitionCN: 总支出中分给食品、住房、交通等不同类别的份额
senses.example: The survey found that the expenditure pattern of city households had shifted towards services.
senses.exampleCN: 调查发现，城市家庭的支出结构已向服务倾斜。
senses.why: A pattern is a shape repeated across parts, so the phrase names the shape that spending makes when it is divided by category.
senses.whyCN: 模式是各部分重复呈现的形状，因此这个短语指支出按类别切分后所呈现的形状。

senses.title: A household's habitual way of spending
senses.definition: the recurring way a household distributes its income among needs and wants
senses.definitionCN: 家庭在需要与想要之间反复分配收入的惯常方式
senses.example: Their expenditure pattern leaves little room for savings.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的支出模式几乎没有留下储蓄空间。
senses.why: Repetition is the core of pattern: a single month is a set of bills, but twelve similar months make a pattern.
senses.whyCN: 重复是模式的要点：单月只是一叠账单，十二个相似的月份才构成模式。

senses.title: A statistical trend over time
senses.titleCN: 随时间变化的统计走势
senses.definition: a measurable direction of change in the composition of spending across successive periods
senses.definitionCN: 连续时期内支出构成的可测量的变化方向
senses.example: Official figures show a steady expenditure pattern over the decade.
senses.exampleCN: 官方数据显示，这十年间的支出走势相当平稳。
senses.why: Statistics turns the household habit into a line on a chart, and the line itself is called a pattern.
senses.whyCN: 统计把家庭习惯变成图表上的一条线，而这条线本身也被称作模式。

senses.title: A regional or national structure
senses.titleCN: 地区或国家的支出结构
senses.definition: the typical distribution of spending across a region, income group or whole economy
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区、收入群体或整个经济的典型支出分布
senses.example: The expenditure pattern of the coastal provinces differs from that of inland ones.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海省份的支出结构与内陆省份不同。
senses.why: Once aggregated, individual habits become a social fact, and the phrase is used for whole populations.
senses.whyCN: 一旦加总，个人习惯就成了社会事实，这个短语便用于整个群体。

senses.title: A company's spending profile
senses.definition: the split of a firm's outgoings among wages, materials, marketing and other headings
senses.definitionCN: 企业支出在工资、材料、营销等科目之间的划分
senses.example: Auditors compared the firm's expenditure pattern with its rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 审计人员将该公司的支出结构与竞争对手作了比较。
senses.why: Firms also keep category accounts, so the same phrase transfers from households to balance sheets.
senses.whyCN: 企业同样按类别记账，因此同一个短语从家庭账本转到了资产负债表。

senses.title: A shift in the composition
senses.definition: a recognised change in the relative weight of categories, as when services take a larger share
senses.definitionCN: 各类别相对权重的显著变化，例如服务所占份额变大
senses.example: Rising incomes produced a marked shift in the expenditure pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 收入上升使支出结构出现明显转变。
senses.why: The word pattern invites comparison, and comparison makes change visible, so the phrase often appears with shift or change.
senses.whyCN: 「模式」一词天然引出比较，比较又让变化显现，因此这个短语常与「转变」「变化」连用。

senses.title: An analytical template in economics
senses.definition: a standard classification used by economists to compare spending across households or countries
senses.definitionCN: 经济学家用来比较家庭或国家支出的标准分类框架
senses.example: The model takes the expenditure pattern as its starting input.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型以支出结构作为起始输入。
senses.why: Here pattern is no longer observed behaviour but a fixed shape imposed for comparison.
senses.whyCN: 这里的模式不再是观察到的行为，而是为了比较而设定的固定框架。

senses.title: Any repeatable allocation of resources
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何可重复的资源分配方式
senses.definition: any stable way of dividing limited resources among competing claims, whether money, time or attention
senses.definitionCN: 在相互竞争的需求之间分配有限资源的任何稳定方式，无论资源是金钱、时间还是注意力
senses.example: The laboratory's expenditure pattern favours equipment over staff.
senses.exampleCN: 该实验室的资源分配方式偏向设备而非人员。
senses.why: Generalised beyond money, the phrase describes any recurring budget of scarce means.
senses.whyCN: 超出金钱范围后，这个短语描述任何稀缺手段的重复分配方案。

intro.en: The phrase joins expenditure, an English noun from Latin expendere 'to weigh out, pay', with pattern, which reached English from Latin patronus 'protector' through Old French. The compound itself belongs to modern statistical economics. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语由 expenditure 与 pattern 组成：前者是英语名词，来自拉丁语 expendere「称出、付出」；后者经古法语来自拉丁语 patronus「保护人」。复合短语本身属于近代统计经济学。年代为约数。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus pendere 'to weigh' produced expendere, 'to weigh out and pay out'; its noun expensa gave English expense and, later, expenditure.
items.cn: 表「向外」的前缀加 pendere「称量」构成 expendere「称出、付出」，其名词 expensa 给英语带来 expense，后来又有了 expenditure。

items.en: Patronus meant 'protector, patron', derived from pater 'father'. It named the person who stood in a protective role.
items.cn: patronus 意为「保护人、庇护者」，由 pater「父亲」派生，指居于保护地位的人。

items.en: Old French patron passed into English in the fourteenth century; the same form split into patron, for a supporter, and pattern, for a model to be copied.
items.cn: 古法语 patron 在十四世纪进入英语；同一形式后来分化为 patron（支持者）与 pattern（可供模仿的范本）。

items.en: By the sixteenth century pattern had moved from 'an example to copy' to 'a repeated arrangement of parts', which is the sense economics later used.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，pattern 已从「供人模仿的范例」转为「各部分重复出现的排列」，经济学后来用的正是这个义项。

items.en: The full phrase appears in twentieth-century household-budget studies and national accounts, where spending is classified and compared.
items.cn: 完整短语出现在二十世纪的家庭预算研究与国民经济核算中，那里对支出进行分类与比较。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first use of the exact phrase is not recorded precisely, and the shift of pattern from 'model' to 'recurring form' is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个确切短语的首见记录无法精确定位；pattern 从「范本」转为「重复形态」的年代亦只有约数。

note.en: Group one holds the two halves of the phrase and their near variants, which are often confused; group two holds other ways of describing how money is divided.
note.cn: 第一组是短语的两半及其近似变体，常被混用；第二组是其他描述钱如何分配的说法。

entries.definition: The total money spent; it says nothing about how the total is divided.
entries.definitionCN: 指花掉的总金额，并不说明总额如何划分。

entries.definition: A single charge or the burden of it, too small a unit to form a distribution.
entries.definitionCN: 指单笔费用或费用负担，单位太小，构不成一种分布。

entries.definition: The everyday synonym; it is equally correct but less formal than the phrase with expenditure.
entries.definitionCN: 日常同义说法，同样正确，但不如含 expenditure 的说法正式。

entries.definition: On its own it can mean a printed design; only with expenditure does it name a budget structure.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时可以指印花图案；只有与 expenditure 连用才指预算结构。

entries.definition: The formal economic term for the same division of household spending, common in translated statistical reports.
entries.definitionCN: 同一家庭支出划分的正式经济术语，常见于统计报告译本。

entries.definition: The intended division of a budget; it is a plan, while an expenditure pattern is observed.
entries.definitionCN: 预算的预期划分，是计划；而支出结构是观察到的实况。

entries.definition: A person's usual way of spending, stressing behaviour rather than measurable shares.
entries.definitionCN: 个人惯常的花钱方式，强调行为而非可计量的份额。

entries.definition: The act of assigning resources to purposes; it names the decision, not the resulting shape.
entries.definitionCN: 把资源分配给用途的动作，指决定本身，而非由此形成的形状。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real halves of the phrase, the real family and the real statistical context.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用短语真实的两半、真实词族与真实统计语境。

normal.en: Expenditure is the total; pattern is the shape it makes when divided.
normal.cn: expenditure 是总额，pattern 是它被划分后形成的形状。

normal.en: The family runs expend, expense, expenditure, pattern, patterned.
normal.cn: 词族包括 expend、expense、expenditure、pattern、patterned。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the analysis: household expenditure pattern, a shift in the pattern.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出分析语境：家庭支出结构、结构的转变。

normal.en: The phrase answers 'what share goes where', not 'how much in total'.
normal.cn: 这个短语回答「各占多少份额」，而不是「总共多少」。

normal.en: Economics compares patterns; budgets plan totals.
normal.cn: 经济学比较结构，预算则规划总额。

abstract.en: Picture a pie cut into slices whose widths slowly change from year to year.
abstract.cn: 想象一块馅饼被切成若干片，各片的宽窄逐年缓慢变化。

abstract.en: Picture a graph whose bars swap heights without the total moving much.
abstract.cn: 想象一张图，各条柱子的高低互换，而总量几乎不变。

abstract.en: Picture a household that quietly spends less on food and more on fares each decade.
abstract.cn: 想象一个家庭，每过十年就悄悄少花些饭钱、多花些车费。

examples.en: Rising rents changed the expenditure pattern of young workers.
examples.cn: 租金上涨改变了年轻劳动者的支出结构。

examples.en: The report compares the expenditure pattern of rural and urban households.
examples.cn: 该报告比较了农村与城市家庭的支出结构。

examples.en: A stable expenditure pattern makes next year's budget easier to draft.
examples.cn: 稳定的支出结构让来年预算更容易起草。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「支出（expenditure）排成花样（pattern）」——各类开销按比例摆出的花样，就是支出结构

root: 拉丁语 expendere（称出、付出）＋拉丁语 patronus（保护人，经古法语 patron 转为「范本、花样」）；前者给出 expenditure，后者给出 pattern。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape: a total is divided into categories, and the same division is read as a household habit, a trend, a regional fact, a corporate profile, a visible shift, a comparison template and finally any recurring budget of scarce means.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形状展开：总额被切成类别，这个切分再被读成家庭习惯、时间走势、地区事实、企业概况、可见的转变、比较用的框架，最后泛指任何稀缺手段的重复分配。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page of accounts divided into bands of different widths.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页账目被分成宽窄不同的色带。

branches.en: SHAPE AND HABIT: one month shows shares, twelve months show a routine.
branches.cn: 形状与习惯：一个月显出份额，十二个月显出惯例。

branches.en: SCALE: the same shape is read as a trend in time and as a structure across a region.
branches.cn: 尺度：同一形状在时间上读作走势，在地域上读作结构。

branches.en: FIRM: a company's headings reproduce the household's categories on a balance sheet.
branches.cn: 企业：公司的科目在资产负债表上复现了家庭的类别。

branches.en: CHANGE: comparing two shapes makes a shift visible, which is why the phrase travels with words for change.
branches.cn: 变化：比较两个形状就让转变显形，因此这个短语常与表示变化的词同行。

branches.en: TEMPLATE: once fixed for comparison, the shape can be imposed on any scarce resource.
branches.cn: 框架：一旦为比较而固定，这个形状就可以套到任何稀缺资源上。

intro.en: The phrase has two transparent halves: one for money laid out, one for a repeated shape, and both are built from Latin nouns and verbs.
intro.cn: 这个短语的两半都很透明：一半指付出的钱，一半指重复的形状，两者都由拉丁名词与动词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin expendere supplies the first half; Latin patronus, through Old French, supplies the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 expendere 提供前半，拉丁语 patronus 经古法语提供后半。

items.example: The prefix marks the outward flow of money.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出金钱向外流出。

items.example: Payment began as weighing.
items.exampleCN: 支付最初就是称量。

items.example: The verb underlies expenditure.
items.exampleCN: 动词构成 expenditure 的基础。

items.example: Expenditure rose with the price of fuel.
items.exampleCN: 支出随燃料价格上升。

items.example: The root names the protecting father.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根点明保护者的父亲角色。

items.example: Patronus named the one who shielded others.
items.exampleCN: patronus 指庇护他人的人。

items.example: The word moved from model to repeated form.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从「范本」转为「重复形态」。

items.example: The cloth was patterned with small squares.
items.exampleCN: 布上印着小方格图案。

items.example: The expenditure pattern shifted towards services.
items.exampleCN: 支出结构向服务倾斜。

definition_zh: 传粉者；传播花粉的动物或媒介
definition_en: an animal, or sometimes the wind, that carries pollen from one flower to another
core_image: 一只毛茸茸的蜂腿上沾满金色花粉团，正落在下一朵花的花蕊上
scene: 园丁在田埂边留出一块不除草的地，野花茂密，蜂蝶往来。 That strip of wildflowers serves as a pollinator refuge between the crop rows.
sceneCN: 这里 pollinator 指「传粉者」（第 1 个义项：搬运花粉的动物）；句意为那条野花带在作物行间充当传粉者的庇护所。

pos.zh: 传粉者；传粉动物；传粉媒介

senses.title: An animal that carries pollen
senses.definition: any animal that regularly moves pollen from one flower to another
senses.definitionCN: 经常把花粉从一朵花搬到另一朵花的动物
senses.example: The bee is the most familiar pollinator in temperate farmland.
senses.exampleCN: 蜜蜂是温带农田中最常见的传粉者。
senses.why: the -or suffix names the doer, so the word answers who does the carrying rather than what the carrying is.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -or 命名执行者，因此这个词回答「谁在搬运」，而不是「搬运是什么」。

senses.title: An insect pollinator
senses.definition: an insect such as a bee, wasp, fly, beetle or moth that moves pollen
senses.definitionCN: 蜜蜂、黄蜂、蝇、甲虫或蛾等搬运花粉的昆虫
senses.example: Flies take over as pollinators in cold, wet weather.
senses.exampleCN: 在寒冷潮湿的天气里，蝇类接手传粉工作。
senses.why: insects are the largest group of carriers, so the general word is often used where insect is understood.
senses.whyCN: 昆虫是最大的载体类群，因此这个通名常用于默认指昆虫的语境。

senses.title: A vertebrate pollinator
senses.definition: a bird, bat or small mammal that moves pollen while feeding
senses.definitionCN: 取食时搬运花粉的鸟、蝙蝠或小型哺乳动物
senses.example: The long-tongued bat is the main pollinator of that cactus.
senses.exampleCN: 长舌蝙蝠是那种仙人掌的主要传粉者。
senses.why: body size and flight allow vertebrates to serve the same role as insects, so the term covers them without change.
senses.whyCN: 体型与飞行让脊椎动物能担任与昆虫相同的角色，因此这个词不加改变地覆盖它们。

senses.title: Wind as an abiotic carrier
senses.definition: moving air treated as the carrier in wind-pollinated plants
senses.definitionCN: 在风媒植物中被视为载体的流动空气
senses.example: For grasses, the wind is the only pollinator that matters.
senses.exampleCN: 对禾草而言，风是唯一重要的传粉者。
senses.why: the word normally implies a living agent, so using it for wind is a deliberate extension of the role, not of the meaning of animal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词通常暗示活的媒介，因此用于风是对「角色」的有意延伸，而不是把词义改指动物。

senses.title: A specialist pollinator
senses.definition: a species that pollinates only one or a few plant species
senses.definitionCN: 只为一种或少数几种植物传粉的物种
senses.example: The fig wasp is an obligate specialist pollinator.
senses.exampleCN: 榕小蜂是严格的专性传粉者。
senses.why: specialisation is measured by the number of partners, so the term needs a qualifier rather than a new noun.
senses.whyCN: 专化程度以伙伴数量衡量，因此这个词需要限定语而非另造新名词。

senses.title: A generalist pollinator
senses.definition: a species that visits many kinds of flowers
senses.definitionCN: 访问许多种类花的物种
senses.example: Honeybees are generalists, which makes them useful in mixed orchards.
senses.exampleCN: 蜜蜂是泛性传粉者，因此在混种果园中很有用。
senses.why: a visitor that accepts many hosts is described by the range of its diet, not by a different word.
senses.whyCN: 接受许多寄主的来访者以其食谱范围来描述，而不是另用一词。

senses.title: A garden built for pollinators
senses.titleCN: 传粉者花园（为其营造的栖息地）
senses.definition: a planting designed to feed and shelter pollinating animals
senses.definitionCN: 为传粉动物提供食物与庇护的种植区
senses.example: The school planted a pollinator strip along the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 学校沿围栏种了一条传粉者花带。
senses.why: the noun moves from the animal to the place prepared for it, a common pattern in ecology compounds.
senses.whyCN: 名词从动物转到为它准备的地方，这是生态复合词中常见的转移。

senses.title: Metaphor: a person who spreads ideas
senses.titleCN: 比喻：在领域间传递想法的人
senses.definition: figurative, a person who carries a method or idea from one field into another
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指把方法或观念从一个领域带进另一个领域的人
senses.example: She became a pollinator between laboratory science and classroom practice.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了实验室科学与课堂实践之间的传递者。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps only the carrying role, dropping the flower and the pollen.
senses.whyCN: 比喻只保留搬运角色，舍去花与花粉。

intro.en: Pollinator is pollinate plus the Latin agent suffix -or, so it means 'the one that pollinates'. The base pollen 'fine flour, dust' has an uncertain deeper origin.
intro.cn: pollinator 是 pollinate 加拉丁施事后缀 -or，意为「执行传粉的那一个」。词基 pollen「细面粉、粉尘」的更早来源不确定。

items.en: Pollen meant 'fine flour, mill dust', and the flower grains were named by resemblance.
items.cn: pollen 意为「细面粉、磨坊粉尘」，花上的颗粒是凭相似而得名的。

items.en: Source uncertain: the ancestry of pollen before Latin is unresolved; the polenta and pulvis connections are hypotheses only.
items.cn: 来源不确定：pollen 在拉丁语之前的谱系尚无定论；与 polenta、pulvis 的联系仅为假说。

items.en: Modern Latin pollinare and English pollinate came first; the agent noun followed when ecologists needed to name the carrier.
items.cn: 先有近代拉丁 pollinare 与英语 pollinate；生态学家需要为搬运者命名时，施事名词才随之出现。

items.en: Latin -or marks the person or thing that performs an action, as in actor and conveyor.
items.cn: 拉丁 -or 标记执行动作的人或物，如 actor 与 conveyor。

items.en: Pollinator became a standard term in the twentieth century as studies of crop dependence on insects expanded.
items.cn: 随着作物对昆虫依赖的研究扩展，pollinator 在 20 世纪成为标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first use of pollinator for an animal is not firmly recorded, so the dating here is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：pollinator 首次用于指动物的确切记录不详，此处系年为约数。

note.en: Group one separates the words of the same pollen family; group two separates the carrier from the things carried and from other ecological roles.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一 pollen 词族的词；第二组区分载体与被搬运之物以及其他生态角色。

entries.definition: The action of carrying pollen; the pollinator is the one that performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 搬运花粉的动作；pollinator 是执行这一动作的那一个。

entries.definition: The event as a whole, named with -ation; it includes the carrier but is not the carrier.
entries.definitionCN: 整个事件，由 -ation 命名；包含载体，但并不等于载体。

entries.definition: The grains moved; the pollinator is the vehicle, pollen is what it carries.
entries.definitionCN: 被搬运的颗粒；传粉者是载具，花粉是它所载之物。

entries.definition: Also -or 'one who acts', but it acts by eating; the shared ending does not make the words related in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 同样由 -or「行动者」构成，但它的行动是捕食；相同的词尾并不使二者词义相关。

entries.definition: An animal or agent that carries seeds or spores away from the parent plant; the destination is the ground, not a stigma.
entries.definitionCN: 把种子或孢子带离母株的动物或媒介；目的地是地面，而不是柱头。

entries.definition: An animal that comes to a flower, whether or not it carries pollen effectively; pollinators are the subset that does.
entries.definitionCN: 来到花上的动物，无论是否有效搬运花粉；传粉者是其中真正做到的那一部分。

entries.definition: A general term for an agent that transmits something, including disease; pollinator is the specific ecological case.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指传递某种东西的媒介，包括疾病；pollinator 是其中特定的生态学情形。

entries.definition: The sugary liquid a plant provides; it attracts the pollinator but is not the pollinator.
entries.definitionCN: 植物提供的糖液；它吸引传粉者，但不是传粉者本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the agent suffix, the real ecological phrases and the real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：施事后缀、真实的生态学搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: pollinate + -or: the one that does the pollinating.
normal.cn: pollinate + -or：执行传粉的那一个。

normal.en: The same ending names actor and predator, all doers.
normal.cn: 同一词尾构成 actor 与 predator，都是执行者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: pollinator decline, pollinator garden, key pollinator.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：传粉者衰退、传粉者花园、关键传粉者。

normal.en: Four kinds of carrier: bee, fly, bird, bat; wind is the odd fifth.
normal.cn: 四类载体：蜂、蝇、鸟、蝙蝠；风算特殊的第五种。

normal.en: The family runs pollen, pollinate, pollination, pollinator.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 pollen、pollinate、pollination、pollinator。

abstract.en: Picture a courier whose bag is full of gold dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一名信使，包里装满金粉。

abstract.en: Picture a field edge left unmown on purpose so that the carriers survive the season.
abstract.cn: 想象田边特意留着一片不割的草，好让这些搬运者熬过一季。

abstract.en: Picture a person who brings a borrowed method home and makes it work.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把借来的方法带回家，并让它奏效。

examples.en: Pollinator numbers have fallen sharply in the region.
examples.cn: 该地区的传粉者数量急剧下降。

examples.en: The orchard plantings a pollinator strip beside every block.
examples.cn: 果园在每一片地块旁种上一条传粉者花带。

examples.en: A single generalist pollinator can serve many crops.
examples.cn: 一种泛性传粉者就能服务许多作物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pollinate（传粉）+ or（做某事者）」——负责传粉的那一位 → 传粉者

root: 拉丁 pollen, pollinis「细面粉、粉尘」→ pollinate + -or（施事）。pollen 更早来源不确定，与 polenta、pulvis 的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of pollinator stay close to one role: whoever or whatever performs the carrying, from a bee to a bat to the wind, and finally to a person carrying ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: pollinator 的八个义项都围绕一个角色：执行搬运的那一位或那一种，从蜂到蝙蝠再到风，最后到搬运观念的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pollen-laden body arriving at the next flower.
core.cn: 核心意象：沾满花粉的身体抵达下一朵花。

branches.en: THE BASIC ROLE: an insect that moves pollen is the default case.
branches.cn: 基本角色：搬运花粉的昆虫是默认情形。

branches.en: WIDER CARRIERS: vertebrates and moving air can do the same work.
branches.cn: 更广的载体：脊椎动物与流动空气能做同样的工作。

branches.en: NARROW OR BROAD DIET: specialists and generalists split the role by range of hosts.
branches.cn: 窄食或广食：专性与泛性按寄主范围划分这一角色。

branches.en: PLACE FOR THE ROLE: a garden can be named after the animals it supports.
branches.cn: 为角色留地：花园可以按它所供养的动物来命名。

branches.en: HUMAN CARRIER: only the transporting part survives the metaphor.
branches.cn: 人的载体：比喻中只剩下「搬运」这一部分。

intro.en: Pollinator is a verb plus an agent suffix, and its family names the cargo, the action, the process and the carrier separately.
intro.cn: pollinator 是动词加施事后缀，其词族把货物、动作、过程与载体分开命名。

latinIntro.en: Latin pollen 'dust' gives pollen and pollinare; English builds pollinate, pollination and pollinator on that base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pollen「粉尘」衍生 pollen 与 pollinare；英语在此基础上构成 pollinate、pollination 与 pollinator。

items.example: Pollen is the cargo the carrier moves.
items.exampleCN: 花粉是载体搬运的货物。

items.example: Pollinate means to move the grains.
items.exampleCN: pollinate 意为搬运这些颗粒。

items.example: Pollination is the process the carrier performs.
items.exampleCN: pollination 是载体所执行的过程。

items.meaning: one who or that which performs
items.example: The -or marks the doer of the action.
items.exampleCN: -or 标记动作的执行者。

items.example: The bee pollinates the blossom.
items.exampleCN: 蜜蜂给花传粉。

items.example: Pollination happens before fertilization.
items.exampleCN: 传粉发生在受精之前。

items.example: The farm uses pollinator-friendly borders.
items.exampleCN: 农场采用对传粉者友好的边界种植。

items.meaning: relying on animals for pollen transfer
items.example: Most orchard crops are pollinator-dependent.
items.exampleCN: 大多数果园作物依赖传粉者。

latinEntries.structure: pollinator, pollinatoris (m., Modern Latin, third declension)
